entries.name: Move into light or dense terrain to become Hidden
entries.description: End the move with every alive model of an INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM unit within a terrain area that contains a dense feature (ruins, woods, buildings, containers), and plan not to shoot. While the unit made no ranged attacks this turn or the previous turn, each such model is visible only to enemy models within its detection range (15″ by default). Beyond that range it cannot be targeted by direct fire, Fire Overwatch, Explosives, Surveil or Precision. A unit is visible if any one model is, so every model must qualify; an attached leader without one of those keywords breaks it. Advancing in is free if the unit was not going to charge or start an action anyway. On a terrain objective the same move holds the objective (a model within the area is in range) and hides the unit.
entries.when_to_use: Use when the unit is INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM and its shooting this turn is absent or low-value. A dense area must be reachable this move (M, or M+D6 when Advancing costs nothing) and must fit every model. Score by the share of enemy ranged threat that would still be beyond detection range at their next-turn firing positions (enemy M + range): a Hidden spot that hides from nobody is worth nothing. Strongest in rounds 1-2, against gunlines, and for objective holders on terrain objectives, action units and melee units that are staging. Discount it when enemy melee can reach the spot (Hidden does not stop charges), against [INDIRECT FIRE], and against Hidden-removing abilities (e.g. Burna Bomb).
entries.unit_types: INFANTRY, BEASTS, SWARM. Attached units qualify only if every model has one of those keywords. Never MONSTER, VEHICLE or MOUNTED.
entries.move_type: Normal Move / Advance / Remain Stationary (already inside) / Disembark (tactical, then move) / Reserves arrival into a dense area
entries.rules_basis: 13.09 HIDDEN (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2292-2303): an INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM model within a terrain area containing one or more dense features, whose unit made no ranged attacks this turn or the previous turn, is visible only to enemy models within its detection range, 15″ unless otherwise stated. 13.05 dense examples (:2089-2095). 06.01: a unit is visible if any model is visible (:1087-1110). 04.02: targets must be visible (:628-642). 10.07: [INDIRECT FIRE] can still target non-visible units (:1549-1574). 09.06: an Advance bars only charges and actions (:1401-1415). 14.02: a model is in range of a terrain objective while within that area (:2401-2406). Engine: TerrainManager.is_model_hidden (40k/autoloads/TerrainManager.gd:999-1043) checks any part of the base, the area group, and a turn stamp delta < 2. The unit is hidden only while every alive model is hidden (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/RULINGS.md:169). Unconfirmed (web snippet only): a later commentary letting light-only areas qualify; the core text and the engine both require dense.
evidence: docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2292-2303 (13.09 text) and :2346-2356 (worked example: B and C hidden, D inside B's 15″ detection range)

entries.coverage_detail: Implemented but shipped OFF. _hidden_gain_value (40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:28578-28589) returns 0 because WEIGHT_HIDDEN_GAINED = 0.0 (:2633, after two inconclusive A/Bs, :2615-2631). It is only added at objective-trip endpoints (:10306-10314) and to threat-dodge candidates (:28965-28970). Even when switched on it never generates a 'go into this dense area' destination. It sizes the immunity by enemy centroid against the 15″ base range (_hidden_immunity_fraction :28548-28575), which ignores per-observer Gone to Ground and enemy movement. The cover nudge (:14817-14877) tests 'any polygon between me and one enemy centroid', which is unrelated to 13.09.
entries.engine_support: Reuse TerrainManager.is_model_hidden through the probe-model pattern _position_would_be_hidden (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28515). Use TerrainManager.area_at (:847), build_area_group_map, category_of (:792) and pieces_model_within_of (:927) to enumerate dense areas, and hidden_model_visible_to / detection_range_inches_for (:1047/:1061) per enemy observer. Use the placement ladder _try_move_with_collision_check (AIDecisionMaker.gd:15405) to fit every model inside. NEW: a candidate generator for dense areas reachable within M (or M + average D6) that can hold the whole unit, scored by the enemy shot volume that cannot get within detection range next turn, minus a discount for melee reach and indirect fire.
entries.value_reason: The corpus calls 'get to hidden 12' the main infantry movement goal in rounds 1-2 (F001: high confidence, 4 channels). It blanks a whole enemy shooting phase at no cost for units with nothing to shoot, and the full rule is already live in the engine. The bench says it pays only where infantry can reach dense terrain and survive there, so it must be scored by immunity fraction, not given a flat bonus.

entries.skeptic_note: Hidden is not dense-only. The 13.09 errata changes the first bullet to 'a terrain area that contains one or more light/dense terrain features' (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:529). The engine already implements this (TerrainManager.is_model_hidden -> category_allows_hidden, TerrainManager.gd:1001-1051, commit dc9d3b0). So both the 'unconfirmed light-only' caveat and 'the core text and the engine both require dense' are stale. Also wrong: '09.06: an Advance bars only charges and actions'. After an Advance the unit may shoot only with [ASSAULT] weapons (10.04 :1489-1491, 10.05 :1506-1516), and is barred from indirect shooting (10.07 :1553) and Explosives (15.05 :2659-2662). Per 01.02.07, a 'hidden unit' needs only one hidden model (errata_faq:49). Denying targeting still needs every model to be non-visible (06.01 :1098-1099). — 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:529, :49; 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2292-2303, 1098-1099, 1489-1516, 1553; TerrainManager.gd:1001-1051
entries.errata_note: Hidden needs a terrain area containing a light OR dense feature, not dense only (13.09 errata). The 'no ranged attacks in the previous turn' condition counts as met in the first turn (13.09.01), and a hidden model the attacker cannot fully see because of intervening DENSE features has gone to ground: its detection range drops by 3″, from 15″ to 12″, and can never go below 9″ (13.11.01, 02.02.01). A 'hidden unit' needs only one hidden model (01.02.07), not every alive model as RULINGS.md:169 says, but denying targeting still needs every model to be non-visible (06.01). — 13.09 errata; Commentary 13.09.01 Hidden and the First Turn; Commentary 13.11.01 Gone to Ground; Commentary 01.02.07 Describing Units; Commentary 02.02.01 Modifiers

entries.name: Break line of sight completely behind obscuring or Solid terrain
entries.description: End fully unseen by the enemy's dangerous shooters. Either stand just outside (not inside) a terrain area containing a light or dense feature so that every sight line crosses it, or stand behind the ground-level walls of a dense (Solid) feature. An unseen unit cannot be targeted by direct fire, Fire Overwatch, Explosives, Surveil or Precision. Only [INDIRECT FIRE] can still reach it: the target gets cover, and hits fail on 1-5 unless the shooter stayed stationary and has a spotter. This works for every unit type, including vehicles and monsters that can never be Hidden and units that shot last turn.
entries.when_to_use: Use when the unit does not need to shoot this turn, or can shoot from an angle that keeps the main threats blind, and it must survive: damaged or high-value units, characters, transports, units the opponent's kill cards pay for, and units that cannot be Hidden. Weight each enemy by the damage it could do next turn from where it can move to, not only from where it stands now. Do not step inside the obscuring area: 13.10 ignores any area that either model is within.
entries.unit_types: All. Essential for VEHICLE, MONSTER and MOUNTED units, and for units that shot recently.
entries.move_type: Normal Move / Advance / Fall Back (landing behind terrain) / Remain Stationary
entries.rules_basis: 13.10 OBSCURING (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2305-2311): areas with light or dense features are obscuring; if every line of sight crosses obscuring areas (excluding areas either model is within), the two models are not visible to each other. 13.11 SOLID (:2313-2316): no line of sight across enclosed gaps 3″ or less from ground level. 06.01 (:1024-1034, :1087-1110). 04.02 (:628-642). 10.07 (:1549-1574). Engine: TerrainManager._line_blocked_11e (:1169) via model_visible_11e (:1201), using 9-point base sampling. The 13.11 gap branch is dead code, but dense terrain always blocks at ground level (docs/rules/11th_edition_delta_audit.md:135-136). Models never block line of sight in the engine (:100).

entries.coverage_detail: Only the unscored Task-8 cover nudge exists. When the direct path is clear, _find_cover_path (40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:14746, :14817-14855) tries ±15° and ±30° headings and takes the first endpoint where _position_has_cover (:14857-14877) finds any terrain polygon between it and any single enemy centroid. There is no 13.10 test, no requirement that all threats be blind, and no destinations generated behind terrain. The threat model (:28794-28880) is distance-only. Only deployment (not movement) prefers line-of-sight blockers for characters and fragile shooters (_score_terrain_for_role :5594-5640).
entries.engine_support: TerrainManager.model_visible_11e / model_fully_visible_11e (:1201-1211) accept probe model dictionaries, and is_obscured_between (:976) handles point checks. LineOfSightManager.calculate_los_to_position (40k/autoloads/LineOfSightManager.gd:101) and calculate_visibility_grid_to_target (:340) answer 'who can see this spot'. RulesEngine.unit_sight_line (:6641) works on a copied board. NEW: a candidate generator for points on the far side of obscuring areas from the threat-weighted enemy positions, plus a 'visible enemy damage at destination' score that uses enemy next-turn positions.
entries.value_reason: It is the only full protection for vehicles, monsters and units that have just fired, and F005 calls staging out of line of sight the default opening. Line-of-sight queries that accept probe positions already exist, but the movement planner never calls them (inventory gap 1).

entries.name: Move into cover (Benefit of Cover: attacker's BS worsened by 1)
entries.description: This is the user's own 'move into cover' example. End the move so the unit has the benefit of cover against the expected attackers. Either every model of an INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM unit is within some terrain area (exposed craters and debris count), or every model is not fully visible to the attacking model because of intervening terrain features or obscuring areas. In 11e cover worsens the BS of each incoming ranged attack by 1; it is not a save bonus, so its value grows with shot volume rather than AP. It is all-or-nothing for the unit: one model in the open loses it. Use it when Hidden is not available: the unit will shoot, has shot recently, or enemies are inside detection range.
entries.when_to_use: Use when the unit expects to be shot next turn and cannot be Hidden or out of line of sight, and a terrain area within M can hold every model while keeping its own firing lanes. It is worth most against many weak BS-based shots. It is worthless against [TORRENT] (auto-hit), [IGNORES COVER], [PSYCHIC] (may ignore BS modifiers) and snap shooting (unmodified 6s). It is redundant for STEALTH units and against indirect fire (the target always has cover), and does nothing in melee. A [HEAVY] unit that creeps 3″ or less into cover keeps its +1 to hit.
entries.unit_types: INFANTRY, BEASTS, SWARM through the in-area clause; any unit through the not-fully-visible clause (see SUR-08 for vehicles and monsters).
entries.move_type: Normal Move / Advance / Remain Stationary; a Normal Move of 3″ or less for [HEAVY] units
entries.rules_basis: 13.08 BENEFIT OF COVER (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2278-2290): every model must qualify; worsen BS by 1. Terrain categories 13.03-13.05 (:2074-2095). 24.18 [IGNORES COVER] (:3783-3795). 24.33 STEALTH (:3922-3930). 24.37 [TORRENT] (:3943-3950). 24.29 [PSYCHIC] may ignore BS modifiers (:3878-3888). 15.09: snap shots hit on unmodified 6s irrespective of modifiers (:2749-2760). 10.07: an indirect target has cover (:1549-1574). 24.16 [HEAVY]: no model moved more than 3″ (:3751-3770). Engine: TerrainManager.unit_has_cover_11e (40k/autoloads/TerrainManager.gd:1380-1418), judged per attacker model. Cover is skipped for TORRENT, IGNORES COVER and PSYCHIC (RulesEngine.gd:17755-17761) and for snap shooting (RULINGS.md:498).

entries.coverage_detail: Only the B34 cover nudge applies (40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:14746, :14817-14877): the first ±15°/±30° heading whose endpoint has any terrain polygon between it and one enemy centroid. This is not 13.08: there is no candidate with every model inside a terrain area, and terrain categories are not checked. The AI's own _target_has_benefit_of_cover (:25044-25120) is 10e-style and used only to score shooting targets. A [HEAVY] creep of 3″ or less is never planned: B23 either holds or moves (:7419-7430).
entries.engine_support: TerrainManager.unit_has_cover_11e(unit with probe positions, attacker_model) (:1380), area_at (:847) and pieces_model_within_of (:927). ModifierStack.collect_hit_context_11e (ModifierStack.gd:96-121) prices the -1 BS, and ModifierStack.heavy_applies_11e (:168) handles the 3″ Heavy rule. NEW: a candidate generator for terrain areas within M that fit the whole unit and keep at least one target visible, scored by expected incoming hits removed (enemy BS-based shots × 1/6) minus firing lanes lost.
entries.value_reason: It is the user's own example. It gives -1 BS from every direction to the most common unit type, comes up all the time and is cheap to evaluate, and the current nudge does not implement the 11e rule.
entries.errata_note: Cover is decided separately for each attacking model (FAQ 13.08): each target model may qualify by either condition (in a terrain area or not fully visible), and a model in the open loses cover only against attackers that can fully see it. So it is not all-or-nothing against a whole enemy unit, and because BS can never be worsened past 6+ (Commentary 02.02.01), cover does nothing against BS 6+ attacks. — FAQ 13.08 Benefit of Cover; Commentary 02.02.01 Modifiers

entries.name: End the Movement phase out of Fire Overwatch reach
entries.description: Fire Overwatch (1CP) is used once, at the END of our Movement phase, after the opponent has seen every move. One unengaged, non-TITANIC, non-battle-shocked enemy unit snap-shoots ONE visible, eligible (unengaged) unit of ours within 24″, hitting only on unmodified 6s with no hit re-rolls. Only final positions matter. Units can cross open ground freely, but the ones we can least afford to lose should end the phase unseen (out of line of sight, Hidden beyond detection range, beyond Lone Operative range, or embarked), engaged, or more than 24″ away and outside the weapon range of the enemy's high-volume and [TORRENT] shooters. The opponent can shoot only one unit, so manage the army's worst exposure (the best target they will have), not the sum. Baiting with a cheap model does not work in 11e (see rejected).
entries.when_to_use: Use when the opponent has 1+ CP and at least one unengaged, non-battle-shocked unit with high shot volume or [TORRENT] weapons, within 24″ and line of sight of where our valuable units would end. It matters most when those units are fragile, high-value, about to charge or about to score. It matters least for cheap chaff and in rounds 4-5, when objective moves are mandatory.
entries.unit_types: All. Most important for low-Toughness multi-wound infantry, characters, fragile vehicles and units that need full strength to charge.
entries.move_type: End position of every move in our Movement phase (Normal / Advance / Disembark / Reserves arrival / Embark)
entries.rules_basis: 15.08 FIRE OVERWATCH (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2735-2747): WHEN is the end of the opponent's Movement phase; TARGET is one friendly unengaged unit, excluding TITANIC. 15.09 SNAP SHOOTING (:2749-2760): one visible, eligible enemy unit within 24″; hits only on an unmodified 6 irrespective of BS or modifiers (so cover is irrelevant); no hit re-rolls. 15.01: the same stratagem only once per phase (:2496-2499). 01.07: battle-shocked units cannot be targeted with their own side's stratagems (:212-216). 04.02: targets must be unengaged (:628-642). 17.03: engaged MONSTER/VEHICLE units can be targeted only in the attacker's own Shooting phase (:2894-2909). Engine: 11e timing is movement_phase_end only (40k/phases/MovementPhase.gd:1745-1749; StratagemManager.gd:174, :5086-5100); RulesEngine.snap_shooting_targets_11e (:1475). In the engine [TORRENT] still auto-hits under snap shooting (RulesEngine.gd:2443, :2474, :2509); the core text does not settle Torrent against 15.09.

entries.coverage_detail: _overwatch_exposure_penalty (40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:28660-28687) exists, but OVERWATCH_EXPOSURE_PENALTY = 0.0 (:2662), and it is applied only to objective-trip candidates (:10290-10304). Even when switched on it is range-only (a 24″ band around enemy centroids) and sums every newly exposed enemy's shot volume instead of taking the single best target the opponent gets. It ignores visibility, Hidden and engagement, and does not skip engaged or TITANIC watchers. Its header comment (:2650-2656) wrongly says the engine still uses the 10e timing.
entries.engine_support: RulesEngine.snap_shooting_targets_11e (:1475) on a copied board answers 'which of my units could this enemy overwatch'. TerrainManager.model_visible_11e (:1201) and hidden_model_visible_to (:1047) handle probe positions. _unit_ranged_shot_volume (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28637) gives volume, and RulesEngine.is_torrent_weapon (:11361) identifies auto-hit volume. NEW: an army-level, end-of-phase evaluator: the maximum over our units of expected snap-shot damage × unit value, given the opponent's CP and unengaged watchers, applied to each mover's candidate set.
entries.value_reason: It applies in every one of our Movement phases, the corpus treats it as a top 11e consideration (F004: high confidence, 4 channels), and only end positions need scoring. The cost per phase is bounded (one unit, 6s to hit), so it is a tie-breaker-plus rather than an override.

entries.name: Stay outside enemy charge reach (kite)
entries.description: End the move beyond the next-turn charge reach of every dangerous enemy melee unit. That reach is the enemy's M, plus D6 only if it can Advance and still charge (e.g. riled-up Orks), plus 12″: a charge target must be within 12″ and within the 2D6 roll, and engagement range does not extend this. Shooters should keep those enemies inside their own weapon range at the same time (retrograde shooting). Dense features over 2″ high, which non-INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM/MOBILE models cannot move through horizontally, lengthen the enemy's real reach. Hidden does not stop charges, so this is the counter to melee.
entries.when_to_use: Use for fragile shooters, characters, aura/support carriers, artillery and melee-weak vehicles facing enemy melee units, when the unit is not needed on a priced objective this turn and being charged would be a bad trade. Advance away when no shooting is lost (no targets in range, or [ASSAULT] guns). Skip it for lockers and for units that want to be charged.
entries.unit_types: Ranged infantry, characters, support/aura units, artillery, light vehicles
entries.move_type: Normal Move / Advance (break contact) / Fall Back (to a spot outside reach)
entries.rules_basis: 11.02: eligible to charge if within 12″ of an enemy, unengaged, and did not Advance or Fall Back this turn (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1603-1625). 11.04: targets must be within 12″ and within the roll; the move must end engaged (:1640-1666). 09.05/09.06 move distances (:1390-1415). 13.06: dense sections over 2″ block horizontal moves by models without INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM/MOBILE (:2163-2183). Orks riled up: their Advance does not prevent a charge (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/RULES.md:76). Engine: ChargeMove11e.eligible / selectable_distance_ceiling (40k/scripts/rules/movetypes/ChargeMove11e.gd:31, :106).

entries.name: Ordered Retreat out of a losing combat to a safe landing spot
entries.description: Fall back up to M with an engaged unit that is not battle-shocked when it would lose the coming fights or is wasted tied up. Land somewhere actually safe or useful: out of line of sight or Hidden, outside the enemy's charge reach, in cover, or still contesting an objective. Ordered Retreat cannot pass through enemy models. Afterwards the unit cannot shoot, charge or start an action this turn unless an ability allows it, so price that loss.
entries.when_to_use: Use when the unit is engaged and not battle-shocked, and its expected losses in the next Fight phases (ours and theirs) exceed the value of staying (OC kept, shield from shooting, lock). A legal route around the enemy models must lead to a landing spot whose next-turn exposure is lower than staying. Prefer units with fall-back-and-shoot or fall-back-and-charge abilities, and be wary with vehicles, which lose a whole turn of shooting.
entries.unit_types: Any engaged unit that is not battle-shocked
entries.rules_basis: 09.07 FALL-BACK MOVE (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1417-1441): eligible if engaged; Ordered Retreat only if not battle-shocked; the unit must end unengaged; afterwards it is not eligible to shoot, declare a charge or start an action this turn. 03.01: bases cannot move through enemy models (:389-395). Engine: FallBackMove.select_mode / after_moving_effects (40k/scripts/rules/movetypes/FallBackMove.gd:52, :116-135); ShootingType honours fall-back-and-shoot abilities (ShootingType.gd:80-93).

entries.coverage_detail: _decide_engaged_unit falls back by default whenever the unit is not holding an objective (40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:12123-12161). The survival estimate (:12373-12427) only changes on-objective decisions and the narration. The landing spot (_compute_fall_back_destinations :12185-12273) is the best objective 'behind' the unit, or straight away from the engaging enemies, tried at 100/75/50/25% of M. It is never scored for cover, line of sight, Hidden or charge threat.
entries.engine_support: _compute_fall_back_destinations (:12185) and _try_fall_back_positions as the executor. To score landing spots: TerrainManager.model_visible_11e (:1201), is_model_hidden (:999), unit_has_cover_11e (:1380), and _evaluate_position_threat (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28794). entries.value_reason: The decision comes up most turns once armies meet. The AI makes it by a fixed rule and lands in the open.
entries.errata_note: Ordered Retreat is also unavailable when an enemy stratagem or ability instructs the unit to take a Desperate Escape test. The unit must then use Desperate Escape (a hazard roll per model, with that rule's penalty applied to each roll, plus a battle-shock roll), so check the engaged enemy for such rules before pricing the retreat. — Commentary 09.07.01 Desperate Escape

entries.name: Hull-down a vehicle or monster behind intervening terrain
entries.description: Models without INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM never get cover by standing inside terrain and can never be Hidden. They get the benefit of cover only against attacking models that cannot see them fully because of intervening terrain features or obscuring areas, judged per attacking model. Park the model so terrain clips the main enemy anti-tank's view of it while it keeps its own firing lanes. Do not stand inside the obscuring area you rely on: 13.10 ignores any area either model is within.
entries.when_to_use: Use when a VEHICLE or MONSTER must stay exposed enough to shoot or hold an objective and cannot fully break line of sight, and the enemy anti-tank comes from a predictable arc. It is worthless against [IGNORES COVER], [TORRENT], [PSYCHIC] and snap shooting. For [HEAVY] weapons, an adjustment of 3″ or less keeps the +1 to hit.
entries.unit_types: VEHICLE, MONSTER, MOUNTED and any unit without INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM (infantry outside a terrain area can use the same clause)
entries.move_type: Normal Move / Remain Stationary (a shuffle of 3″ or less for [HEAVY])
entries.rules_basis: 13.08 second bullet (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2283-2286): not fully visible to the attacking model because of intervening terrain features and/or obscuring areas. 06.01: a model is fully visible only if every part facing the observer is visible (:1087-1104). 13.10: areas either model is within are excluded (:2305-2311). 13.09: Hidden requires INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM (:2292-2297). Engine: the not-fully-visible branch of TerrainManager.unit_has_cover_11e, per attacker model (40k/autoloads/TerrainManager.gd:1403-1416), via model_fully_visible_11e (:1207).

entries.name: Stage as far forward as possible while out of line of sight
entries.description: In the opening rounds, move units to the far side of mid-board obscuring or Solid terrain from every enemy gun, as far forward as they can go while staying unseen. They cannot be shot or overwatched now, yet threaten objectives and charges next turn. This includes vehicles, monsters and jump/melee units that cannot use Hidden, and it also physically occupies the staging space the opponent wants.
entries.when_to_use: Use in rounds 1-2, or the turn before a strike, against a shooting army or when going first. The unit must not be needed on an objective this turn, and from the staging point its next-turn move plus charge or weapon reach must still cover its targets or objectives.
entries.unit_types: All; especially melee units, jump-pack infantry, fast units, vehicles and monsters
entries.move_type: Normal Move / Advance (if it will not charge or act this turn anyway)
entries.rules_basis: 13.10/13.11 (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2305-2316). 15.09: snap shooting needs a visible target within 24″ (:2749-2760). 11.02: a charge next turn needs the target within 12″ (:1603-1625). The rules mechanics are verified; 'this is the default opening' is player opinion (ai_learnings.json F005, medium confidence).

entries.name: Go dark: hold fire in light or dense terrain to keep or reset Hidden
entries.description: Plan the turn so a unit that can be Hidden deliberately makes no ranged attacks. It stays in, or moves into or within, a dense area to a spot where it has nothing worth shooting, because firing forfeits Hidden for this turn AND the next (the opponent's coming turn). Reset variant: a unit that shot last turn is Hidden again in the opponent's turn only if it skips shooting in our turn in between. Units whose abilities say their attacks do not prevent them being hidden (Shadow Masters) shoot instead.
entries.when_to_use: Use when the unit is or will be Hidden, its best shot this turn is low value, it holds an objective or a backfield position, and a large share of enemy shooters are outside detection range, so the immunity being given up is large. Drop it when the unit's expected damage is significant.
entries.unit_types: INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM objective holders, screens and backfield shooters; Phobos/Scout units with Shadow Masters are the exception
entries.move_type: Remain Stationary, or Normal Move into dense terrain, paired with skipping the unit in the Shooting phase
entries.rules_basis: 13.09: 'did not make one or more ranged attacks during this turn or during the previous turn' (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2292-2303). Engine stamp: flags.last_shot_idx, hidden again only when delta ≥ 2 (40k/autoloads/TerrainManager.gd:1014-1026). Shadow Masters exception (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/RULINGS.md:356). Inference, not validated: under 15.08/15.09 a Fire Overwatch is the unit shooting as described in Making Attacks (:2735-2760), so it should also forfeit Hidden, but the engine stamps only Shooting-phase shots (RULINGS.md:356).

entries.value_reason: It is a corpus-confirmed two-turn trade (F002) and is already implemented but switched off. It is mostly a shooting decision.
entries.skeptic_note: Hidden works in light OR dense terrain areas (13.09 errata, errata_faq:529), so 'in dense terrain' is too narrow. The Overwatch inference is supported by the text: snap shooting is the unit shooting as in Making Attacks (15.09 :2754-2755), i.e. ranged attacks, which forfeits Hidden this turn and the next (13.09 :2298-2299). 13.11.01 adds that a unit that shot cannot go to ground, even with an ability that lets it shoot and stay hidden (errata_faq:539). In the first turn the 'previous turn' condition is treated as met (errata_faq:533). — 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:529, :533, :539; 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2298-2299, 2749-2755
entries.errata_note: Hidden works in a terrain area with a light OR dense feature, not dense only (13.09 errata), and in the first turn the 'previous turn' condition counts as met (13.09.01). Holding fire also keeps Gone to Ground (-3″ detection range against attackers whose view is blocked by intervening dense features), which a unit that shot this turn or last turn always loses, even if an ability like Shadow Masters lets it shoot and stay hidden (13.11.01 Designer's Note). — 13.09 errata; Commentary 13.09.01 Hidden and the First Turn; Commentary 13.11.01 Gone to Ground

entries.name: Stand off outside enemy shooting reach (out-range or break contact)
entries.description: End beyond each dangerous enemy shooter's next-turn reach: its M (plus D6 only for an Advance with [ASSAULT] weapons) plus weapon range. Ideally the enemy stays inside our own range (out-ranging). When we have nothing to shoot, simply Advance away to break contact. Distances are measured between the closest models.
entries.when_to_use: Use when our range or speed beats theirs (long guns against short-ranged shooters, fast units against slow ones), and for units that must survive (Beacon holder, characters, damaged units) with no option to break line of sight. If the unit has no target this turn, Advancing costs nothing. It is usually infeasible against 36-48″ guns; use SUR-02 then.
entries.unit_types: Long-ranged shooters, fast units, characters, damaged units
entries.rules_basis: 04.02: targets must be within range and visible (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:628-642). 09.05/09.06 (:1390-1415). 10.05: after an Advance only [ASSAULT] weapons can shoot (:1506-1520). 01.04: measure to the closest part of the base (:163-170).

https://www.tabletopbattles.com/start-competing-40k-deployment-tactics-surviving-turn-zero/ (search snippet: 36″ threat ranges are manageable; ~48″ makes avoidance near impossible)
entries.coverage_detail: The threat model has a shooting zone equal to the enemy's max weapon range around its centroid, without enemy movement (40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:28718). It is weighted by THREAT_SHOOTING_PENALTY 0.5 (:2587) inside the threat dodge (:28892-28990) and objective scoring (:10285). The MOV-1 clamp and firing-position preservation keep our own targets in range (:14476-14484, :7574-7593). No candidate maximises our reach minus theirs, and none retreats to break contact.
entries.engine_support: RulesEngine.max_ranged_weapon_range_inches (:6693) for both sides (it includes attached characters and codex range bonuses); unit_within_weapon_reach (:6718); _calculate_enemy_threat_data (:28695) once the shooting radius includes enemy M (and D6 for Assault). NEW: 'stand-off band' candidates between the enemy's reach and our own range.
entries.value_reason: It is decisive in asymmetric matchups and for scoring-critical units, but often infeasible against long-range armies.

entries.name: Keep standalone characters out of sight or reach
entries.description: 11e has no Look Out, Sir. A CHARACTER that is not part of an attached unit (never attached, bodyguard destroyed, or unable to attach) is an ordinary target unless it has Lone Operative. Move it Hidden, out of line of sight, into a transport, or beyond enemy reach, and keep it near the units it buffs only if it can still stay unseen there.
entries.when_to_use: Use for standalone characters with valuable auras or buffs and for leaders whose bodyguard died, and whenever the opponent scores Assassination (3 VP per CHARACTER model, +1 if W4+) or fields [PRECISION] snipers.
entries.unit_types: CHARACTER units not in an attached unit and without Lone Operative
entries.rules_basis: The 11e core text has no Look Out, Sir rule (grep of docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt), and .llm/rules-audit.md:17 notes that standalone protection lives only in Lone Operative. 24.24 Lone Operative (:3813-3828). 19.01: an attached unit is a single unit for all rules purposes (:3094-3101). 05.03: CHARACTER groups come last only within the target unit (:783-800). 24.28 [PRECISION] (:3856-3870). Assassination card: 40k/data/40kdc/missionCards.json:2272.
evidence: .llm/rules-audit.md:17 (Look Out Sir removed; standalone protection only via Lone Operative)

entries.coverage_detail: _evaluate_position_threat multiplies threat by 1.5 for CHARACTER units (40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:28805-28809, :28865-28867). Screen-protect sends a cheap unit 60% of the way from an unattached character toward the nearest enemy (+50 priority, :15055-15076). Both are distance-only, and models never block line of sight in the engine, so the screen does nothing against shooting.
entries.engine_support: The destination queries from SUR-01/02/16. NEW: a CHARACTER multiplier on visible enemy damage (line-of-sight based) instead of on distance.
entries.value_reason: Characters carry buffs and VP, and standalone ones die fast, but each army has only a few of them.

entries.name: Lone Operative: end beyond the range it can be seen from (12″ or X″)
entries.description: An unattached LONE OPERATIVE unit is not visible to enemy models more than 12″ (or its X″) away and cannot be targeted by [INDIRECT FIRE] from beyond that range. End every move so that no enemy model that could shoot it next turn can get within that range (enemy M + 12″/X″, between the closest models), or so that terrain blocks their view, while it still spots, scores, performs actions or snipes. It does not stop charges.
entries.when_to_use: Use on every move of an unattached Lone Operative (assassins, lone characters, snipers).
entries.unit_types: LONE OPERATIVE units that are not part of an attached unit
entries.rules_basis: 24.24 LONE OPERATIVE and Lone Operative X″ (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3813-3828). Engine: RulesEngine.has_lone_operative (40k/autoloads/RulesEngine.gd:9829-9853; includes the X″ variant and conditional grants) and get_lone_operative_range (:9953-9969); docs/rules/11th_edition_delta_audit.md:193 marks it done.

entries.coverage_detail: The T7-11 override (40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:7432-7465): if the nearest enemy centroid is within 12″ + M, the unit retreats to the candidate point (directly away, or ±30°/60°) that is more than 12.5″ from every enemy centroid and closest to the objective (_get_lone_operative_safe_position :14010-14076); otherwise it holds. Problems: the range is a fixed 12″ (:7437) that ignores Lone Operative X″; centroid-to-centroid distances (:13999-14008) overstate the real model-to-model gap; enemy movement is not added; and AIAbilityAnalyzer.has_lone_operative only matches an ability named exactly 'lone operative' (AIAbilityAnalyzer.gd:400-407), so X″ variants and conditional grants are missed. It is an override, not a scored candidate.
entries.engine_support: RulesEngine.get_lone_operative_range (:9953) and has_lone_operative (:9829); Measurement.model_to_model_distance_px for closest-model distances; TerrainManager.model_visible_11e as a line-of-sight fallback. NEW: score Lone Operative candidates by the enemy models able to get within X″ with line of sight next turn, combined with the unit's firing or scoring value.
entries.value_reason: Few units have it, but the protection is total when respected. The existing override is close and needs fixes rather than a new mechanism.
absorbed: COO-32 (Keep Lone Operative spacing while staying in your own range)
entries.errata_note: Lone Operative is not limited to unattached units: an attached unit in which every model has it also benefits, with the highest X among its models on the battlefield applied to the whole unit. It also becomes active again once an attached unit is reduced to only Lone Operative models (e.g. its bodyguard is destroyed), and a Lone Operative range can never be modified below 9″ or above 30″. — Commentary 24.24.01 Attached units and Lone Operative; Commentary 02.02.01 Modifiers

entries.name: Choose Desperate Escape (or take to the skies) to escape through enemy models
entries.description: When an Ordered Retreat cannot reach a legal or useful unengaged spot (the unit is wrapped, or the safe spot or objective lies beyond the enemy), choose Desperate Escape. Models may then move through enemy models. The cost is one hazard roll per model before moving (1-2 fails: 1 mortal wound, or 3 if every model is a MONSTER/VEHICLE) and, if the unit was not already battle-shocked, a battle-shock roll afterwards. It is mandatory for battle-shocked units, so for them the real choice is escape vs stay (SUR-06/SUR-18). A FLY unit can instead take to the skies for the fall-back (-2″, or no penalty with HOVER) and move through all models and terrain with no hazard rolls.
entries.when_to_use: Use for surrounded units, for destinations reachable only through the enemy, and for expendable or numerous models where losing about a third to hazards costs less than staying. For battle-shocked units, use it only if leaving still beats staying. FLY units should prefer taking to the skies.
entries.unit_types: Any engaged unit; especially FLY units (take to the skies) and hordes; avoid with small elite units
entries.move_type: Fall Back (Desperate Escape mode, or FLY taking to the skies)

entries.name: Stay outside distance-gated enemy bonus bands (half range, Explosives 8″, TOWERING 12″)
entries.description: Deny enemy bonuses that switch on by distance when targets are selected. [MELTA X] adds X damage, and [RAPID FIRE X] adds X attacks, if the target unit is within half range. The EXPLOSIVES stratagem (six D6, each 4+ is a mortal wound) needs a visible, unengaged target within 8″ of an EXPLOSIVES/GRENADES model whose unit did not Advance. A TOWERING attacker gets Plunging Fire (+1 BS, cancelling cover) within 12″. Keep the closest model of a valuable unit beyond enemy M + band, or screen the approach. The enemy moves before it shoots.
entries.when_to_use: Use for our vehicles and monsters against melta units (including melta arriving from reserves), for elite infantry against rapid-fire blobs, for any unit against EXPLOSIVES/GRENADES units when the opponent has CP, and for ground units against TOWERING models. It is most achievable against slow or stationary enemy units (heavy weapons, artillery).
entries.unit_types: VEHICLE, MONSTER, elite multi-wound infantry; any ground-level unit against TOWERING attackers
entries.rules_basis: 24.25 [MELTA] (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3833-3848) and 24.30 [RAPID FIRE] (:3896-3908): half range is judged at the Select Targets step. 15.05 EXPLOSIVES (:2651-2671). 22.05 PLUNGING FIRE (:3453-3462). Engine: half range is measured from each firing model to the closest target model (40k/autoloads/RulesEngine.gd:2343-2366); TerrainManager.plunging_fire_applies (:1425-1442). This corrects first-principles#5 and #12, which said these texts are not in the local sources: they are.

entries.name: Tuck the attached CHARACTER model where the main shooters cannot see it
entries.description: When moving an attached unit, place the leader or support CHARACTER model behind terrain or on the far side of the unit, so the enemy's [PRECISION] shooters cannot see that model even if the bodyguards are visible. [PRECISION] can only promote a CHARACTER allocation group that is visible to an attacking model. This protects the leader's buffs and denies Assassination.
entries.when_to_use: Use when the enemy has [PRECISION] ranged weapons or snipers, when the leader carries key buffs, or when Assassination is in play. It matters mostly against ranged Precision; in melee the character is usually visible.
entries.unit_types: Attached units (Leader or Support characters)
entries.rules_basis: 24.28 [PRECISION] (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3856-3870): only CHARACTER models visible to one or more attacking models can be picked. 05.03: CHARACTER groups otherwise go last (:783-800). entries.name: Shape the unit defensively: compact, near edge pulled back, all models in the area
entries.description: Arrange the models for defence. Keep the unit compact: coherency is 2″ to one other model and 9″ to every model, and a unit that casualties from Overwatch, hazard rolls or shooting split into two groups loses models at the end of the turn. Pull back the models closest to the enemy, because charge, Overwatch (24″), half-range and detection distances are all measured to the closest model. Keep every model inside the terrain area when relying on cover or Hidden. Spreading out buys nothing in 11e: the defender orders the allocation groups, [BLAST] counts models rather than spacing, and Deadly Demise and Explosives hit whole units.
entries.when_to_use: Use on every move of a multi-model unit that will be exposed: large units, screens, objective chains, and units near the edge of a threat band.
entries.unit_types: Multi-model units
entries.rules_basis: 03.03 COHERENCY and Regaining Coherency (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:518-537). 05.03: the defender declares the allocation order (:783-800). 24.05 [BLAST] counts models in the target unit (:3595-3610). 24.08 Deadly Demise hits each unit (:3670-3690). 01.04: measure to the closest part of the base (:163-170). 13.08/13.09 require every model. Engine: PhaseManager._enforce_coherency_11e (40k/autoloads/PhaseManager.gd:576); AttackSequence.check_unit_coherency (40k/scripts/rules/AttackSequence.gd:229); GameConstants.coherency_envelope_inches (GameConstants.gd:76).

Keeping every model in the area still matters because the unit can be targeted if any one model is visible (06.01); cover does need every model to qualify, but this is judged separately for each attacking model (FAQ 13.08). — Commentary 01.02.07 Describing Units; FAQ 13.08 Benefit of Cover

entries.name: Stay unseen by every enemy unit to deny indirect-fire spotting
entries.description: Enemy [INDIRECT FIRE] weapons hit only on unmodified 6s, improving to 4+ only if the firing unit remained stationary AND one or more of its friendly units can see the target. A unit that ends unseen by ALL enemy units (out of every enemy's line of sight, or Hidden beyond every enemy model's detection range) keeps enemy artillery hitting on 6s. A Lone Operative cannot be targeted by indirect fire at all from beyond its range.
entries.when_to_use: Use when the opponent fields stationary artillery or mortars, our unit is a likely indirect target (dense infantry, objective holders), and a spot unseen from all sides is reachable.
entries.unit_types: All (most often Hidden infantry)
entries.rules_basis: 10.07 INDIRECT SHOOTING (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1549-1574): the target has cover; no hit re-rolls; an unmodified 1-5 fails, unless the unit remained stationary and the target is visible to one or more friendly units, in which case 1-3 fails. 24.24 Lone Operative against indirect fire (:3813-3828). Engine: RulesEngine._indirect_hit_fail_band_11e (40k/autoloads/RulesEngine.gd:6594-6605) returns 3 only when the shooter remained stationary and some friendly unit has line of sight; IndirectShooting.has_spotter (40k/scripts/rules/shootingtypes/IndirectShooting.gd:47).

entries.name: Keep bystander units clear of melee scrums (more than 5″, at least more than 3″)
entries.description: Shooters and characters parked next to an ongoing combat can be dragged into it in the Fight phase. An enemy unit that was engaged at the start of the Fight step but is now unengaged may make an Overrun fight, whose extra pile-in can target our units within 5″. An enemy unit that fought may consolidate, and if it is within 3″ of our units it must then use Engaging Consolidation to engage them. Our bystander is then locked for the next turn: it must fall back or use only close-quarters shooting.
entries.when_to_use: Use when moving shooters, characters or objective holders near a combat that will continue in either player's Fight phase.
entries.unit_types: Shooting units, characters, objective holders
entries.move_type: End positions of Normal / Advance moves (adjacent consequence: Fight-phase pile-in and consolidation)
entries.rules_basis: 12.04: a unit is eligible to fight if it is engaged or was engaged at the start of the step (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1819-1824). 12.06 OVERRUN FIGHT: one additional pile-in (:1866-1877). 12.03: an unengaged unit's pile-in targets enemy units within 5″ (:1737-1766). 12.07/12.08: consolidating is optional, but a unit that consolidates within 3″ of enemy units must use Engaging Consolidation (:1725-1728, :1934-1990). CORRECTED: core-rules#18 said the enemy 'must' consolidate into us; the move itself is optional, only its mode is mandatory.

entries.engine_support: The ConsolidationMove and PileInMove templates for reach; RulesEngine.units_in_engagement_range (:18481) to find enemy units that will fight. NEW: 5″/3″ bands around engaged enemy units in the threat model for units that are not melee-focused.

entries.errata_note: Engaging Consolidation applies only to an unengaged enemy unit within 3″; a still-engaged enemy uses Ongoing Consolidation, and its 3″ move can also end engaged with a nearby bystander. Per the 12.08 errata, after either mode each of our units it ends engaged with that has not fought this phase must be selected to fight, so a dragged-in bystander fights back at once but is still locked in combat afterwards. — 12.08 errata (Consolidation Move, After Moving, Ongoing Consolidation)

entries.name: Keep friendly units more than 6″ from our own Deadly Demise models that may die
entries.description: When a Deadly Demise model is destroyed, on a 6 every unit within 6″, friend or foe, suffers X mortal wounds. This happens after any passengers have made their emergency disembark, which leaves them inside the radius. Do not park fragile characters, infantry or other Deadly Demise vehicles (chain explosions) next to our damaged Deadly Demise vehicles and monsters. The mirror move, driving a dying Deadly Demise model into enemies, is the existing ram override.
entries.when_to_use: Use when our DEADLY DEMISE model is damaged and likely to die this round, especially with D3/D6 values. Give it low weight, since it fires only on a 6.
entries.unit_types: Friendly units near our own DEADLY DEMISE VEHICLE/MONSTER models
entries.rules_basis: 24.08 DEADLY DEMISE (docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3670-3690): on a 6, each unit within 6″ suffers X mortal wounds, after emergency disembarks. 18.05: passengers are set up wholly within 6″ (:3061-3078). entries.description: Some characters and support pieces have Lone Operative only while within 3″ of a specified friendly unit: Ghazghkull (Da Grand Warlord's Ladz), Big Mek with Shokk Attack Gun (Support Shokka), Beastboss on Squigosaur and Mozrog (Boss of da Hunt, Beast Snagga Following), Wartrakks (Speednob Support, every model), a Dreadherder Big Mek near an ORKS WALKER, Techmarine and Iron Father Feirros near an ADEPTUS ASTARTES VEHICLE, Iron Priest near a SPACE WOLVES VEHICLE, and Guilliman (Leader of Astartes) near ADEPTUS ASTARTES INFANTRY. entries.name: Spend a temporary defensive buff: accept an exposed route this turn
entries.description: Defensive effects that last until the start of our next turn change how much exposure a move can accept. Examples: riled-up Orks (5+ InSv), Librarian Force Dome (4+ InSv), Tigurius Prescience (+1 Sv), and Dread Host GOLDEN LIGHT OF THE MOIRAIDES on ingress (-1 to hit against the unit and no snap shooting at it). While such a buff is active, or castable this Movement phase, take the open-ground route or the forward objective that would normally be too exposed.
entries.when_to_use: Use when the buff is active or will be cast this phase, the exposed route gains an objective, charge position or tempo, and the enemy's damage is mostly the kind the buff blunts (AP-heavy fire for an invulnerable save; any shooting for -1 to hit).

entries.name: Deny Surveil the Foe: stay unseen or beyond 18″ of surveillers, or shelter under our decoyed objectives
entries.description: When the opponent's primary is Surveil the Foe, their Surveil action in the Shooting phase tags one visible enemy unit within 18″ of the acting unit and pays 4 VP at the end of the turn, unless every surveilled unit is within range of an objective shielded by our operation markers. Deny it by ending our units unseen (out of line of sight or Hidden), or more than 18″ plus enemy M from their likely acting units. When we play Smoke and Mirrors, also park exposed units within range of our decoyed objectives whose markers survive, and keep enemy units from ending moves within range of them, since that scrubs the marker.
entries.when_to_use: Use when our primary is Smoke and Mirrors or the opponent's is Surveil the Foe. It is low priority against kill and objective intents.
entries.unit_types: Any; preferably the units that decoyed the objective

entries.name: Move toward an enemy to shoot it
entries.description: User example. Pick the most valuable target the unit can hurt this turn and end a Normal move where as many firing models as possible have it within range (judged per model, edge to edge) and visible (see OFF-03). Prefer endpoints that reach several targets, which gives the Shooting phase options, and measure with the unit's effective range, including codex range extensions. An Advance limits the unit to [ASSAULT] weapons (OFF-13), so walk unless that trade is better.
entries.when_to_use: The unit's best target (expected damage × target value) is out of range now but reachable within M, the shot is worth more than the objective trip, and the unit is not held by a stationary gate (OFF-06 Heavy, OFF-07 Indirect).
entries.unit_types: Any unit with ranged weapons
entries.rules_basis: 04.02: each target must be visible to the firing model, within range and unengaged (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:628-642). 06.01: a unit is visible if any of its models is (:1098-1099). 10.04: normal shooting requires the unit to be unengaged and not to have advanced (:1489-1491). 10.05: after an Advance, only [ASSAULT] weapons can fire (:1506-1515). Effective range including the Ork Dakka! Dakka! Dakka! bonus: RulesEngine.gd:6693-6703.

entries.name: Move toward an enemy to charge it
entries.description: User example. Choose the target by value, not by proximity, and end the Movement phase where it is within 12″ and the charge roll is most likely to cover the edge-to-edge gap, counting the 2D6 plus any modifiers and re-rolls. In 11e the target must be within the roll itself: a 7″ gap needs a 7 (58%), a 9″ gap a 9 (28%). The move must end unengaged. Do not Advance or Fall Back unless a rule allows a charge afterwards (OFF-23, OFF-33), and do not start an action or make a Rapid or Combat disembark with a unit that has to charge. Units with +1/+2 or a charge re-roll (Command Re-roll re-rolls the whole roll) can stage farther back, outside the target's threat. If no charge is possible this turn, close in so it is possible next turn.
entries.when_to_use: A melee-capable unit has a worthwhile target within roughly M + 7-9″, with a 12″ maximum gap after the move. Aim for a final gap of 7″ or less without bonuses. Account for Overwatch (OFF-05), lanes (OFF-12) and Heroic Intervention support (OFF-24).
entries.unit_types: Melee units, and any unit whose charge pays off (Fights First, [LANCE])
entries.move_type: Normal (Advance only with an advance-and-charge rule, or to close in for next turn)
entries.rules_basis: 11.02 eligibility: within 12″, unengaged, and no advance or fall-back this turn (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1617-1622). The 2D6 roll is the maximum distance, and the player may decline after rolling (:1624-1629). 11.04: targets must be within 12″ AND within the roll; the unit must end engaged with every target and with no other unit; Fights First until end of turn (:1647-1665). 16.01: a unit that starts an action cannot charge (:2819-2822). 18.04: Rapid and Combat Disembark forbid charging (:3050-3057). 15.02: Command Re-roll re-rolls the whole charge roll (:2658-2673). 24.21 [LANCE]: +1 to wound after a charge move (:3767-3775). Correction: first-principles#33 says an unmodified 2 always fails. The sidebar says a double 1 never suffices only in the absence of modifiers (:1593-1613).

entries.coverage_detail: B04 charge_intent (AIDecisionMaker.gd:3812-3906) keeps one target per melee-capable unit. Score = 2×melee damage plus a lock bonus, ×1.3 if the target is on an objective, ×0.5 if the post-move centroid gap is over 9″, ×1.2 if it is 6″ or less. It has no roll odds and no edge gaps. The T7-23 steer blends the move 30/50/70% toward that target (CHARGE_BLEND_WEIGHTS 2541) only if it then ends within 9″ centroid to centroid (CHARGE_BLEND_REACH_INCHES 2540; 7491-7548); otherwise it re-plans straight to the objective (7600-7622). The charge_lane term adds +3×alignment to objective scores (10316-10334). Melee-focused units take the chase gate instead (2947-3099): the NEAREST enemy by centroid distance plus terrain penalty (3114-3151), filtered by round and horde distance limits, then a full Normal move or Advance straight at the target centroid with threat avoidance off (7228-7272). There is no stop-short staging. Planning ignores charge modifiers (FIX_CHARGE_REROLL_ODDS = 0.0 at 1960; charge_roll_bonus is never read). The real odds helpers (_charge_roll_needed 18840, _charge_success_probability 18928) are only used in the Charge phase.
entries.engine_support: Reuse _charge_roll_needed (18840), _charge_success_probability (18928), _charge_odds_with_reroll (18968), _get_closest_model_pair_info (19703), _estimate_charge_terrain_penalty (98) and _estimate_melee_damage (19576) at a probe end position, plus the codex charge_roll_bonus helpers (SMDetachmentsB.gd:315, SWDetachments11e.gd:200, CustodesDetachments.gd:711, CustodesEnhancements.gd:515, OrkAbilities11e.gd:931). The chase gate should then pick its target by this value instead of by proximity.
entries.value_reason: The user's own example and the only way melee units deal damage. The current chase, aimed at the nearest target's centroid with no odds model, wastes charges.

entries.name: Open a sight line to the target
entries.description: Reposition so each firing model has at least one sight line to the target that crosses no obscuring terrain area that neither model is within, and that does not pass through a Solid feature's enclosed gaps 3″ or less above ground. In practice: step around a ruin corner, or put part of a base into the edge of an obscuring area, which stops that area blocking because areas a model is within are excluded. Prefer a 'peek' spot that sees the target while as few other enemy units as possible can see back. Standing inside the area also lets enemies see in.
entries.when_to_use: The target is in range but not visible from the current spot or from the straight-line endpoint. Suits glass-cannon shooters that need a single lane, and vehicles or monsters, which have no Hidden to lose.
entries.unit_types: Any ranged unit (visibility is checked per firing model)
entries.move_type: Normal (3″ or less to keep [HEAVY], see OFF-06)
entries.rules_basis: 13.10 Obscuring, excluding areas that either model is within (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2305-2311). 13.11 Solid: no line of sight through enclosed gaps 3″ or less from ground level (:2313-2316; example :2361-2378). 06.01 model and unit visibility (:1080-1099). 04.02: the target must be visible to the firing model (:637-639).

entries.name: Close inside detection range to unmask Hidden or Lone Operative targets
entries.description: A Hidden model is INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM in a terrain area with dense terrain whose unit has not shot this turn or last. It is only visible to enemy models within its detection range: 15″, reduced in the engine by 3″ (floor 9″) when a dense/Solid feature obscures it from that observer (Gone to Ground). A Lone Operative is only visible within 12″ (or X″) and cannot be targeted by [INDIRECT FIRE] from farther away. Move enough shooters inside that radius, on a line that avoids dense terrain so the full 15″ applies, accepting that the unit is now in the target's reach too. Timing: an enemy in dense terrain that fired last turn but not this turn will be Hidden again in its own next turn, so shoot it now (F003). Units with hidden-target buffs (Kommandos Nowhere to Hide, Venator Omni-auspex) gain the most. [INDIRECT FIRE] can target unseen Hidden units without closing, with the 10.07 penalties.
entries.when_to_use: A priority enemy is Hidden (often on a terrain objective) or is a Lone Operative, our shooters' range covers the gap, they can survive at 15″/12″ or less, and there is no indirect option.
entries.unit_types: Short- and mid-range shooters; durable or fast shooters; units with detection-range boosts
entries.rules_basis: 13.09 Hidden, with a 15″ detection range 'unless otherwise stated' (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2292-2303; example :2346-2357). 24.24 Lone Operative X″ (:3813-3830). 10.07: [INDIRECT FIRE] weapons can target non-visible units (:1562-1563). Gone to Ground (−3″) and the 9″ floor are engine rules taken from the review doc; they are not in the core text (GameConstants.gd:86-95; TerrainManager.gd:1053-1080).

entries.name: Keep [HEAVY] while moving 3″ or less
entries.description: In 11e, [HEAVY] gives +1 to hit in your Shooting phase if the unit is unengaged, was not set up this turn, and no model moved more than 3″ this turn; vertical distance counts toward that. So a heavy-weapon unit can step up to 3″ to gain line of sight, enter cover or a terrain area, reach objective range or clear a lane, and keep the bonus. Any model moving more than 3″ loses it, and arriving from reserves or disembarking (both are set-ups) loses it for that turn. The same 3″ envelope applies to rules that grant [Heavy] (Gunnery Honours) or that require a limited move (the chapter-only Ceramite Sentinels 'entrenched': 3″ or less, inside a terrain area).
entries.when_to_use: A [HEAVY] unit has targets in range and a step of 3″ or less improves LoS, cover or objective presence, or an objective move has to be weighed against losing +1 to hit. Does not apply to Overwatch, since the bonus is Shooting-phase only.
entries.unit_types: Units with [HEAVY] weapons (heavy-weapon squads, artillery, tanks); vehicles with Gunnery Honours
entries.move_type: Normal (3″ or less for every model) or Remain Stationary
entries.rules_basis: 24.16 [HEAVY] (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3759-3768). 13.06: distance moved vertically is added to the distance moved (:2192-2194). Disembark and ingress are set-ups (18.04 EFFECT :3027; 20.04 EFFECT :3262). entries.name: Remain stationary to arm Indirect Fire and other stationary-gated shooting
entries.description: [INDIRECT FIRE] attacks fail on an unmodified 1-5. They fail only on 1-3 if the firing unit remained stationary this turn AND one or more friendly units can see the target. The target also gets cover, and hit rolls cannot be re-rolled. So indirect units should Remain Stationary on every turn they rely on indirect fire, ideally out of sight, and pair with a spotter (OFF-19); even a 1″ move drops them back to 6s. The same strict 'remained stationary' gate arms datasheet buffs such as Powerful Volley (Rapier Carrier: [HEAVY] attacks also gain [LETHAL HITS]) and Atomantic Arc-reactor (Cerberus).
entries.when_to_use: The unit's best damage this turn is indirect (or stationary-gated), and a friendly unit already sees the target or can be moved to see it. Units with both direct and indirect weapons choose each turn.
entries.unit_types: [INDIRECT FIRE] units (artillery, mortars); Rapier Carrier; Cerberus
entries.rules_basis: 10.07 Indirect shooting (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1549-1574). 09.04 Remain Stationary (:1378-1387). 24.19 [INDIRECT FIRE] (:3796-3805). 24.24: a Lone Operative can only be indirect-targeted from within X″ (:3818-3822). Engine: RulesEngine._indirect_hit_fail_band_11e (RulesEngine.gd:6594-6605). Powerful Volley: .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:87.

If the unit's best expected damage is indirect, prefer REMAIN_STATIONARY and value it by whether a friendly unit sees the best target, or can be made to see it via OFF-19.

entries.name: Close to a bonus range band (half range, datasheet bands)
entries.description: Move so the target is inside a distance band that boosts the attack in the Select Targets step. Core bands: half range for [RAPID FIRE X] (+X attacks) and [MELTA X] (+X damage). Datasheet bands: Fury of the First 9″ +1 AP, Close-quarters Firestorm 9″ +1 S, Fury of the Machine Spirit 12″ [LETHAL HITS], Priority Target Acquisition 12″ +1 S, Ballistus Strike 24″ [SUSTAINED HITS 1], Tempered Ferocity 6″, GLOWIN' DAKKA 9″ +1 AP, TIP OF THE TALON 9″ +1 S. Use effective range (Dakka! Dakka! Dakka! +3″, Targetin' Squigs +3″, Thunderous Force +6″, Salvus +6″). Skip the half-range approach for Tacticus units under Codex Fire-patterns, whose [RAPID FIRE] works out to maximum range.
entries.when_to_use: The band is reachable this turn without walking into a worse threat, and the bonus applies to the unit's main weapons (especially melta against vehicles and monsters). Pick the tightest band that pays.
entries.unit_types: [RAPID FIRE]/[MELTA] units; Terminator Squads, Aggressors, Land Raider Crusader/Redeemer, Gladiator Valiant, Ballistus Dreadnought, Wolf Guard Battle Leader, Shoota Boyz, Aquilan Shield Custodes
entries.rules_basis: 24.30 [RAPID FIRE X] (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3903-3908). 24.25 [MELTA X] (:3837-3844). Half range is judged in the Select Targets step. entries.name: Stage within reach of several charge targets
entries.description: In 11e you declare the charge, roll 2D6 and only then pick targets, each of which must be within 12″ and within the roll; you can also decline after a bad roll. So end the move with two or more acceptable targets at staggered distances, a near, safe option and a far, high-value one, so that most rolls produce a useful charge.
entries.when_to_use: A melee unit approaches a cluster where the preferred target is at a low-probability distance and an acceptable nearer target exists, or where a failed charge would strand the unit.
entries.unit_types: Melee units
entries.rules_basis: 11.02 steps 2-3: the roll comes first, then the charge is attempted 'if it is possible ... and if you still want to' (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1624-1629). 11.04 BEFORE MOVING: targets are selected after the roll (:1647-1650). Worked example (:1669-1702).

entries.coverage_detail: charge_intent keeps one best target per unit (AIDecisionMaker.gd:3834-3906) and the steer aims only at that target (7503-7548). The chase gate picks the single nearest enemy (2951). Choosing targets after the roll is modelled only at declaration in the Charge phase (_evaluate_multi_target_charge 18973-19130), after positions are already fixed.
entries.engine_support: Reuse _charge_success_probability (18928) per target gap and the roll-EV maths in _evaluate_multi_target_charge (18973). New: a 'charge option value' at each candidate endpoint, Σ over rolls r of P(r) × max(EV of the target sets reachable with r), so staging maximizes expected value across all rolls rather than the odds against a single target.
entries.value_reason: 11e's roll-first targeting makes this a free gain in charge reliability, but it needs several targets close together.

entries.name: Approach the charge target on a clean lane
entries.description: Stage so that the charge path to the intended target neither passes through enemy bases nor ends within 2″ of an enemy unit that is not a target. Screens and neighbouring units otherwise force a failed charge or an unwanted multi-target one. Every charging model must also end closer to a target, and those that can get within 1″ must. Account for climbing on the path: non-INFANTRY models cannot cross dense sections taller than 2″. FLY units can take to the skies over blockers (OFF-27).
entries.when_to_use: Crowded fronts, screened targets, or ruins between the charger and the target.
entries.unit_types: Melee units, especially non-INFANTRY near dense terrain
entries.rules_basis: 11.04 WHILE and AFTER MOVING (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1652-1663). 03.01: bases cannot be moved through enemy models (:393). 17.01: MONSTER/VEHICLE move-through applies to normal and advance moves only (:2871-2874). 13.06 dense terrain (:2167-2182). 11.04 example of a target that cannot be engaged around terrain (:1669-1682).

entries.coverage_detail: Path terrain is considered only when ranking the nearest target: _get_nearest_enemy_for_charge adds _estimate_charge_terrain_penalty to the distance (AIDecisionMaker.gd:3134-3136). Moves aim at the target's centroid (7228-7272, 7503-7548). Nothing checks for enemy bases in the way or for non-target units within 2″ of the likely charge end. _find_flank_around_terrain (3153-3190), which builds a waypoint around terrain blocking a charge path, has no callers.
entries.engine_support: Reuse the ChargeMove11e after-moving conditions, TerrainManager.calculate_charge_terrain_penalty (TerrainManager.gd:509), the unused _find_flank_around_terrain (AIDecisionMaker.gd:3153), and _compute_charge_move (19797) to simulate the charge end from a probe start. New: a lane check that rejects or penalizes endpoints whose minimal engaging placement touches a non-target unit or crosses enemy bases.
entries.value_reason: A charge that touches a stray unit fails outright, and 11e's 2″ engagement range widens the danger zone. Matters most on crowded boards.
entries.errata_note: Taking to the skies must be declared before the charge roll and (unless the unit has HOVER) subtracts 2″ from the maximum distance used to pick charge targets (a roll of 9 only reaches targets within 7″), so a flier relying on it to clear a screen must stage about 2″ closer. Friendly units do not block the lane: in a charge every model, MONSTER/VEHICLE included, can move through friendly models. — FAQ 21.03 Flying Models; FAQ 02.02 Profiles (charge-roll modifiers / Take to the Skies); FAQ 17.01 Moving Monsters and Vehicles

entries.name: Advance and still shoot with [ASSAULT] weapons
entries.description: Advance (M + D6) when the extra inches are needed for range or LoS on a target, for an objective or for a Hidden spot, and then fire only the [ASSAULT] weapons using assault shooting. The cost: no charge, no actions, no [HEAVY] bonus (a model moved more than 3″), and no EXPLOSIVES this turn. The same applies when a rule grants [ASSAULT]: Orks riled up, Dakka! Dakka! Dakka!, Devastator Doctrine, Adrenaline Junkies, Wind Walker, and post-advance Custodes stratagems.
entries.when_to_use: The target or objective is just beyond a Normal move, the unit's damage is in its [ASSAULT] weapons, and it will not charge or start an action this turn.
entries.unit_types: Units with [ASSAULT] weapons; riled-up Orks; Shoota Boyz; Adeptus Astartes under Devastator Doctrine
entries.rules_basis: 10.05 Assault shooting (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1506-1518). 09.06: after an Advance, no charge or actions until end of turn (:1401-1414). 24.04 [ASSAULT] (:3617-3624). 16.01 (:2816). 15.05 requires the unit not to have advanced (:2659-2662). entries.name: Approach the enemy units your mission cards pay for
entries.description: Many 11e cards pay for killing particular enemy units, scored at the end of either player's turn. Assassination pays per CHARACTER model (3VP, +1 if W4+; tactical 5VP). Bring It Down pays per W10+ model (4VP). A Grievous Blow pays for units with Starting Strength 13+. No Prisoners pays 2VP per unit. Overwhelming Force pays 3VP per unit that STARTED the turn within range of an objective (max 5). Primaries pay for victims that started the turn on objectives (Purge and Secure 3VP), on a CENTRAL objective (Secure Asset), or inside terrain (Search and Scour), and for Condemned units (Punishment: 5VP each, condemned at the start of your turn mostly from units on objectives). Snapshot the qualifying enemies at the start of the turn and move shooters and chargers into range, LoS or charge reach of them, inside detection range if they are Hidden (OFF-04). The kill still counts if the victim has moved off the objective.
entries.when_to_use: Such a card is active and a qualifying target can be killed this turn (or next).
entries.unit_types: Damage dealers matched to the target profile (anti-tank for W10+, precision for characters, volume for 13+ hordes)
entries.rules_basis: 40k/data/40kdc/missionCards.json awards: purge-and-secure (:232; destroyer_on_objective / victim_started_turn_on_objective, exclusive_group purge-kill), punishment (condemned left-battlefield, either player's turn, 5VP), assassination (3VP per CHARACTER model, +1 if W4+), bring-it-down (4VP per W10+ model), overwhelming-force (3VP per unit that started within range of an objective, max 5). All five were read and checked. Engine auto-condemns enemy units in range of objectives: MissionManager.gd:1754-1795.

entries.name: Hunt enemy characters (make the CHARACTER model visible or reachable)
entries.description: Position [PRECISION] shooters so that a CHARACTER model in the target unit is itself visible to at least one attacking model: Precision can only promote the allocation group of a visible CHARACTER. Separately, move a CHARACTER that can use EPIC CHALLENGE (1CP: its melee weapons gain [PRECISION]) into charge reach of an attached leader, ideally after the bodyguard has been battle-shocked or thinned. Killing characters strips auras and leader buffs and scores Assassination.
entries.when_to_use: An enemy leader provides key buffs, Assassination is active or the unit carries the HUNT_CHARACTERS plan verb, and a precision attacker can reach.
entries.unit_types: [PRECISION] units, snipers, CHARACTERs able to use Epic Challenge, Wolf Guard Headtakers (precision against their quarry)

entries.name: Set up a multi-unit charge
entries.description: Deliberately bring a second (or third) enemy unit inside the likely roll so one charge can select and engage several targets. The charge must end engaged with all of them and with no other unit. This locks more shooters, uses Fights First on more targets, and makes falling back harder (the Death Guard style).
entries.when_to_use: Two adjacent enemy units are both worth locking, the charging unit is durable, and the end positions can engage every target.
entries.unit_types: Large-footprint melee mobs, monsters, Death Guard-style lock armies

entries.name: Flank to strip the target's cover
entries.description: Cover is judged per attacking model. A target has it only if EVERY one of its models either is INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM within a terrain area, or is not fully visible to that attacking model because of intervening terrain. Against vehicles, monsters and mounted units, and against infantry outside terrain areas, move firing models to angles where at least one target model is fully visible, denying the −1 BS. Infantry inside a terrain area keep cover from every angle, so use [IGNORES COVER], [TORRENT] (auto-hits) or Plunging Fire against them instead. Cross-fire from two directions defeats a single piece of terrain.
entries.when_to_use: High-BS shooters face a partly obscured priority VEHICLE/MONSTER and have movement to spare after reaching range.
entries.unit_types: Mobile shooters
entries.rules_basis: 13.08 Benefit of Cover (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2278-2290). 06.01 'fully visible' (:1087-1093). 24.18 [IGNORES COVER] (:3783-3793). 24.37 [TORRENT] automatically hits (:3943-3950). 22.05 (:3453-3462).

entries.name: Spot for the gunline
entries.description: Move one unit so it enables OTHER units' shots. (a) Give a stationary [INDIRECT FIRE] battery a friendly unit that can see its target, which raises its hits from 6s to 4+. (b) Bring a detection-range raiser within its ability's range of a Hidden enemy so the gunline 12-15″ away can target it. Raisers: Kommandos Found 'Em! (Movement phase, within 12″, +3″), Infiltrator Omni-scramblers (18″, +3″), Prosecutors Purity of Execution (18″, +3″), Eliminators Special-issue Optics (24″, +6″), Stormlance Auspex Triangulation Shrines (12″, +3″), Lieutenant Priority Target Identified. The spotter has to move before the shooters do.
entries.when_to_use: An indirect battery is holding still (OFF-07) and nothing sees its best target, or a priority enemy is Hidden beyond the gunline's detection reach.
entries.unit_types: Any cheap or fast unit as a LoS spotter; Kommandos, Infiltrator Squad, Prosecutors, Eliminators, Stormlance speeders, Lieutenant with Combi-weapon

entries.name: Strike first: charge the enemy melee threat before it charges you
entries.description: If an enemy melee unit will reach us next turn anyway, move in and charge it now. Every model in a unit that made a charge move has Fights First until the end of the turn, and Fights First units fight before all others. Waiting means being charged and struck first instead.
entries.when_to_use: Melee-against-melee standoffs where both sides are inside each other's next-turn reach and our unit wins, or trades well, when it strikes first.
entries.unit_types: Melee units
entries.rules_basis: 11.04 AFTER MOVING: Fights First until end of turn (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1664-1665). 24.13 Fights First (:3736-3745). Fights First units must be selected to fight before other units (:1885-1886). 12.04 (:1819-1850).

entries.name: Advance into charge range when a rule allows advance-and-charge
entries.description: An 11e Advance forbids charging 'unless otherwise stated'. With a granting rule the unit can Advance M + D6 and still charge. Grants include Orks riled up (Waaagh!, Da Boss is Watchin', Keep Huntin'! ...), Adrenaline Junkies, Assault Doctrine, Berserk Charge, Spear of Chogoris, Sally Forth, and post-advance Custodes stratagems (UNLIMITED ENDURANCE and others). Use it to reach charge range from farther away, and time the Waaagh! so several units benefit at once.
entries.when_to_use: The target is beyond a Normal move plus a likely charge but within an Advance plus a likely charge, and the grant is active or affordable.
entries.unit_types: Orks (riled up), Speed Freeks, Adeptus Astartes under Assault Doctrine, Blood Claws, Custodes infantry

entries.name: Line up a Crushing Impact charge
entries.description: Just after a MONSTER/VEHICLE unit ends a charge move, the 1CP Crushing Impact stratagem rolls D6 equal to one engaged model's T. Each 5+ inflicts a mortal wound on the engaged enemy unit (max 6), and each 1 inflicts one on your own unit. Move a high-T model into charge reach of low-T, wounded or cheap targets such as screens, objective holders or characters. If the target dies, the charger can still pile in (it made a charge move) and make an overrun fight.
entries.when_to_use: A high-T MONSTER/VEHICLE is near light infantry or a wounded character, CP is available, and it has nothing better to shoot.
entries.unit_types: MONSTER, VEHICLE
entries.rules_basis: 15.06 Crushing Impact (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2673-2696). 12.03: a unit that made a charge move is eligible to pile in, even if unengaged (:1740-1753). 12.06 Overrun fight (:1866-1877). Worked example (:1772-1781).

entries.name: Fall back to re-charge or shoot when a rule allows it
entries.description: 11e Fall Back normally forbids shooting, charging and actions. With a granting rule it becomes a tactical reset: leave a grinding or losing combat and re-charge a better target, or the same one, to regain Fights First and on-charge bonuses (Lance, Hammer of Wrath, Crushing Impact and similar), or fall back and shoot. Granting rules include Tactical Doctrine (shoot and charge), Suspiciously Well Organised (Boyz/Kommandos/Stormboyz: charge), Adrenaline Junkies, Talon Sortie and MANOEUVRE AND FIRE. Ordered Retreat is only available to units that are not battle-shocked; Desperate Escape forces hazard rolls and a battle-shock roll.
entries.when_to_use: The unit is engaged with something the fight will not kill or is not worth it, a better target is within charge reach after the fall-back, and the on-charge payoff outweighs staying.
entries.unit_types: Adeptus Astartes under Tactical Doctrine, Boyz/Kommandos/Stormboyz (Taktikal Brigade), Speed Freeks, Custodes (Solar Watch)
entries.rules_basis: 09.07: no shooting, charging or actions 'unless otherwise stated'; Ordered Retreat and Desperate Escape modes (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1417-1441). Tactical Doctrine (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/RULES.md:234-235). Suspiciously Well Organised (orks/RULES.md:184). 11.04 Fights First (:1664-1665).

entries.name: Climb for Plunging Fire, or bring a TOWERING model within 12″
entries.description: Ranged attacks against a visible unit with models on ground level get +1 BS if the attacking model is on a terrain section 3″ or more high, or if it is TOWERING and the target is within 12″. Only INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM/FLY/MONSTER models may end a move on upper levels. Climbing distance counts toward the move, and models must stay within ½″ of the feature while climbing. The +1 offsets the −1 BS from the target's cover. Plunging Fire has no effect on attacks by or against AIRCRAFT.
entries.when_to_use: Shooters next to tall ruins facing ground-level targets in cover (a climb of 3″ or less also keeps [HEAVY]), or TOWERING models closing to 12″.
entries.unit_types: INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM/FLY/MONSTER climbers; TOWERING models (e.g. the Stompa in armies/recon_stomps.json)
entries.rules_basis: 22.05 Plunging Fire (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3453-3462). 13.06 moving vertically and ending a move on non-ground surfaces (:2184-2208). 23.03: Plunging Fire has no effect by or against AIRCRAFT (:3522). 13.08: cover worsens BS by 1 (:2289-2290). Correction: core-rules#30 and web#20 say Plunging Fire 'cancels' cover. It does not remove cover; its +1 BS offsets cover's −1 BS, so 'cancels' is only true of the net hit roll.
