entries.name: Hold objectives through the opponent's turn for your next Command-phase score
entries.description: From round 2 most 11e primaries pay at the end of YOUR Command phase: Battlefield Dominance 3VP per objective, Immovable Object 5VP per non-home objective (R2-4), Purge and Secure / Unstoppable Force / Search and Scour 4VP per non-home objective, Outmanoeuvre 5VP per non-home objective (R2-3), and a flat 4VP for holding 1+ non-home objective on most other cards. Burden of Trust and Defend Stronghold score at the end of the opponent's turn. Control is re-totalled after the opponent's whole turn and after your own battle-shock step, which runs before mission scoring. So the move that scores is made the turn before. Leave a holder in place (Remain Stationary, or a short move that keeps a model in range) that will still control the objective at that check: durable, out of enemy reach and line of sight where possible, with an OC margin over what the enemy can bring in one move, and not at or below half strength (it must pass a battle-shock roll first). Do not move or redeploy a scoring unit off the objective during this window.
entries.when_to_use: Rounds 1-4, for every objective your next Command-phase rows pay for (round-1 positions set up the round-2 score). Also at the end of your turn whenever Burden of Trust or Defend Stronghold (R2+) is active. Not round 5, where Command rows score at the end of your own turn (see OBJ-04).
entries.unit_types: Durable OC holders: Battleline, high-OC vehicles and monsters, full-strength squads, units inside Ld/OC auras. Avoid units at or below half strength.
entries.move_type: Remain Stationary (or a short Normal Move that keeps a model in range)
entries.rules_basis: 14.02: control is determined at the end of each phase and turn from summed OC, and a tie leaves the objective uncontrolled (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2401-2419). 08.03: the battle-shock step rolls for units at or below half-strength (:1242-1255), before 08.05 mission scoring (:1264-1275). 01.07: battle-shocked models have OC '-' (:216-217). 09.04 Remain Stationary (:1378-1388). GDM timing key 'C = your Command phase (switches to end of turn in Round 5)' (11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:7). missionCards.json Command rows {end-of-phase, command, battle_round min 2} (battlefield-dominance :3, immovable-object :108, outmanoeuvre :854) and end-of-opponent's-turn rows (burden-of-trust :2225, defend-stronghold :2706).

'Threatened' means any enemy unit within 12in (9170-9175). A hold always executes as REMAIN_STATIONARY (7187-7200), so the AI never looks for a safer spot within range (see OBJ-06). A battle-shocked holder can still be picked as keeper, because candidate unit_oc comes from _unit_alive_oc (13432-13439).

entries.name: Take an objective: move enough OC into its range
entries.description: Normal Move (or Advance if the D6 is needed to arrive) so enough models end within range to beat the enemy's level of control at the next end-of-phase or end-of-turn check. On 11e terrain objectives the terrain area IS the objective. A model is in range while any part of its base is within the area, so a vehicle only needs to touch it. Where a layout has no area, a model is in range within 3in horizontally and 5in vertically of the 40mm marker. Infantry that end inside the area also gain cover, and Hidden if the area contains dense terrain.
entries.when_to_use: Uncontrolled or weakly held objectives that your primary or secondary cards pay for. Adding a second OC source to win a contest is OBJ-05.
entries.unit_types: Any unit with OC 1+ that is not battle-shocked.
entries.rules_basis: 14.01: the terrain area is the objective; measure to its closest part (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2389-2398). 14.02: a model is within range of a terrain objective while it is within that area (:2405-2406); control is summed at the end of each phase and turn (:2409-2416). 01.04: measure from the closest part of the base (:163-166). Rules appendix: objective markers, 3in horizontally / 5in vertically (:4085-4103). 13.08 / 13.09: cover and Hidden for INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM within a terrain area (:2279-2303). 09.05 / 09.06 (:1390-1414).

entries.name: Contest an enemy-held objective to deny their next score and break their majority
entries.description: When you cannot out-OC the holder, move just enough OC into range to TIE their level of control. A tie leaves the objective uncontrolled (unless they secured it). That removes it from their next Command-phase rows (per-objective, hold 1+ and threshold) and from their count for majority rows (Battlefield Dominance, Inescapable Dominion, Punishment, Consecrate, Destroyer's Wrath, Surveil the Foe). With more OC you flip it outright. Between the end of your turn and their scoring, only their Command phase happens: their own battle-shock rolls and Command-phase abilities. So an end-of-your-turn contest in rounds 1-4 almost certainly denies that score. Expendable units are fine here: the VP denied outweighs the unit.
entries.when_to_use: The opponent holds a non-secured objective that their card pays for at their next Command phase, and you can bring equal OC. Majority rows are tied or within one. Your turns in rounds 1-4. From the opponent's round-5 turn, their Command rows score at the end of THEIR turn, so a contest must then survive their whole turn, unless it is made in the last turn of the game (OBJ-04).
entries.unit_types: Any unit with OC 1+ that is not battle-shocked: cheap fast units, deep strikers, multi-model infantry.
entries.move_type: Normal Move / Advance (also via Deep Strike or Rapid Ingress arrivals)
entries.rules_basis: 14.02: a tie means not controlled unless secured (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2417-2419). 14.03: a secured objective needs strictly greater control to flip (:2427-2435). 08.03: only the active player's units take battle-shock rolls (:1242-1251); 08.05 scoring follows (:1264-1275). 07.02: the same player takes the first turn every round (:1135-1139). GDM timing key (11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:7); 11th_edition_doc_change_audit.md:197 applies the round-5 switch to both players. missionCards.json 'objective-majority' rows: battlefield-dominance :3, inescapable-dominion :159, punishment :371, destroyers-wrath :560, consecrate :646, surveil-the-foe :1757.

entries.name: Go all-in on objectives in the final round
entries.description: In round 5 the Command-phase rows score at the end of your own turn, so survival no longer matters for them. Drop exposure and Hidden preferences. Advance freely, since it only costs this turn's charge and actions. Charge or consolidate onto objectives, contest every enemy objective you can reach, and pour units into the end-of-battle bonus areas: enemy home 5/8/10VP, central 5VP, hold 4+ objectives 10VP, no enemy wholly in your territory 5VP, 4+ decoyed objectives 10VP. Turn order matters. The second player's round-5 turn is the last of the game, so nothing it takes or contests can be retaken, and that includes contesting the opponent's end-of-battle objectives. The first player's end-of-battle holdings must still survive the opponent's last turn.
entries.when_to_use: Battle round 5 (plan it from late round 4). Price it differently for the first and the second player.
entries.unit_types: Every unit, including characters, vehicles and units normally kept back.
entries.rules_basis: GDM timing key: 'C ... switches to end of turn in Round 5' (11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:7); 11th_edition_doc_change_audit.md:197 applies it to both players. missionCards.json: battlefield-dominance text ('or end of your turn in the fifth battle round', :3); immovable-object round-5 end-of-turn row (:108); end-of-battle rows (unstoppable-force :302, inescapable-dominion :159, punishment :371, vital-link :1412, vanguard-operation :1597, triangulation :1874, search-and-scour :2005, smoke-and-mirrors :1100). 07.02: the same player goes first every round (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1135-1139). 09.06: an Advance only bars charges and actions (:1401-1414).

entries.name: Reinforce a contested or threatened objective to win the OC count
entries.description: Move a second OC source onto an objective you hold or contest when the enemy could match or beat your level of control at the next check. Three cases: enemy OC is already in range; enemy OC is one move away; or the holder is at or below half strength and must pass a battle-shock roll in your Command phase before scoring (failing makes its OC '-'). Count only models that are not battle-shocked.
entries.when_to_use: Contested objectives; held objectives with enemy OC in range or one move away; a lone half-strength holder before your next Command phase; an objective that decides a majority or threshold row.
entries.unit_types: Any unit with OC 1+ that is not battle-shocked; high-OC multi-model infantry.
entries.rules_basis: 14.02: the highest summed OC of models in range controls (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2409-2416). 01.07: battle-shocked models have OC '-' (:216-217). 08.03: units at or below half-strength roll in your Command phase (:1242-1255), before 08.05 mission scoring (:1264-1275).

entries.name: Move into cover on the objective: hold from a Hidden or obscured spot inside its terrain area
entries.description: Because the terrain area IS the objective, holders need not stand in the open part of it. A holding unit whose models are all INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM within the area has the benefit of cover: attacks against it worsen BS by 1. In an area with dense terrain, its models are Hidden (visible only to enemies within 15in) while the unit has not shot this turn or last. Behind Solid walls, or across obscuring areas, they can be out of line of sight entirely. Shuffle the holders to the spots in the area that are Hidden or out of sight of the main shooters and away from the side the enemy will charge from, keeping the OC needed in range. Use a short Normal Move, or no more than 3in so [HEAVY] still applies. This is the objective form of the user's 'move into cover'.
entries.when_to_use: Holding against shooting armies; the objective area contains dense or light features or Solid walls; the holders are INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM; the holder can skip shooting (for Hidden) or only needs cover; the opponent is paid for kills on objectives.
entries.unit_types: INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM objective holders (vehicles and monsters use OBJ-15 instead).
entries.move_type: Normal Move (short reposition within range) / Remain Stationary
entries.rules_basis: 14.02: within range while within the area (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2405-2406). 13.08: benefit of cover when every model is INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM within a terrain area or not fully visible; BS worsened by 1 (:2279-2290). 13.09 Hidden: inside an area with dense terrain, no ranged attacks this turn or the previous turn, 15in detection range (:2292-2303). 13.10 obscuring (:2305-2310). 13.11 Solid (:2313-2315). 24.16 [HEAVY]: +1 to hit if no model moved more than 3in (:3751-3768).

entries.name: Flip an objective you did not control at the start of your turn
entries.description: Determined Acquisition pays 2VP at the end of your turn for every objective you newly controlled this turn, in every round. Purge and Secure and Unstoppable Force pay 3VP at the end of your turn, from round 2, for taking a non-home objective you did not control at the start of the turn. Control at the start of the turn is recorded, so every uncontrolled, contested or enemy-held objective is a target. Movement comes before Shooting and Fight, so the plan can be: move enough OC into range now, then remove the enemy OC with shooting, charges, fights or battle-shock before the end of the turn (OBJ-09, OBJ-10). Deep strike or ingress onto an uncontested objective also counts. Prefer such flips to sitting on objectives you already hold.
entries.when_to_use: One of those cards is active and at least one objective was not yours at the start of the turn. Prefer objectives where your OC after shooting will exceed theirs.
entries.unit_types: Fast OC units, melee units that charge onto the objective, deep strikers, ranged units that clear holders first.
entries.rules_basis: missionCards.json determined-acquisition: 'objective-newly-controlled-this-turn', 2VP at the end of your turn, every round, with no home exclusion (:63). The GDM summary row says 'excl. home', but neither the official dataset nor the engine excludes it (PrimaryMissionData11e.gd:142). purge-and-secure (:232) and unstoppable-force (:302): 'new-objective-controlled', 3VP from R2 (non-home in the engine: PrimaryMissionData11e.gd:124, :157). 14.02: control at the end of the turn (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2409-2416). Start-of-turn control is recorded at MissionManager.gd:1726-1731.

entries.name: Grab an objective for this turn's end-of-turn award even if you will lose it
entries.description:
End-of-turn rows pay for control at the end of YOUR turn, so a capture scores even if the opponent retakes it next turn. Commit expendable or exposed units to these:
- Battlefield Dominance: majority, 2VP (R1-2).
- Immovable Object: central, 3VP every turn.
- Inescapable Dominion: 4VP for 3+ objectives.
- Determined Acquisition: 2VP per new objective.
- Outmanoeuvre: 4VP per non-home objective (R1), 6VP per non-home objective (R4+), 10VP for the enemy home in any turn.
- Meatgrinder: enemy home, 5VP (R2+).
- Gather Intel: central, 6VP (R1).
- Search and Scour: central, 3VP.
- Vital Link: central, 2VP plus markers.
- Delaying Action: central plus an expansion objective, 3VP (R2+).
- Secondaries: Forward Position, Secure No Man's Land and A Tempting Target, 5VP each.
Count the OC that charges and Objective Consolidation will add before the end of the turn.
entries.when_to_use: Inside those round windows, especially when the objective cannot realistically be held through the enemy turn. Prefer this over holding back when the row pays at end of turn rather than in the Command phase.
entries.unit_types: Fast or expendable OC units, melee units charging onto the objective, deep strikers.
entries.rules_basis: 14.02: control is determined at the end of the turn (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2409-2416). missionCards.json end-of-turn rows for your turn: battlefield-dominance :3, immovable-object :108, inescapable-dominion :159, determined-acquisition :63, outmanoeuvre :854, meatgrinder :474, gather-intel :2071, search-and-scour :2005, vital-link :1412, delaying-action :916, forward-position :2181, secure-no-mans-land :2489, a-tempting-target :2759. entries.name: Move toward the enemy objective holder to shoot it off before the control check
entries.description: To flip or contest an objective, the enemy OC in range has to go. Move a shooting unit to where it can see and reach the enemy unit(s) standing in the objective's area, and into half range for Rapid Fire / Melta when that matters. This turn's shooting then destroys or battle-shocks enough of them before the end-of-turn check while your OC unit steps in. Choose firing spots that see past the area's obscuring and Solid terrain; a Hidden holder can only be seen from within its detection range (15in). This is the objective form of the user's 'move toward an enemy to shoot it'.
entries.when_to_use: An enemy unit holds or contests an objective you want this turn (flip, contest, new-capture or end-of-turn rows) and its OC exceeds what you can bring. Your shooters cannot currently see or reach it. Late rounds.
entries.unit_types: Ranged units, especially high-volume or anti-infantry guns against multi-model holders, and [IGNORES COVER] or anti-Hidden tools.
entries.rules_basis: 14.02: control at the end of each phase and turn (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2409-2416). 10.04: normal shooting requires no advance (:1489-1491). 10.05: assault shooting after an advance uses [ASSAULT] weapons only (:1506-1516). 13.08: cover worsens BS by 1 (:2279-2290). 13.09: Hidden models are visible only within detection range (:2292-2303). 13.10 / 13.11 line of sight (:2305-2315). 01.07: battle-shocked models have OC '-' (:216-217).

entries.name: Move toward the enemy objective holder to charge it off the objective
entries.description: Use a Normal Move to close to reliable charge distance of the enemy unit holding the objective (a charge needs an enemy within 12in and a 2D6 roll). Don't Advance: that forbids the charge unless an ability allows it. Each step then works on the objective. The charge move often ends your models inside the area. The fight destroys or ties up the holder. If no enemy is left within 3in, Objective Consolidation can add more models before the end-of-turn check. Approach from cover and out of Overwatch sight where possible. This is the objective form of the user's 'move toward an enemy to charge it'.
entries.when_to_use: A melee unit can reach charge range of an objective holder this turn; flip, contest, new-capture or end-of-turn rows are active; holders are weak in melee; late rounds.
entries.unit_types: Melee units; advance-and-charge units (riled-up Orks, etc.).
entries.move_type: Normal Move (Advance only with an advance-and-charge ability)
entries.rules_basis: 11.02: declaring a charge needs an enemy within 12in and no advance or fall back this turn (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1603-1625, :1620, :1622). 09.06 (:1411-1414). 12.08: Objective Consolidation applies when the unit is not engaged and not within 3in of enemies but is within 3in of an objective; moved models end within range if possible (:1942-1975). 14.02 (:2409-2416). 15.08: Fire Overwatch at the end of the opponent's Movement phase (:2735-2742).

entries.name: Garrison your home objective with the cheapest sufficient OC unit and push only part of the army
entries.description: Your home objective matters in several ways. It enables Battlefield Dominance's +2VP per non-home objective (only while you hold home). It scores Defend Stronghold (3VP at the end of the opponent's turn, R2+). It counts toward thresholds that don't exclude home (Inescapable Dominion, Secure Asset 3+, Triangulation 4+). And losing it feeds the opponent's enemy-home rows (up to 10VP). Keep a cheap OC unit in range of it, ideally Hidden in its area, and send the expensive units forward. Commit only part of the army to the forward objectives instead of pushing everything.
entries.when_to_use: Always, while a home-dependent row is active for you or the opponent's card pays for your home. Give it more weight against deep strikers, Scouts and Infiltrators.
entries.unit_types: Cheapest OC units (Gretchin-class job units, small Battleline squads) as the garrison; bricks push forward.
entries.rules_basis: missionCards.json: the battlefield-dominance cumulative row requires controlling your home objective (:3); defend-stronghold pays for your home at the end of the opponent's turn, R2+ (:2706); opponent-home rows (outmanoeuvre :854, vital-link :1412, punishment :371, vanguard-operation :1597). 14.02 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2409-2419).

entries.name: Take and keep the central objective
entries.description:
Every shipped 11e layout has one central objective at the board centre, built from two linked terrain areas that count as one objective (a model in either area is in range). It pays on many cards:
- Immovable Object: 3VP at the end of every turn.
- Unstoppable Force: 5VP at the end of the battle.
- Gather Intel: 6VP at the end of R1.
- Search and Scour: 3VP at the end of every turn.
- Vital Link: 2VP plus 1VP per marker at end of turn, and +4VP at Command.
- Delaying Action: together with an expansion objective.
It is also where the Sensor Sweep (Extract Relic) and Maintain Control (Vital Link) actions start. Put a durable high-OC unit into either half early, and keep a second body there so an action unit can work.
entries.when_to_use: Any of those cards is active; R1 for Gather Intel; every turn for Immovable Object and Search and Scour.
entries.unit_types: Tanky high-OC units, plus a second body for actions.
entries.rules_basis: 14.01 / 14.02 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2389-2419). Central = the no-man's-land objective nearest the board centre (MissionManager.gd:268-288). missionCards.json central rows: immovable-object :108, unstoppable-force :302, gather-intel :2071, search-and-scour :2005, vital-link :1412, delaying-action :916, extract-relic :1286.

entries.name: Raid the opponent's home objective on the card's timing
entries.description:
Many cards pay for the enemy home:
- Outmanoeuvre: 10VP at the end of ANY of your turns.
- Meatgrinder: 5VP at end of turn from R2.
- Forward Position: 5VP at end of turn.
- Punishment 8VP, Vital Link 10VP, Vanguard Operation 10VP and Inescapable Dominion 5VP at the end of the battle.
- Gather Intel markers there pay at the end of the battle.
Time the raid to the card: for end-of-turn rows, grab it at the end of any turn; for end-of-battle rows, arrive late and survive. Deep Strike can land in the enemy deployment zone from R2 (more than 8in from enemy units). Ordinary strategic-reserve ingress cannot enter it before R3.
entries.when_to_use: One of those cards is active and the enemy home is lightly held or reachable by deep strike or fast units. End-of-battle rows from R4.
entries.unit_types: Deep strikers, fast melee, transports, durable high-OC units.
entries.move_type: Reserves arrival (Deep Strike / ingress) / Advance / Normal Move
entries.rules_basis: 20.03: ingress from R2 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3250-3253). 20.04: no set-up in the opponent's deployment zone before the third round (:3267-3269). 24.09: Deep Strike anywhere more than 8in from enemy units, even in the opponent's deployment zone (:3649-3661). missionCards.json opponent-home rows: outmanoeuvre :854, meatgrinder :474, punishment :371, vital-link :1412, vanguard-operation :1597, inescapable-dominion :159, forward-position :2181, gather-intel :2071.

entries.name: Toe in: put only the models you need into the objective area, from the side away from threats
entries.description: Only models within the area add OC, and a base that only partly overlaps it still counts. Touch the area's edge with just enough models (or a vehicle or monster's hull) to win or tie the count, on the side away from enemy firing and charge lanes. Keep the rest of the unit in coherency behind terrain or outside the area. On open-ground markers, stop at the 3in ring instead of on the marker. Trade-off: an infantry unit only partly inside the area loses the 13.08 'within a terrain area' cover, unless its other models are not fully visible.
entries.when_to_use: Control is needed at the next check but standing inside the area is very exposed; vehicles and monsters that cannot be Hidden; units with surplus OC per model; large areas and the two-area centre.
entries.unit_types: VEHICLE / MONSTER holders; multi-model units with spare OC.
entries.rules_basis: 14.01 / 14.02 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2389-2419); the rules diagram counts a VEHICLE 'within the terrain area' with only part of its hull inside (:2439-2450). 01.04: measure from the closest part of the base (:163-166). Rules appendix: objective markers 3in / 5in (:4085-4103). 03.03: coherency 2in / 9in (:518-530). 13.08: every model must qualify for cover (:2279-2290).

entries.name: Steal an objective held only by battle-shocked enemies
entries.description: Battle-shocked models have OC '-', so an objective held only by shocked units flips to any unshocked unit with OC 1+ that steps into range. No kill is needed. Shock lasts until the owner passes a battle-shock roll in their own Command phase, and that roll comes BEFORE their scoring. So the steal certainly scores your end-of-turn rows. It denies their next Command-phase score if they fail the re-test, or regardless of the re-test if your OC there is at least equal to theirs.
entries.when_to_use: Enemy holders are battle-shocked now (they failed a test, or one of your abilities forced one this turn) and your unit can reach range. Pairs with OBJ-40.
entries.unit_types: Any unshocked unit with OC 1+; cheap fast units.
entries.rules_basis: 01.07: battle-shocked models have OC '-' (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:216-217). 08.03: a shocked unit re-tests in its owner's battle-shock step and recovers only on a pass (:1242-1255). 14.02 (:2409-2416).

entries.name: Take the objective that completes a count threshold, not surplus ones
entries.description:
Threshold rows put all the value on the objective that crosses the line:
- Inescapable Dominion: 4VP at end of turn for 3+, 5VP at Command for 2+.
- Secure Asset: 4VP at Command for 3+.
- Triangulation: 10VP for 4+ at the end of the battle.
- Secure No Man's Land: needs 2 no-man's-land objectives.
- Delaying Action: needs central plus an expansion objective.
- The flat '4VP for 1+ non-home' row on most cards.
Primary VP is also capped at 15 per turn. Send the next free unit to the objective that reaches (or keeps) the threshold rather than reinforcing a surplus one, stop spending units once the tier or the cap is reached, and re-evaluate after each move.
entries.when_to_use: Threshold or flat 'hold 1+' rows are active, and the count is one short of a tier or exactly at it.
entries.unit_types: Any OC unit; send the cheapest to the deciding objective.
entries.rules_basis: missionCards.json count_min rows: inescapable-dominion :159, secure-asset :1189, triangulation :1874, secure-no-mans-land :2489, delaying-action :916. PrimaryMissionData11e.gd:59-60 (MAX_PRIMARY_VP_PER_TURN_11E = 15). 11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:7 (15VP per turn cap).

entries.name: Hand off an objective: move a cheap unit in so an expensive holder can leave
entries.description: Free an expensive or offensive unit sitting on a safe objective. First move a cheap job unit into range, so control still holds at the end of the phase, then move the expensive unit to its real job. With a securing ability, use OBJ-16 instead.
entries.when_to_use: An expensive melee or offensive unit holds a low-threat (often home) objective, a cheap OC unit can reach it this turn, and the freed unit has a valuable target.
entries.unit_types: Expensive melee units leaving; cheap infantry taking over.
entries.rules_basis: 14.02: control at the end of each phase and turn (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2409-2416).

entries.name: Flip an abandoned secured enemy objective
entries.description: An objective the opponent secured stays theirs with nobody in range until your level of control is greater at the end of a phase. So a single OC 1+ model ending its move in an empty enemy-secured area flips it at the end of your Movement phase. From then on it counts for you and against their count. Look for objectives that the opponent's securing units have walked away from.
entries.when_to_use: The opponent has secure abilities (Get da Good Bitz, Thievin' Scavengers, Raise the Banner, DUBIOUS RESTRAINT, IMPENETRABLE BASTION, VIGILANCE ETERNAL, ...) and has left a secured objective; cheap fast units are nearby.
entries.unit_types: Fast or cheap units with OC 1+.
entries.rules_basis: 14.03 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2427-2435); 14.02 end-of-phase determination (:2409-2416).

entries.name: Stage within one Normal move of next turn's scoring condition
entries.description: In 11e you draw two tactical cards per turn with no hand limit, unscored cards stay in hand, and several actions only open from round 2. A card or action that can't be done this turn should still shape the move. End within one Normal move of next turn's spot; don't Advance there, because an Advance bars starting an action. Spots include the enemy deployment zone (Behind Enemy Lines), a flank edge band (Outflank), an uncovered table quarter, the centre ring, a forward terrain area (Plunder), the Tempting Target, and a non-home objective for Triangulate / Extract Intelligence. Prefer Hidden or out-of-sight spots, so the card scores next turn without a long exposed run.
entries.when_to_use: A held card or upcoming action can't be reached this turn but can be next turn. Weigh it against discarding the card for 1CP.
entries.unit_types: Fast or cheap units assigned to positional or action jobs.
entries.rules_basis: Engine 11e deck rules: CARDS_DRAWN_PER_TURN_11E = 2, no hand limit, only achieved cards discarded (SecondaryMissionManager.gd:27-31, 1602-1625). 'Discard a secondary at end of turn for 1CP' (11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:67). 16.01: a unit that advanced or fell back can't start an action (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2816). missionCards.json: the triangulation and gather-intel actions run 'from the second battle round onwards' (:1874, :2071).

entries.name: Advance now to pre-position when nothing is lost this turn
entries.description: If the unit has nothing to shoot (or only [ASSAULT] weapons), cannot charge this turn anyway, and has no action to start, Advance so it reaches next turn's objective, charge or action spot a turn earlier. Command Re-roll can re-roll the advance roll. Don't Advance a loaded transport whose cargo must disembark this phase.
entries.when_to_use: Long trips; round-1 forward staging; units out of range of everything; units whose guns are all [ASSAULT].
entries.unit_types: All; especially fast units and melee units far from targets.
entries.rules_basis: 09.06 Advance: M + D6, no charge or action afterwards (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1401-1414). 10.04 normal shooting requires no advance; 10.05 assault shooting uses [ASSAULT] weapons (:1489-1491, :1506-1516). 15.02: Command Re-roll covers the advance roll (:2651-2672). 16.01 (:2816). 18.04: no disembark from a transport that advanced this phase (:3019-3024).

entries.name: Choose who commits first: bait with cheap holders or hang back so the opponent exposes first
entries.description: Decide deliberately who steps onto the contested central objectives first. Either move cheap infantry onto them early, forcing the opponent to come out of cover and commit into you. Or hold the strike units just out of reach so the opponent has to expose themselves first, then counter-punch. The 11e trade-off is concrete: round-1 holds are what score your first Command-phase rows (round 2), but anything the opponent can kill there scores nothing and feeds their kill rows. Card timing shapes the choice (Disruption: 'score at least 8 on T1, hold 1 on T2-3, push on T4-5'), and so does the score (protect a lead or chase).
entries.when_to_use: Symmetric missions with contested middles; you have cheap holders and a stronger second wave; the opponent's alpha strike out-ranges yours; the VP difference.
entries.unit_types: Cheap objective units plus strike units.
entries.rules_basis: A strategy built on 14.02 end-of-phase/turn control (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2409-2416), the GDM Command timing (11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:7) and 07.02 fixed turn order (:1135-1139).
evidence: https://www.tabletopbattles.com/40k-competitive-innovations-in-11th-to-take-perchance-to-hold-pt-1 (search snippet: Orks move infantry onto objectives early to force the Blood Angels to move first)
https://www.tabletopbattles.com/40k-11th-edition-force-disposition-review-disruption/ (snippet: 'score at least 8 on T1, and hold on to 1 objective on turns 2 and 3 before pushing on turns 4 and 5')

Round 1 always pushes (WEIGHT_SCORING_URGENCY +3 at 9235-9239; STRATEGY_EARLY_SURVIVAL 0.7 at 2720 accepts more risk). There is no 'hang back' candidate and no turn-order logic.
entries.engine_support: Reuse _calculate_tempo_modifier (AIDecisionMaker.gd:17387), _get_round_strategy_modifiers (17421) and _calculate_enemy_threat_data (28695). New: a per-objective 'commit now vs next turn' comparison. Committing now is worth the next Command rows minus expected losses and opponent kill VP given the enemy's reach; compare that with the same units striking a turn later.
entries.value_reason: Shapes the first two rounds, but needs a survival model to price well.

entries.name: Stand within objective range to switch on objective-gated abilities
entries.description:
Many 11e datasheets fight at full power only when they, or their target, are within range of an objective. Examples:
- Intercessor Squad, Bolter Discipline: +1 to hit if this unit OR the target is within range of an objective.
- Custodian Guard, Impenetrable Defence: [SUSTAINED HITS 1].
- Sentinel Guard, Stand Vigil: [LETHAL HITS].
- Flash Gitz, Finderz Keeperz: +1 AP.
- Wreckas, Wreckin' and Lootin'.
- Heavy Intercessors, Unyielding in the Face of the Foe: +1 save while controlling.
- Bladeguard Ancient, Deeds of Legend; Grey Hunters, Cunning Hunters; Vulkan He'stan, Seeker of the Unfound.
So objectives double as buff zones. End within range of one while still shooting or fighting the target, or pick firing lanes onto enemies standing on objectives.
entries.when_to_use: The unit can end within an objective's range and still reach its target while choosing firing positions, and the buff changes the expected damage materially.
entries.unit_types: Intercessors, Heavy Intercessors, Bladeguard Ancient, Grey Hunters, Centurion Devastators, Custodian / Sentinel Guard, Flash Gitz, Wreckas units, Vulkan He'stan, etc.
entries.rules_basis: Datasheet text, e.g. Bolter Discipline (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:371, checked). Objective range per 14.02 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2405-2406) and MissionManager.model_in_objective_range (MissionManager.gd:529).
evidence: /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:371 (Bolter Discipline: 'In your Shooting phase, if any of the following apply, this unit's ranged attacks have +1 to hit rolls: This unit is within range of an objective. The target of that attack is within range of an objective.')

Per the factions stream: same file :399 (Unyielding in the Face of the Foe), :384 (Deeds of Legend), :318 (Cunning Hunters), :421 (Decimator Protocols), :628 (Seeker of the Unfound); /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/custodes/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:131 (Impenetrable Defence), :127 (Stand Vigil); /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:154 (Finderz Keeperz); orks/RULES.md:206 (Wreckin' and Lootin')

entries.engine_support: Reuse MissionManager.model_in_objective_range (MissionManager.gd:529) and the RulesEngine weapon-profile modifiers. New: an 'objective-gated buff' flag per unit (parsed once from ability text) that adds the expected-damage gain to destinations within objective range.
entries.value_reason: Intercessors and Custodian Guard are common, and the buff is worth roughly 15-20% more damage.

entries.name: Stay locked on the objective: remain stationary while engaged to keep holding or contesting it
entries.description: An engaged unit on an objective keeps its OC there. Falling back gives the objective away and also forbids shooting, charging and starting actions for the rest of the turn; Desperate Escape adds hazard rolls and a battle-shock roll. If your OC there is winning or tied, or your presence denies their score, stay engaged. Fall back only if the unit will die anyway and other units keep control without it.
entries.when_to_use: Engaged on an objective you control or contest, especially in late rounds, when the enemy can't destroy the unit outright in the Fight phase.
entries.unit_types: Any engaged unit with OC on an objective.
entries.move_type: Remain Stationary (engaged), instead of Fall Back
entries.rules_basis: 09.04 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1378-1388). 09.07: after a fall-back, no shooting, charge or action; Desperate Escape adds hazard rolls and a battle-shock roll (:1417-1441). 14.02: OC counts whether or not the unit is engaged (:2409-2416).

entries.name: Keep options open: end in central, flexible spots that reach two or more objectives next turn
entries.description: Prefer central positions from which the unit can reach two or more objectives or targets next turn, instead of committing to one flank before the opponent reveals reserves, Rapid Ingress or reactive moves.
entries.when_to_use: Early rounds; the opponent's plan or reserves are still unrevealed; the unit has no scoring job this turn.
entries.unit_types: Mobile units.
entries.rules_basis: A strategy supported by 11e reactive timing: Rapid Ingress 15.07 and Fire Overwatch 15.08 both happen at the end of the opponent's Movement phase (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2714-2742).

entries.name: Bring the OC-granting character to the contested objective
entries.description: Some units only reach full OC near a specific friendly model. Move the enabler (or the units) so the bonus is active on the contested objective when control is checked. Curse of the Wulfen: a Wulfen unit that is not battle-shocked and is within 6in of a SPACE WOLVES CHARACTER (non-Wulfen) or 12in of a Wolf Priest has +1 OC (INFANTRY) or +3 OC (VEHICLE: Wulfen Dreadnought, Murderfang). Hunting Hounds: +1 OC for Fenrisian Wolves and hunting wolves within 6in of a Space Wolves CHARACTER. The same applies to Ld auras that keep holders from being battle-shocked.
entries.when_to_use: An objective is tied or contested; a Wulfen VEHICLE (+3 OC) or several wolf units can reach it; the enabler can get within 6in / 12in safely; scoring rounds.
entries.unit_types: Space Wolves Wulfen units, Wulfen Dreadnought, Murderfang, Fenrisian Wolves, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wolf Scouts; Space Wolves characters and Wolf Priests as enablers.

entries.name: Buy the reach: pair the move with a move or advance boost when it turns 'one turn short' into 'arrives now'
entries.description:
Plan objective and charge reach with the real, modified distances:
- +M: Follow Me Ladz, Cybork Boosta, Lightning-fast Strike, Wolf-Touched, FUNGUS-FUEL INJECTION (+2in), etc.
- Advance-roll bonuses: 'ERE WE GO (+2 to advance rolls in 11e), Fuel-mixa Grot (+1).
- Effects that set the advance roll to 6: SUDDEN ONSLAUGHT, Wind Walker, Veil of Time, Shokk-boosta.
- Re-rolls: Waaagh!, Supercharged Engines, etc.
Spend the CP or ability when it converts a maybe into a guaranteed arrival on the objective this turn.
entries.when_to_use: The objective or charge distance is beyond M but within the modified M or a fixed-6 advance; the unit has the modifier, or a CP-cost boost is affordable; arriving now is worth a scoring window.
entries.unit_types: Ork bosses, Meks, Wagons, Speed Freeks, Boyz; Space Marine Mounted units / Speeders and Jump Pack captains; Space Wolves units near Venerable Dreadnoughts; Custodes (Solar Watch, Knight-Centura).

entries.name: Shoot-and-scoot: take a forward firing position knowing a post-shooting move can reach an objective
entries.description:
Units that can move after shooting can take a forward firing spot in the Movement phase, then use the second move to reach an objective, break line of sight or leave charge range. Examples:
- Wreckas GRAB IT: a normal move of up to 6in that must end within range of an objective; no charge afterwards.
- Gravis PURGATION PUSH: 5in, must end within objective range.
- Land Speeder Purgation Run; Pallas Mobile Hunter; Phobos Execute and Redeploy / Shadow Masters; Captain in Phobos Armour Tactical Fluidity.
entries.when_to_use: Targets are just out of range from a safe spot, an objective or safe spot lies within the post-shooting distance, and the unit doesn't need to charge.
entries.unit_types: Breaka Boyz, Flash Gitz, Tankbustas (Wreckas), Gravis (Linebreaker), Land Speeders, Pallas Grav-attack, Phobos units.

entries.name: Keep a bombing lane open for strikes at the end of the opponent's Fight phase
entries.description:
Three aircraft abilities act at the END of the opponent's Fight phase, from wherever your Movement phase left the aircraft:
- Burna-bommer, Burna Bomb: a visible non-Lone-Operative, non-MONSTER/VEHICLE enemy within 36in. On a 2+ it takes D3 mortal wounds, cannot be hidden until the end of your next turn, and your ranged attacks against it gain [IGNORES COVER].
- Blitza-bommer, Boom Bomb: within 24in.
- Ares Gunship, Infernus Firebombs: within 24in.
End the aircraft's move with broad central visibility over the enemy's likely Hidden objective holders, so the bomb strips Hidden and cover before your next shooting at them.
entries.when_to_use: The enemy holds objectives with Hidden infantry, and the aircraft can end its move safely with central visibility.

The engine implements 'cannot be hidden' at TerrainManager.gd:999-1005.

entries.skeptic_note: All three bombers are AIRCRAFT: Burna-bommer and Blitza-bommer (orks Datasheets_keywords.csv) and Ares Gunship (custodes Datasheets_keywords.csv). AIRCRAFT can only make ingress moves (23.02 :3505-3506), so 'Normal Move' is illegal. They start in strategic reserves (23.01 :3500-3501) and arrive by ingress from round 2; they cannot use Rapid Ingress (15.07 :2724). They stay on the battlefield through the opponent's Fight phase and return to reserves at the end of the opponent's turn (23.02 :3507-3509). So the lane is chosen at the ingress set-up: wholly within 6″ of an edge and more than 8″ from enemies (20.04 :3264-3266). In the rules, friendly models of other units can block that sight line (06.01 :1029-1030). Burna Bomb needs a visible target within 36″; Boom Bomb and Infernus Firebombs within 24″. — 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3499-3509, 3255-3273, 2724; orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:111,115; custodes/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:94
entries.errata_note: The bombs target a 'visible' enemy unit, which must be visible to the aircraft itself, and a Hidden model is visible only to enemy models within its detection range (15in unless modified); Hidden now also covers INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM in areas with only light features. So to bomb a holder unit whose models are all Hidden, the aircraft must set up within that range, not merely within 24in/36in with open sight lines. — Commentary 06.01.01 Describing Visible Units; 13.09 errata

entries.name: Stage a cheap action carrier with a Normal move, then keep it still
entries.description: Shared rule for every 11e action card. Primary actions: Secure Asset, Sabotage, Vanguard Operation, Maintain Control, Sensor Sweep, Booby Trap, Decoy, Triangulate, Extract Intelligence, Surveil. Secondary actions: Cleanse, Plunder. Each card's site is in MIS-02 to MIS-06, MIS-18 and MIS-23. Send the unit whose lost shooting and charge cost least and that can reach and survive the site (small, cheap, mobile, able to become Hidden), not simply the nearest unit. It must get there by a Normal move, Remain Stationary, a Rapid or Tactical Disembark followed by a Normal move, or an ingress or Deep Strike arrival. It must never Advance or Fall Back. It must end unengaged, not battle-shocked, with OC 1+, and not already acting (an attached unit counts as one unit). After it starts the action in the Shooting phase it cannot shoot (TITANIC excepted) or charge. Any further move other than pile-in or consolidation, or becoming battle-shocked, makes the action fail, so plan no further move for it. TITANIC units lose nothing: they can start while engaged and still shoot.
entries.when_to_use: Any turn an action card is live and a qualifying site is within Normal-move reach. Choose the carrier before deciding whether that unit Advances. Rank candidates by ranged and charge output forgone plus points at risk. Exclude units holding screen, denial or objective-keeper jobs.
entries.unit_types: OC 1+ units that are not AIRCRAFT/FORTIFICATION and not battle-shocked: cheap infantry and small-base units, characters with nothing worth shooting, TITANIC units (no shooting cost).
entries.move_type: Normal (also Remain Stationary, Disembark rapid/tactical, Reserves arrival)
entries.rules_basis: 16.01 Performing Actions (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2794-2828): eligibility :2808-2817; no shooting (excluding TITANIC) and no charge :2819-2822; any move except pile-in or consolidation, or leaving the battlefield, cancels :2824-2828. 09.06 Advance :1413-1415 and 09.07 Fall-back :1436-1439 bar starting an action. 01.07: battle-shocked units have OC '-' and cannot start or complete an action (:216-222). 18.04: a disembark is not a barred move, but Combat Disembark battle-shocks the unit (:3055-3056). Engine: ActionsManager.gd:117-193 (eligibility and faction waivers), :247-257 (a move cancels), :263-280 (battle-shock blocks completion). Corrections: youtube#46 says Knights must pay CP to shoot and act, but 16.01 exempts TITANIC units from the no-shooting effect (:2821), so the 1CP quote is unverified. core-rules#82's Gather Intel site is any non-home objective without your marker (missionCards.json:2071), not only NML objectives. Plunder needs a terrain AREA outside your territory (missionCards.json:2367).

entries.coverage_detail: No movement candidate stages a carrier. The AI never dispatches START_ACTION; only the human ShootingController.gd:4894 does. In the Shooting phase the AI only takes PERFORM_SECONDARY_ACTION with a unit that already stands on a site, scored as VP x1.5 minus shooting value (AIDecisionMaker.gd:16472-16484, 23780-23818). The Advance decision never checks that 09.06 bars actions (_should_unit_advance 12650-12748, long trip 12946-13015). MissionManager resolves primary-card actions by position at end of turn (MissionManager.gd:1841-1953). Sabotage, Vanguard and Extract Intelligence fall back to a positional score when no action was started (e.g. :2749-2767), so in the engine the AI scores without giving up shooting. Action rule types add only a flat +1.0 objective pressure (AIDecisionMaker.gd:22874-22878).
entries.engine_support: Reuse ActionsManager.can_start_action / get_startable_actions (ActionsManager.gd:117, :60), MissionManager.can_start_mission_action_11e (MissionManager.gd:2030-2047) and get_card_action_summary_11e (:2210), _estimate_unit_shooting_value (AIDecisionMaker.gd:23954) for the cost of forgone shooting, and _compute_movement_toward_target (14212). entries.errata_note: Becoming battle-shocked fails a started action only for units with no rule that lets them start actions while battle-shocked. Per FAQ 16.01, such units (e.g. Tactical Mainstay, CONSERVAI ka'tah; see MIS-36) keep the action going if they become battle-shocked after starting it, but a battle-shocked carrier still has OC '-' and so cannot meet a 'controls the objective' completion (01.07, 14.02). — FAQ 16.01 Performing Actions (also filed under FAQ 01.07 Battle-shock Rolls)

entries.name: Send action carriers to different qualifying objectives
entries.description: Control actions with unlimited uses pay per carrier or per objective. Send several carriers to DIFFERENT qualifying objectives; each carrier must itself control its objective at end of turn, so bring enough OC. Sabotage: any non-home objective, 3VP per saboteur, +2VP in enemy territory (enemy home first, then central, which counts as enemy territory). Stop at the 15VP primary cap (three 5VP saboteurs). Decoy (Smoke and Mirrors): only UNDECOYED non-home objectives. The tag never clears and pays 2VP (+2VP in enemy territory) every turn, and 4+ decoyed objectives pay 10VP at end of battle. Each layout has 4 non-home objectives (2 expansions, central, enemy home), so all four, including the enemy home, must be decoyed at some point. Extract Intelligence (Gather Intel, R2+): non-home objectives with none of your markers, 7VP per completion, so two per turn nearly reaches the cap. End of battle pays 5VP for 3+ markers and 5VP for a marker in range of the enemy home. Cleanse (secondary): two different non-home objectives for 5VP; one alone is 2VP.
entries.when_to_use: Your primary is Sabotage, Smoke and Mirrors or Gather Intel (R2+), or Cleanse is in hand. Two or more qualifying objectives are within Normal-move reach of spare carriers that can still control them at end of turn.
entries.unit_types: Several cheap OC 1+ carriers, durable OC for contested objectives, transports that drop carriers (MIS-31).
entries.rules_basis: missionCards.json sabotage (:1531; unlimited, one objective each, completes at end of turn if that unit controls that objective; 3VP per unit +2VP in enemy territory). smoke-and-mirrors (:1100; undecoyed non-home; decoyed never clears; 2VP +2VP per objective; 10VP at end of battle for 4+). gather-intel (:2071; R2+; non-home with none of your markers; 7VP per completion; end of battle 5VP for 3+ markers and 5VP for a marker in range of the opponent's home). cleanse (:2599; 2VP/5VP tiers). 15VP per-turn primary cap: PrimaryMissionData11e.gd:60 and 11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:7. 14.02: a model is in range of a terrain objective while within its terrain area (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2405-2406); controlling unit :2421-2424. Central counts as enemy territory for Sabotage: 11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:113. All 46 shipped layouts with objectives have 2 home, 2 expansion (NML) and 1 central objective (40k/terrain_layouts/*.json). Conflict: the missions doc (:142-144) limits Extract Intelligence to NML objectives; the card data says any non-home objective.

entries.name: Keep an action carrier and a separate OC holder on central every turn
entries.description: Vital Link's Maintain Control and the shared Sensor Sweep (Extract Relic, Locate and Deny) need a carrier within range of a central objective that does not move after starting. Both complete only if that unit controls central at end of turn. Vital Link pays 2VP plus 1VP per operation marker within range of central at each end of turn you control it, adds one marker per successful action, and pays +4VP at the R2+ Command check when a held non-home objective is central. Extract Relic pays 4VP per completed sweep (once per turn; not while only one marker remains). Locate and Deny sweeps its own markers down to the one it can hold. Put a cheap carrier and a durable high-OC holder there, and use the 2in engagement range to tie up would-be contesters.
entries.when_to_use: Your primary is Vital Link, Extract Relic or Locate and Deny. Every turn from R1 while central can be controlled at end of turn.
entries.unit_types: Cheap carrier plus a durable high-OC holder.
entries.rules_basis: missionCards.json vital-link (:1412): maintain-control once per turn, central only, completes if controlling; EOT 2VP + 1VP per marker within range of a controlled central objective; R2+ Command +4VP for central; end of battle 10VP for the enemy home. extract-relic (:1286) and locate-and-deny (:983) sensor-sweep: central only, once per turn, completes if controlling, restricted when one marker remains. 03.04 engagement range 2in (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:542-552). 16.01. Correction to missions#18: losing central only zeroes that turn's payout. The card does not remove placed markers; the engine keeps a counter (MissionManager.gd:1905-1909) and scores it only while central is held (:2769-2777).

entries.name: Send the once-per-turn carrier to the best qualifying non-home objective
entries.description: Secure Asset: any non-home objective, every round including R1, 4VP if the carrier controls it at end of turn. The card also pays 2VP for killing an enemy unit that started the turn on central, and at the R2+ Command check 4VP for holding 1+ non-home and 4VP for holding 3+ objectives. Triangulate: from R2, one NEW untriangulated non-home objective per turn; the tag is permanent. End-of-turn tiers are 3/6/10VP for 1/2/3+ triangulated objectives, with no need to keep control. End of battle pays 10VP for controlling 4+ objectives. Pick the qualifying objective the carrier can control at end of turn with least risk (often your-side expansion) and keep a second OC source next to it. For Triangulation plan the order (e.g. R2 own expansion, R3 central, R4 enemy expansion) and spread to 4+ objectives in R5.
entries.when_to_use: Your primary is Secure Asset (every turn) or Triangulation (R2-R4 for the action, R5 for the 4+ spread).
entries.unit_types: One cheap OC carrier per turn plus an OC holder.
entries.rules_basis: missionCards.json secure-asset (:1189): once per turn; completes at end of turn if the unit controls the targeted non-home objective; awards as listed. triangulation (:1874): battle_round min 2, once per turn, non-home, tag never clears; tiers; end-of-battle count_min 4. 16.01; 14.02 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2401-2424). Secure Asset is modelled as a hold_min rule, not an action (PrimaryMissionData11e.gd:293-299).

entries.name: Booby-trap as many untrapped terrain areas as you have spare units, objective areas first
entries.description: Death Trap's Booby Trap completes immediately, so the unit needs neither to survive nor to control anything. Each distinct unit that Normal-moves into a different untrapped terrain area outside your deployment zone (or in range of a non-home objective) traps it: 2VP per area trapped this turn, +3VP if the area is an objective. Areas stay trapped, so each turn needs fresh ones. Send every spare unit that has not advanced, OC-1 chaff included, into different areas, objective areas first. 45 of the 48 shipped layouts have 16 areas, and 4 non-home objectives lie outside your DZ. Trap the areas the Take and Hold opponent must stand in, then kill units that started their turn there for 3VP.
entries.when_to_use: Your primary is Death Trap. Every turn while untrapped areas are within Normal-move reach.
entries.unit_types: Many cheap units including OC-1 chaff; infantry becomes Hidden in dense areas.
entries.rules_basis: missionCards.json death-trap (:767): Shooting phase; a unit in range of a non-home objective or within an untrapped terrain area outside your DZ; unlimited, one area each; completes immediately. entries.name: End a real move within range of objectives that carry enemy operation markers
entries.description: Under Surveil the Foe, whenever a friendly unit ENDS A MOVE within range of an objective with any of the opponent's operation markers in range, those markers are removed. entries.name: Put the planned killer on an objective before it kills
entries.description: Purge and Secure pays 3VP when a friendly unit within range of an objective destroys an enemy unit, or when an enemy unit that started the turn on an objective is destroyed (one branch, not both). At the end of your turn it may consecrate one unconsecrated non-home objective it is within range of (3VP for 1-2, 6VP for 3+, and 5VP at end of battle if the opponent's home is consecrated). entries.name: Prefer objectives inside the opponent's territory when the card pays a territory bonus
entries.description: Determined Acquisition (Take and Hold vs Disruption) pays 2VP at end of turn per objective you newly control this turn. From R2 its Command check pays 3VP per controlled objective plus another 3VP for each one in the opponent's territory. Sabotage (+2VP per saboteur) and Smoke and Mirrors (+2VP per decoyed objective) pay the same kind of territory bonus. When choosing between capture trips, rank objectives in the opponent's territory (their home, their-side expansion, and central for Sabotage) above equally costly objectives in your own half. For Determined Acquisition also value flipping objectives you did not hold at the start of the turn.

entries.name: Advance into positional scoring geometry, never with a unit that must start an action
entries.description: Advancing costs only the charge and the right to start an action this turn. It does not affect OC or the positional cards: Behind Enemy Lines, quarters, Display of Might, Centre Ground, Outflank, Beacon, Forward Position, Secure No Man's Land, Tempting Target, Defend Stronghold's home objective. When such geometry is beyond M but within M + D6 and the unit has no worthwhile shooting or charge, Advance there; in R5 that is almost always right. Never Advance the unit planned as this turn's action carrier, unless it has a faction exemption (MIS-36).

entries.name: Send a backup action carrier when the first is exposed to Overwatch
entries.description: Fire Overwatch happens at the end of your Movement phase, before the Shooting phase in which your actions start. A carrier that ends visible within 24in of an enemy unit can therefore be shot before it acts. Snap shooting only hits on unmodified 6s, so this mostly matters against high-volume shooters. When the action is worth a lot, send a second unit that can perform an action toward the same or another site.
entries.when_to_use: A high-value action, a carrier ending visible within 24in of an unengaged enemy unit with many shots, and a spare cheap unit that can reach.
entries.unit_types: Cheap units able to perform actions.
entries.rules_basis: 15.08 Fire Overwatch (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2735-2761): end of the opponent's Movement phase; one visible enemy unit within 24in; hits only on unmodified 6s. 16.01 (:2808-2828).

entries.name: Screen deep-strike and Rapid Ingress landing zones with 8″ denial bubbles
entries.description: Spread cheap units so no spot near your home/backfield objectives, artillery, characters and gunline is more than 8″ from one of your units: reserves arriving by an ingress move must be set up more than 8″ horizontally from ALL enemy units (Deep Strike anywhere, even inside your deployment zone; strategic reserves only within 6″ of an edge — see DEN-13). Size each unit's bubble to the real stand-off: 8″ core, 6″ against arrivals allowed closer (Dark Angels RELIC TELEPORTARIUM), 12″ around an Arae-Shrike bearer (enemy ingress cannot be set up within 12″ of it). The screen must already be complete at the END of your own Movement phase (the opponent's Rapid Ingress arrives then) and must still hold after your charges and consolidations (their normal arrivals come in their own Movement phase): move screeners before the units they screen, keep them out of charges, re-check coverage at the end of the turn. Coherency (within 2″ of one model and 9″ of every other model) caps how wide one unit can spread.
entries.when_to_use: The opponent still has units in strategic reserves (incl. Deep Strike) or repositioned units, plus CP for Rapid Ingress. Arrivals start in battle round 2 and Rapid Ingress cannot be used in round 1: if the AI moves second, its round-1 end-of-turn positions already face the opponent's round-2 arrivals; if it moves first, the first check is the end of its own round-2 Movement phase. Unarrived strategic reserves are destroyed at the end of round 3, so drop the task from round 4 unless repositioned units remain. Cap the screeners so objectives keep their OC, and skip it entirely when nothing is left in reserve.
entries.unit_types: Cheap multi-model infantry, fast cheap units, scouts/infiltrators, chaff (Gretchin, spore mines); an Arae-Shrike Custodes bearer as a 12″ anchor; units already holding home objectives count as coverage.
entries.move_type: Normal (Remain Stationary once in place; adjacent pre-battle variant: Scout move / Infiltrators deployment)
entries.rules_basis: 20.03 strategic reserves arrive from battle round 2 and are destroyed if not arrived by the end of round 3 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3249-3253, :3276-3283); 20.04 ingress: wholly within 6″ of an edge, more than 8″ horizontally from all enemy units, not in the opponent's DZ before round 3 (:3255-3274); 24.09 Deep Strike anywhere more than 8″, even in the opponent's DZ (:3649-3661); 15.07 RAPID INGRESS — WHEN: end of your opponent's Movement phase; not in battle round 1 (:2714-2731); 03.03 coherency 2″/9″ (:518-532). entries.name: Charge-screen a valuable unit (bubble-wrap it, with depth)
entries.description: Place a cheap unit across the approaches to a valuable friendly unit (gunline, artillery, character, objective holder) so that any charge ending engaged with it would also end within 2″ of the screen. An 11e charge must end engaged with every charge target and with no other enemy unit, and charge moves cannot pass through models (17.01's MONSTER/VEHICLE pass-through covers only normal and advance moves), so the charger must also declare the screen (within 12″ and within its roll) and engage both with one roll, go around, or fail. FLY chargers can take to the skies over the screen but still need a landing spot engaged with the target and more than 2″ from the screen, so a tight wrap still works. Leave depth: if the screen dies, an enemy unit that has not fought can make an overrun fight (one extra 3″ pile-in toward enemy units within 5″) and units that fought must consolidate 3″ toward any enemy within 3″, so keep the protected unit roughly 5″+ behind where the chargers will stand (derived).
entries.when_to_use: An unengaged enemy melee unit can reach a valuable friendly unit next turn (its M + up to 12″) and a cheap unit can stand in that lane; move the screen before the unit it protects.
entries.unit_types: Screens: cheap infantry, chaff, vehicle hulls. Protected: gunlines, artillery, characters, objective holders.
entries.move_type: Normal (Remain Stationary when already in the lane)
entries.rules_basis: 11.04 charge move: targets within 12″ and within the roll; AFTER MOVING engaged with all charge targets and with no non-target (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1640-1665); 03.01 bases cannot move through enemy models (:385-395); 03.04 engagement range 2″ (:542-552); 17.01 pass-through only on normal/advance moves (:2867-2874); 21.03 taking to the skies includes charge moves (:3358-3375); 12.03 pile-in targets within 5″ and 12.06 overrun pile-in (:1737-1760, :1866-1877); 12.08 engaging consolidation when within 3″ (:1954-1957). entries.name: Move toward a dangerous enemy shooter or action unit to charge and lock it (user example: move toward an enemy to charge it)
entries.description: The denial form of 'move toward someone to charge them': pick the enemy unit whose shooting or next action matters most and move into charge reach, planning to engage and stay engaged. An engaged non-MONSTER/VEHICLE unit cannot make normal shooting (only close-quarters shooting with [CLOSE-QUARTERS] weapons at units it is engaged with), cannot start an action, and if it falls back it cannot shoot, charge or start an action that turn. Against MONSTER/VEHICLE targets the lock is weaker: they may still close-quarters shoot (at -1 to hit unless a [CLOSE-QUARTERS] weapon targets a unit they are engaged with) and your other units can shoot them at -1; a locked transport still cannot make a normal move. The charger need not win the fight — the value is the enemy's lost shooting/action.
entries.when_to_use: An enemy unit with high ranged output, or one that would start a scoring action next turn, is within the melee unit's M + likely charge roll (the target must be within 12″ and within the roll); the charger can survive the return fight; best against non-M/V shooters. Do not Advance unless the unit may still charge after advancing.
entries.unit_types: Melee units, fast melee, durable or cheap tarpit units.
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (Advance only with an advance-and-charge ability)
entries.rules_basis: 10.04 normal shooting needs the unit unengaged (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1489-1494); 10.06 close-quarters shooting (:1522-1545); 17.03 shooting engaged M/V at -1 (:2896-2910; [BLAST] excluded by errata, 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:608); 16.01 an engaged unit cannot start an action (:2806-2817); 09.07 after a fall-back: no shooting, charge or action (:1417-1440); 11.02 charge eligibility within 12″, not after advance/fall back (:1597-1623); 09.06 (:1399-1411). Corrected: F015's vehicle examples overstate the 11e lock (engaged M/V can still shoot at -1).

entries.name: Move-block the enemy's approach corridors and the routes to your objectives
entries.description: Stand blockers across the lanes enemy units must use — gaps between terrain pieces, the approach to an objective you hold or need next Command phase or at the end of the enemy turn — forward of the objective, so walkers detour or stop short: normal and advance moves cannot cross enemy bases and must end more than 2″ from your models (they may pass through your engagement range mid-move). Treat cheap units as consumables: the value is the movement tax. Use MONSTER/VEHICLE hulls as the wall against enemy MONSTER/VEHICLE movers: 17.01 lets M/V models move through non-M/V models on normal/advance moves but not through other M/V, so by the rules infantry blocks do not stop them, nor FLY units that take to the skies (-2″), nor SUPER-HEAVY WALKERs. Engine today: plain M/V movers are blocked by any enemy base, and FLY units cross enemy bases on every normal/advance move without declaring take to the skies.
entries.when_to_use: An objective you must still hold (next Command phase or end of the enemy turn) or your backline is reachable by enemy OC or melee units next turn through predictable gaps; cap the number of blockers so objectives keep OC, and stop spending them once the army is thin.
entries.unit_types: Cheap multi-model infantry, chaff (spore mines, Gretchin, cheap broods), vehicles as walls.
entries.rules_basis: 03.01 a base can pass any gap it fits but cannot be moved through enemy models (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:385-395); 09.05 AFTER MOVING unengaged (:1390-1397); FAQ 03.04: moving through an enemy's engagement range does not engage (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:265); 17.01 (:2867-2874); 21.03 (:3358-3375); 24.35 (:3940-3966); 14.02 control is checked at the end of each phase and turn (:2401-2418; errata doc :557).

entries.name: Seal the screen's gaps against the widest enemy base
entries.description: When a unit acts as a wall (charge screen, corridor block, objective fill), lay out its models so the clear gap between neighbouring bases is narrower than the widest base of any enemy model that could try to pass — the gap seals when centre distance < rA + rB + d. In 11e a mover may pass straight through your engagement range and is blocked only by base overlap, so the 10e rule of thumb (gap < base + 2″, 'stay 1″ away') is wrong. Coherency caps the wall: each model within 2″ of another and within 9″ of every other model, so one unit seals roughly 9″ plus its end bases (derived). Sealing does not stop FLY units taking to the skies, SUPER-HEAVY WALKERs or (by the rules) enemy M/V on normal/advance moves; the wall still denies end positions within 2″ and charge end positions.
entries.when_to_use: Every time a unit is placed as a screen or block; size the gap to the widest non-FLY enemy base that can reach the lane next turn.
entries.unit_types: Multi-model cheap infantry screens.
entries.rules_basis: 03.01: a model can be moved through any space its base can fit through and cannot be moved through enemy models (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:385-395); 09.05 (:1390-1397); FAQ 03.04: moving through engagement range does not engage (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:265); 03.03 coherency 2″ and 9″ (:518-532); 21.03 (:3358-3375); 24.35 (:3940-3966); 17.01 (:2867-2874). entries.name: Move into cover first to deny it: occupy the contested staging terrain (user example: move into cover)
entries.description: The denial version of 'move into cover': in rounds 1-2 put bodies into or against the mid-board terrain both armies want to stage in or behind. INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM models inside a terrain area that contains light or dense features are Hidden (13.09 as amended), and units behind such an area are obscured from enemies whose every sight line crosses it, so your army stages out of sight. At the same time enemy models cannot end a move within 2″ of yours, so they lose that staging spot, and models without INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM/MOBILE cannot move horizontally through dense sections over 2″ tall, so infantry can claim ruins vehicles cannot contest. One move both protects you and denies them.
entries.when_to_use: Rounds 1-2 on layouts with a dominant central ruin or dense area between the armies, when you can get there first (moving first, scouts/infiltrators, fast units), especially against short-range or melee armies that need that cover to approach.
entries.unit_types: INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM (gain Hidden), durable bricks, scouts and infiltrators.
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (adjacent pre-battle variant: Scout move 24.32, Infiltrators deployment)
entries.rules_basis: 13.09 Hidden, first bullet amended to ‘one or more light/dense terrain features’ (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:529; the launch text 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2292-2303 says dense only); 13.10 obscuring, excluding areas either model is within (:2305-2311); 13.11 Solid (:2313-2317); 13.06 dense traversal (:2163-2183); 09.05 end unengaged (:1390-1397); 03.04 (:542-552). entries.name: Move toward the enemy's screens to shoot or charge them away (user example: move toward an enemy to shoot it)
entries.description: The counter-denial form of 'move toward someone to shoot them': enemy chaff that blocks your charge lanes, sits in your reserves' landing zones or walls a corridor is worth more than its points. Move shooters and chargers so they can remove it before the units that need the space act. Within a turn shooting comes before charging, so clearing a screen in the Shooting phase opens the lane for this turn's charges (a charge cannot end engaged with a non-target). Your own arrivals happen in the Movement phase, before your shooting, so landing zones must be cleared the turn before — or this turn, to open space for your Rapid Ingress at the end of the opponent's next Movement phase (they may re-screen first) — because arrivals must be more than 8″ from every enemy unit.
entries.when_to_use: A planned charge on a valuable target is blocked by chaff; you hold reserves for rounds 2-3 and every good landing spot is within 8″ of an enemy screen; or their screen protects their gunline/objective. Worth a trade down (F008), but don't spend your best melee unit on it.
entries.unit_types: High-volume shooters, fast chaff-killers; sequenced before the chargers/arrivals that need the space.
entries.rules_basis: 11.04 a charge cannot end engaged with a non-target (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1660-1665); 20.04 and 24.09 arrivals more than 8″ from all enemy units (:3255-3274, :3649-3661); 09.02 reserves arrive in the Move Units step (:1345-1366); 15.07 Rapid Ingress at the end of the opponent's Movement phase (:2714-2731).

entries.name: Spoil the opponent's presence- or majority-based scoring zones
entries.description: Plant a unit (one model counts) where the opponent's card needs emptiness, or a majority, at its check: (a) Centre Ground — any of your units within 6″ of the centre blocks their 5VP tier and within 3″ blocks both; checked at the end of THEIR turn, so the unit must survive it. (b) Defend Stronghold bonus — one of your units within their DZ at the end of YOUR turn strips their +2VP (the engine needs it wholly within). (c) Vanguard Operation — their action completes at the end of their turn only if none of your units is within that terrain area (an area in your territory), so pre-occupy the areas in your half they can reach. (d) Extract Relic / Locate and Deny — the last-marker condition needs no enemy unit in that terrain area. (e) Search and Scour — their end-of-battle 5VP needs none of your units wholly within their territory (engine: their DZ). (f) Display of Might — their 5VP tier at the end of YOUR turn needs strictly more of their units than yours wholly in No Man's Land (excluding AIRCRAFT and battle-shocked units), so step extra cheap units wholly into NML or kill/shock theirs.
entries.when_to_use: The opponent's revealed cards include one of these and the check falls in a round where it scores; prefer durable, Hidden or Lone Operative units when the check is at the end of their turn.
entries.unit_types: Cheap units; durable/Hidden/Lone Operative units; fast or deep-striking units for their DZ.
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance / Reserves arrival (Deep Strike into their DZ)

entries.name: Don't end moves inside enemy 'ends a move within X″' triggers (reactive moves, snared objectives)
entries.description: Many 11e faction rules fire in your Movement phase when one of your units ENDS a move near theirs: RESPONSIVE TACTICS (Space Marines, D6″), MASTERFUL TACTICS and TRANSHUMAN REACTIONS (D6″, or 6″ with the tactical doctrine), PRACTICAL TACTICS and SWIFT AS THE EAGLE (D3+3″), SCARPER! and WHIRLIGIG EVASION (Orks, D6″ or 6″), Predatory Instinct (Space Wolves, D6″, once per battle round) — all on an enemy ending within 8″, measured edge to edge; MORTIS SNARES hits the first unit that ends a move within range of the snared objective with D6 mortal wounds on a 2+. Unless the reaction helps you, end just outside the trigger (more than 8″) so their unit stays put for your shooting and charges, or Remain Stationary — a unit that remains stationary never triggers start/end-of-move rules. Discount long charges and precise blocks against units that can jump away.
entries.when_to_use: An enemy unit with such a rule (and the CP or use left) is near your planned destination and its dodge would cost you a charge target, a shooting target, an objective or a block; or a valuable unit would end on a snared objective.
entries.unit_types: All units; especially chargers, shooters that need a fixed target, valuable objective-takers.
entries.rules_basis: 09.04 remain stationary triggers no start/end-of-move rules (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1378-1388); trigger texts .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/RULES.md:259 (RESPONSIVE TACTICS), :647 (TRANSHUMAN REACTIONS), :714 (MASTERFUL TACTICS), :625 (MORTIS SNARES), custodes/RULES.md:156 (SWIFT AS THE EAGLE), orks/RULES.md:223 (SCARPER!), :268 (WHIRLIGIG EVASION); PRACTICAL TACTICS in space-marines/wahapedia/Stratagems.csv (D3+3″); predatory_instinct at 40k/scripts/codex/space_wolves/SWAbilities11e.gd:1262; RULINGS.md:396, :482 (8″ edge to edge), :402 (any settled move in any phase triggers a snare); 15.01 once per phase (:2495-2500).

entries.name: Keep enemy units out of your deployment zone through their turn
entries.description: For your own Defend Stronghold (from round 2, scored at the end of the OPPONENT's turn: 3VP for controlling your home, +2VP while no enemy units are within your DZ — the engine counts only units wholly within) and against their Behind Enemy Lines (they score per unit wholly within your DZ at the end of their turn): keep a durable OC unit on home, block the DZ entrances against walkers (DEN-04), deny deep-strike spots inside the DZ (Deep Strike may land there; DEN-01) and, from round 3, your DZ's edge band (DEN-13), so that no enemy unit can be in your DZ when their turn ends.
entries.when_to_use: Defend Stronghold is active for the AI from round 2 (it is redrawn if drawn in round 1), or the opponent holds Behind Enemy Lines, and enemy units can reach or arrive in your DZ next turn.
entries.unit_types: Durable home holder plus cheap screeners.

entries.skeptic_note: The correction of missions#40 is itself wrong. Defend Stronghold scores 'at the end of your opponent's turn or the end of the fifth battle round (whichever comes first)' (missionCards.json:2706 text). For the player going second, a card held or drawn during their own round-5 turn scores at the end of round 5, straight after their own turn, with no enemy turn to survive; that is what the clause is for. The engine does the same: final_round_clause lets the last player of the final round score at the end of that round (SecondaryMissionManager.gd:704-709; ScoringPhase.gd:112-118). Holders must survive the opponent's turn in every earlier round, and in round 5 when the AI moves first. — missionCards.json:2706; SecondaryMissionManager.gd:653-709; ScoringPhase.gd:112-118; 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3267-3270, 3649-3661

entries.name: Hunt the enemy units that score from your half before the check
entries.description: You cannot move enemy units, so some denial needs them dead: your Search and Scour pays 5VP at the end of the battle only if no enemy units are wholly within your territory (engine: your DZ); your Defend Stronghold +2VP needs no enemy in your DZ at the end of their turn; their Behind Enemy Lines (units wholly in your DZ) and Outflank (units within 6″ of an edge and outside their own territory) score at the end of their turn; their Beacon pays at the end of YOUR turn while their beacon unit is alive outside their DZ. Move shooters and chargers back or across to kill the infiltrators, deep strikers and raiders standing there — engaging them is not enough.
entries.when_to_use: Those cards are active and enemy units stand in the scoring position; for Search and Scour start clearing by rounds 3-4, since the check is at the end of the battle.
entries.unit_types: Home-guard killers, fast units that can turn back, deep strikers.

entries.name: Stay out of enemy Heroic Intervention reach
entries.description: At the end of your Charge phase the opponent (1CP) can charge with one unengaged unit within 12″ of your units (a VEHICLE only if CHARACTER/WALKER). Leap to Defend may only target your units that made a charge move this phase and are within its 2D6 roll; Into the Fray (+1CP, 2CP in total) caps the roll at 6 but may target any of your units within 6″. End non-charging units — especially fragile shooters and action units — more than 6″ from unengaged enemy melee/character units, and when choosing charges expect Leap to Defend from enemy units within roll distance of where your chargers end: kill or lock those interceptors first, or charge where they cannot reach.
entries.when_to_use: The opponent has 1-2 CP and unengaged melee-capable units near your charge targets or your forward units.
entries.unit_types: All units; especially chargers and fragile forward units.

entries.name: Zone ground with your threat ranges (counter-punch posture)
entries.description: Park melee and shooting threats at the edge of your own reach but outside the enemy's, so any enemy unit that steps onto a given objective or lane would end inside your charge reach (within 12″ and within your likely 2D6) or your kill zone next turn. entries.when_to_use: Your threat range exceeds the enemy's, or you cannot hold the objective with bodies but can punish whoever steps onto it; mid-game, when ahead or when the enemy must come to you.
entries.unit_types: Fast melee counter-punchers, long-range shooters, durable elite armies.
