entries.name: Fill a small terrain-objective area so enemy models can't end in it
entries.description: A model is in range of a terrain objective only while it is within that terrain area, and enemy normal/advance moves must end more than 2″ from your models and cannot pass through them. Spread a many-model unit across a small objective area so every spot in it is within 2″ of one of your models, and seal the entrances (DEN-05): enemy walkers then cannot end in range and add OC. It does not stop charges (chargers end engaged with your models inside the area and their OC counts) or units already inside; FLY and M/V movers can pass through but still cannot end within 2″.
entries.when_to_use: Small terrain objectives you hold, with a unit that has enough models to cover the area inside coherency (each model within 9″ of every other).
entries.unit_types: Large infantry units.
entries.rules_basis: 14.01-14.02: within range of a terrain objective = within the terrain area (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2389-2410); 09.05 (:1390-1397); 03.01 (:385-395); 03.03 9″ envelope (:518-532); 11.04 charges end engaged (:1640-1665).
entries.coverage_detail: Holding means REMAIN_STATIONARY (B19, AIDecisionMaker.gd:7187-7200; B20 :7314-7355); there is no reposition inside the objective area, no spread to occupy it, and no area-coverage test.
entries.engine_support: MissionManager.model_in_objective_range / model_gap_to_objective_range_px (MissionManager.gd:529-569), TerrainManager.area_at (TerrainManager.gd:792-950), the placement ladder (AIDecisionMaker.gd:14520-14722). New: an area-coverage placer (models packed so the area is within 2″ of a model, in coherency) plus a check that no legal enemy end spot remains in range.
entries.value_reason: Terrain objectives are the 11e default and filling a small one makes walk-on contests impossible, but charges still get in and only small areas can be filled.
entries.errata_note: Per the FAQ, models on upper levels of terrain features inside the area's boundary (and overhanging FRAME parts) are within the terrain area and so in range, but engagement range reaches only 5″ vertically. A ground-level fill therefore does not stop enemy INFANTRY (or other models allowed to end on upper surfaces, 13.06) from ending more than 5″ above your models, e.g. on a ruin's second floor; also occupy those levels, or rely on the fill only for low, single-level areas. — FAQ 14.01 Terrain Objectives (same FAQ under 13.01 Placing Terrain and 17.02 Frame; errata doc :511, :543, :603)

entries.name: Use dense terrain as a moat against enemy vehicles and monsters
entries.description: Hold objectives and backline spots with INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM inside or behind dense terrain that enemy models without INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM/MOBILE cannot cross horizontally where a section is over 2″ tall. By 13.06 such models must climb (the vertical distance counts toward the move) and cannot end on non-ground surfaces of that feature; in this engine the segment is simply refused, so the moat is a hard wall. SUPER-HEAVY WALKERs cross sections up to 4″ and can gamble for MOBILE; FLY units that take to the skies ignore terrain.
entries.when_to_use: Against vehicle- or monster-heavy armies; when choosing which objective or area infantry should hold; when an enemy vehicle threat must path around a ruin.
entries.unit_types: INFANTRY, BEASTS, SWARM (the defenders).
entries.rules_basis: 13.06 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2163-2205); 24.35 (:3940-3966); 21.03 (:3358-3375); 13.06.01 commentary on Solid (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:518-520). entries.name: Box in an enemy transport to spoil its passengers' disembark
entries.description: Ring a loaded enemy transport with models standing just outside 2″ of it (not engaged with it). Disembarking units must be set up wholly within 3″ (rapid/tactical) and unengaged: after the transport makes a normal move they must use Rapid Disembark and cannot get out if there is no legal spot; if it has not moved and Tactical is impossible they are forced into Combat Disembark (6″, a hazard roll per model, battle-shocked, no charge, and only allowed to be engaged with units the transport is engaged with). If you then destroy the transport, Emergency Disembark sets them up within 6″ as close as possible — unengaged if possible, otherwise engaged (errata) — so models die only if they still cannot be placed: the ring now mainly forces them into engagement, battle-shocked and unable to charge, rather than killing them. By the rules the transport itself can drive through non-M/V models on its normal/advance move (not yet in the engine).
entries.when_to_use: A loaded enemy transport is near spare bodies of yours and stopping or degrading its passengers' disembark, charge or action next turn matters — or you plan to kill the transport this turn.
entries.unit_types: Cheap infantry, oval-based models, any units that can reach around the transport.
entries.rules_basis: 03.02 set up unengaged (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:491-512); 18.04 disembark modes (:3013-3058); 18.05 as amended by errata (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:609; launch text :3061-3078); 17.01 (:2867-2874). Corrected: the 18.05 errata removes most of core-rules#62's 'models that cannot be placed are destroyed' payoff.

entries.name: Bait or soak the enemy's one-shot reactions with a cheap unit first
entries.description: Each player can use the same stratagem only once per phase, and a snare fires once. Move an expendable unit first so it ends within 8″ of the enemy reactive unit (or on the snared objective): the enemy spends its once-per-phase reaction and CP (or the snare's D6 mortal wounds, after which the objective is no longer snared) on chaff, or its unit dodges off an objective or out of a firing position; then move the units that matter. Use it to pull a reactive unit off an objective you then take.
entries.when_to_use: The enemy has a reactive unit or snared objective that would spoil your main move, a cheap unit can reach the trigger first, and your main plan does not depend on that enemy unit staying put (it may move D6″).
entries.unit_types: Cheap fast units, chaff.
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (sequenced before the key moves)
entries.rules_basis: 15.01: a player cannot use the same stratagem more than once in the same phase (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2495-2500); triggers as in DEN-10 (space-marines/RULES.md:259, :625, :647, :714; custodes/RULES.md:156; orks/RULES.md:223, :268); RULINGS.md:402 (the snare is cleared whatever the roll; one unit triggers one snare).

entries.name: Block an engaged enemy's fall-back route (surround to trap)
entries.description: Move other units (more than 2″ away, or via charges and pile-ins) to close the escape directions of an enemy unit engaged with yours. An Ordered Retreat cannot move through your models, so the enemy must choose Desperate Escape — a hazard roll per model (1-2 = a mortal wound, 3 for all-M/V units) and then a battle-shock roll — or cannot fall back at all if no unengaged end position is reachable within M. Desperate Escape can always cross your models, so in 11e a trap taxes rather than seals.
entries.when_to_use: A valuable enemy unit is locked by your tarpit (DEN-15), its exits can be closed, and escaping would hand it shooting or scoring.
entries.unit_types: Any friendly units near an existing combat.
entries.move_type: Normal (adjacent: pile-in / consolidation wrap in the Fight phase)
entries.rules_basis: 09.07 fall-back modes; Desperate Escape models may be moved through enemy models (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1417-1440); 03.01 (:385-395); 06.03 hazard rolls (:1067-1073); 09.07.01 commentary (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:474).

entries.name: Pin the enemy with fall-back-punishing units
entries.description: Some units make falling back from them costly: Space Wolves Wulfen (Savage Frenzy) and Custodes Knight-Centura (Corner the Quarry) force engaged non-M/V enemies to use Desperate Escape (-1 to the hazard rolls if battle-shocked); Ork Nobz with Wimp-kickaz force it (-1 when riled up); Da Big Hunt's WHERE D'YA FINK YOU'RE GOING? forces it and gives M/V three extra hazard rolls per Beast Snagga unit; Shadowkeepers NO ESCAPE (2CP) lets an unengaged Custodes Infantry unit within 6″ charge a unit that fell back; Aquilan Shield RAPID REACTIONS lets the Custodes unit it fell back from shoot it. Move or charge these units into the enemy shooters and objective holders you most want held, and keep a NO ESCAPE unit within 6″ behind the lock. Mirror: do not plan to fall back from such enemy units.
entries.when_to_use: The enemy has a valuable shooter or objective holder that will want to fall back next turn and your punisher can reach it; for NO ESCAPE, a second Custodes Infantry unit within 6″.
entries.unit_types: Wulfen, Knight-Centura, Nobz (Wimp-kickaz), Beast Snagga (Da Big Hunt), Custodes Infantry (Shadowkeepers, Aquilan Shield).
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (toward the target to charge)
entries.rules_basis: 09.07 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1417-1440); 09.07.01 (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:474); .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:326 (Savage Frenzy), custodes/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:119 (Corner the Quarry), orks/RULES.md:151 (Wimp-kickaz), :110 (WHERE D'YA FINK YOU'RE GOING?), custodes/RULES.md:141 (NO ESCAPE), :211 (RAPID REACTIONS).

entries.name: Stand within 3″ of a fight to dictate the enemy's consolidation
entries.description: Leave a unit that has not fought within 3″ (but more than 2″) of where an enemy melee unit will be when the fighting ends — for example an enemy unit on an objective that your chargers are attacking. If it consolidates, the Engaging mode comes before the Objective mode, so it must move toward your unit rather than onto the objective, and if it engages your unit you get to fight it. Consolidation is optional, so the enemy may simply stay put, but it can no longer step onto the objective. Conversely, keep enemies more than 3″ from your own fighters that need Objective consolidation.
entries.when_to_use: An enemy fight next to a contested objective, in either player's Fight phase. Exceptions: Custodes rules that allow any mode (Unstoppable Destroyer) or force the objective mode (EMPEROR'S DOMAIN).
entries.unit_types: Any unit near an ongoing combat.
entries.rules_basis: 12.07-12.08 consolidation modes, mandatory and assessed in order (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1934-1985; Ongoing Consolidation errata, 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:492); pile-in and consolidation are optional (:1719-1730). Engine ConsolidationMove.gd:62-91 (incl. the Custodes overrides).

entries.engine_support: ConsolidationMove.select_mode (ConsolidationMove.gd:62-91) run for the enemy unit on a probe board; MissionManager.model_within_inches_of_objective (MissionManager.gd:569) for the 3″ objective test.
entries.value_reason: Narrow geometry and the enemy can decline to consolidate; useful mainly around contested objectives.

entries.name: Remove enemy tokens and markers by ending a move next to them
entries.description: Some enemy assets vanish when your units end moves near them. A Space Marine Teleport Homer token (it gives their Rapid Ingress -1CP and a set-up within 3″ of the token) is removed when one of your units ends a move within 1″ of it — do it during your Movement phase, before the end of the phase when their Rapid Ingress happens. Under Surveil the Foe, whenever your unit ends a move within range of an objective that has any of the opponent's operation markers within range, those markers are removed (the engine scrubs Smoke and Mirrors decoys whenever your unit is in range of a decoyed objective at the end of a turn). Send cheap units to sweep them.
entries.when_to_use: An enemy Teleport Homer token is within reach while their reserves can still arrive (rounds 1-3); you hold Surveil the Foe, or the opponent's Smoke and Mirrors decoys are scoring.
entries.unit_types: Cheap fast units, units already nearby.
entries.rules_basis: Teleport Homer datasheet text (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:108: ‘If an enemy unit ends a move within 1″ of that Teleport Homer token, that Teleport Homer token is removed from the battlefield’); RULINGS.md:502 (engine: removed when an enemy model is within 1″, checked at every phase change); 40k/data/40kdc/missionCards.json surveil-the-foe :1757 (text :1867), smoke-and-mirrors :1100; MissionManager.gd:1849-1864 (decoy scrub, both players, approximating 'ends a move within range').

entries.name: Spread a picket net of Hidden infantry across separate terrain pieces
entries.description: Instead of stacking small Hidden-capable infantry on objectives, post them in separate light/dense terrain areas along the enemy's approach routes. Hidden, they are only visible to enemies within their 15″ detection range (3″ less when gone to ground behind dense terrain), so they are hard to remove; their 8″ bubbles add deep-strike denial (DEN-01), they deny those areas to enemy staging (DEN-06), and they threaten isolated units moving in. Shooting ends Hidden for that turn and the next, so pick shots carefully.
entries.when_to_use: Several small Hidden-capable infantry units (Phobos, Scouts and similar), an enemy that must cross the board, and other units holding the objectives.
entries.unit_types: Small elite or cheap infantry (Phobos, Scouts).
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (adjacent: Scout move, Infiltrators deployment)
entries.rules_basis: 13.09 Hidden, amended to light/dense (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:529; 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2292-2303); 13.11.01 gone to ground -3″ detection (errata doc :535-539); 20.04/24.09 more than 8″ (:3255-3274, :3649-3661). Corrected: light terrain now qualifies, and shooting forfeits Hidden for two turns, so 'picking off' enemies trades against staying Hidden.

entries.value_reason: Real but niche (needs several Hidden-capable units) and largely covered by DEN-01 and DEN-06.

entries.name: Hold ground inside enemy charge reach with a Fights First unit (corrected premise)
entries.description: The raw idea was to stand a Fights First unit (Custodes under Heralds of the Throne, a Judiciar's Tempormortis, objective-gated TRANSHUMAN SWIFTNESS / INDOMITABLE GUARDIANS) in front of enemy melee so it 'strikes first if charged'. In 11e that premise is wrong: every unit that makes a charge move has Fights First until the end of the turn, and the player whose turn it is starts the Fights First alternation, so the charger still swings first. What remains: your Fights First unit fights right after the first enemy Fights First unit instead of after all of them (it matters when several enemy units charge in one phase), and COUNTEROFFENSIVE (2CP) gives the same timing. Use it to hold an objective or bait a charge with a unit that hits back hard, not to pre-empt the charger.
entries.when_to_use: Your defender is a strong Fights First melee unit, several enemy units are likely to charge into the area, and holding the objective matters.
entries.unit_types: Custodes (Emissaries Imperatus), a Judiciar and its unit, Space Marines/Custodes with objective-gated Fights First.
entries.rules_basis: 11.04 AFTER MOVING: each model has Fights First (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1663-1665); 12.04 Fights First combats start with the player whose turn it is and alternate (:1830-1850); 24.13 (:3736-3744); 15.12 COUNTEROFFENSIVE (:2770-2782); .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/custodes/RULES.md:195 (Heralds of the Throne). Engine: ChargePhase.gd:1458-1466 (a charge grants flags.fights_first), FightSequencer.gd:4-20, :91-101. Corrected: factions#43 said charging does not grant Fights First.
evidence: 40k/phases/ChargePhase.gd:1458-1466 (“Mark unit as charged and grant Fights First”)

entries.engine_support: FightSequencer.is_fights_first (FightSequencer.gd:91-101) and next_selection to simulate the order; _estimate_melee_damage (AIDecisionMaker.gd:19576) and _estimate_incoming_melee_damage (:12350).
entries.value_reason: The genuine 11e payoff is small; it is only worth it in multi-charge situations.

entries.name: Converge several units on one priority target
entries.description: Move two or more units so their weapon ranges or charge reach overlap on the same priority enemy, with enough combined expected damage to remove it this turn, instead of each unit choosing its own target. This includes adding a fresh charger to a combat that is already going on and finishing a wounded objective holder or lane blocker: a one-model survivor still scores its OC and still blocks movement.
entries.when_to_use: A high-value enemy (objective holder, character, dangerous shooter, screen blocking a lane) needs more damage than any one unit can deal; a wounded enemy still holds an objective the VP estimator values; or a combat is stalemated and a second charger would end it. Skip when the combined kill chance stays low or the meeting point is inside an enemy kill zone.
entries.unit_types: All shooting and melee units (each charger must be within 12″ of the target to declare)
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (Advance only for assault shooters or units allowed to charge after advancing)
entries.rules_basis: 04.02: each weapon picks its own target, which must be visible, within range and unengaged (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:628-645). 14.02: level of control adds up the OC of every model in range, so one survivor keeps control (:2401-2416). 11.02: each unit declares its own charge (within 12″, not engaged, no advance or fall-back move) (:1612-1622). 11.04: several charge targets are allowed and chargers gain Fights First (:1640-1665).

In movement, charge_intent picks one target per unit with no kill-sufficiency or shared-target term (3830-3912), shooting_lanes only lists enemies already in range (3914-3940), and melee seekers chase the nearest enemy (B11, 2947-3099).

entries.value_reason: It applies to every army in most turns, it is a confirmed corpus principle (F010), and movement has no convergence term, so damage spreads over targets that survive and keep scoring.

entries.name: Stay inside friendly buff auras and place the aura source to cover the most units
entries.description: End the beneficiaries' moves inside a friendly aura (or a 'within X″ of a CHARACTER' ability range), and move the aura source last so it covers the most valuable units at the moment the buff is used. In-engine sources: Ghazghkull's Prophet of da Great Waaagh! (ORKS within 6″: +1 to hit and +1 to wound in melee), Beastboss on Squigosaur's Thundering Stampede (+1 to charge), Venerable Dreadnought's Fervour of the Ancients (+1 to advance and charge within 6″) and Wisdom of the Ancients, Guilliman, Trajann's Captain-General (6″), Murderfang, Psychic Null, and OC auras (Curse of the Wulfen and Hunting Hounds near a SPACE WOLVES CHARACTER).
entries.when_to_use: The beneficiary will shoot, charge, advance or fight this turn or next, and can end inside the bubble without dropping its objective or role. Advance and charge auras must cover the unit when the roll is made, so it must be inside at the end of its own move: move beneficiaries first and the source last, or plan them together. Discount it when clustering exposes the source or invites area attacks. Embarked or reserve sources give nothing, because they are not on the battlefield.
entries.unit_types: Unattached aura characters and walkers (Ghazghkull, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Venerable Dreadnought, Guilliman, Trajann, Murderfang, Anathema Psykana units, Rhino Primaris), and the ORKS / SPACE WOLVES / ADEPTUS ASTARTES / CUSTODES units they buff
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (beneficiaries and source); Remain Stationary when already covered
entries.rules_basis: 22.01 Aura abilities: they affect units within the stated range, the source is always within its own aura, and the same aura applies only once (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3407-3416). 01.04.01: a model is within a distance if any part of its base is, and a unit is within it if one of its models is (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:79-81). 01.02.04 and the 18.02 FAQ: embarked and reserve units are not on the battlefield, so their abilities cannot measure (errata_faq:34-36, 617-620). Datasheet texts: Prophet of da Great Waaagh! (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:34), Fervour of the Ancients (space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:730).

entries.errata_note: An advance roll is made before the unit moves (core 09.06 'BEFORE MOVING'; FAQ 21.03 has take to the skies declared when the unit is selected, before that roll), so a +1-to-advance aura must already cover the beneficiary when it is selected to move: move or place the source first. Only charge auras, rolled in the Charge phase, reward moving the beneficiaries first and the source last. — Core 09.06 Advance Move (Before Moving); FAQ 21.03 Flying Models (errata_faq:681-682)

entries.name: Secure an objective at the end of your Movement phase, then move on
entries.description: With a securing ability, end the Movement phase controlling an objective so that it is secured (14.03). Next turn, release the unit for another job: the objective stays yours until the enemy's level of control is greater than yours at the end of a phase. Prefer objectives the enemy cannot easily out-OC.
entries.when_to_use: The unit has Thievin' Scavengers (Gretchin) or Raise the Banner (Bladeguard Ancient, Ancient in Terminator Armour), or a securing stratagem such as DUBIOUS RESTRAINT or VIGILANCE ETERNAL is affordable. The objective is away from enemy OC, and the army has more objectives to cover than bodies. Next turn, leave a secured objective for an unsecured one rather than sitting on it.
entries.unit_types: Gretchin (Thievin' Scavengers), Bladeguard Ancient and Ancient in Terminator Armour (Raise the Banner), Taktikal Brigade Boyz / Kommandos / Stormboyz (DUBIOUS RESTRAINT), Custodes and Space Marine stratagem targets
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance onto the objective this turn (securing is not an action, so an Advance is fine); Normal / Advance away next turn
entries.rules_basis: 14.03 Secured Objectives (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2427-2433). 14.03 FAQ: a unit that took control at the end of your Movement phase can secure that objective with its ability (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:561-562). 14.02 tie rule for secured objectives (:2410-2416). DUBIOUS RESTRAINT: 'Start/end of your Movement phase ... Select one objective your unit is controlling. That objective is secured.' (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/RULES.md:191).

New queries: which units carry a securing trigger and when it fires; and a capture-candidate bonus for keeping the objective without a keeper next turn, with FIX_SECURED_AWARE on so the plan then frees the securer.

entries.name: Fall back to free the enemy for your guns and fresh chargers
entries.description: Make an Ordered Retreat with an engaged unit so the enemy it was holding becomes a legal ranged target for the rest of the army, and so a fresh unit can charge it and gain Fights First. The unit that fell back gives up its own shooting, charge and actions this turn.
entries.when_to_use: The damage friendly shooters and chargers can do to the freed enemy this turn is worth more than keeping it locked plus the falling-back unit's own lost turn. It pays most when the enemy is not a MONSTER/VEHICLE (an engaged M/V can already be shot at -1 to hit) and the friendly engaged unit is cheap or losing.
entries.unit_types: Any engaged friendly unit (Ordered Retreat needs it not battle-shocked); the payoff comes from other friendly shooters and melee units
entries.rules_basis: 04.02: ranged targets must be unengaged (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:639-644). 17.03: an engaged MONSTER/VEHICLE can still be targeted, at -1 to hit (:2898-2910; errata excludes [BLAST], 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:608). 09.07: after a fall-back move the unit cannot shoot, declare a charge or start an action, and Ordered Retreat is only for units that are not battle-shocked (:1417-1442). 11.04: chargers gain Fights First (:1661-1665).

It falls back by default when off an objective (12093-12157), which frees the target only by accident, and it holds on an objective when winning or tied on OC (12050-12090) even when the army could kill the locked enemy.
entries.engine_support: _estimate_unit_ranged_strength (25866), _estimate_melee_damage (19576), and shooting_lanes / charge_intent from _build_phase_plan (3773) to count friendly units that could engage the freed enemy; RulesEngine.get_eligible_targets (RulesEngine.gd:7137) on a board copy with the friendly unit moved away. New query: friendly expected damage on enemy E if E were unengaged, added as a fall-back bonus in _decide_engaged_unit.
entries.value_reason: An engaged-unit decision comes up most turns in melee matchups, the swing (the whole army's shooting on the freed unit versus one locked enemy) is large, and the AI already has the decision point to hang the term on.

entries.name: Stage the Orks for one coordinated Waaagh! turn
entries.description: In the turn before calling the War Cry, move several Ork units so that next turn, once riled up (5+ invulnerable save, ranged [ASSAULT], an Advance does not stop a charge), as many as possible are within M + re-rolled Advance + 2D6 of worthwhile targets at the same time. Do not call it just because one unit can reach something. This entry was added by the bucket editor from the bucket definition ('faction triggers such as Waaagh!').
entries.when_to_use: Orks with the War Cry still unused: position in rounds 1-2 for a call in round 2-3 (F020: not turn one, not the moment one unit can reach something). Hold faster units back so they arrive with the slow ones. Also consider calling it when the army must cross open ground, because the 5+ invulnerable save is worth it on its own.

entries.coverage_detail: The Command-phase call (AIDecisionMaker.gd:6364-6420) always calls from round 2, or in round 1 if any single unit is within about 22″ of an enemy. It counts units in range but never moves units into range together, and movement has no Waaagh! staging term. WAAAGH_MIN_UNITS_IN_RANGE from profiles/orks.json is not read by the AI (grep finds 0 hits), and that profile is not shipped (40k/data/ai_profiles holds only baseline_2026_08.json).

entries.name: End your move in range of the friendly unit your support ability should target
entries.description: Plan the support model's move, and the order of moves, so a 'select one friendly unit within X″' ability lands on the best recipient: un-shock and rile up another Ork unit, repair a damaged vehicle, hand out a doctrine, or heal infantry. Riling a unit before it moves lets it Advance and still charge.
entries.when_to_use: A friendly unit is battle-shocked (OC '-', cannot be targeted by its own stratagems) or is about to Advance and charge; a damaged vehicle is about to shoot or fight; or a unit needs a doctrine this turn. Use the start-of-move window when the recipient is already in range and the end-of-move window when the support model must close in first. Move the support model before the recipient.
entries.unit_types: Warboss, Warboss in Mega Armour, Nazdreg (Intimidating Motivation, 6″); Beastboss (Keep Huntin'!); Deffkilla Wartrike (Get Back in da Race!); Mek (Clever Know-wotz, 3″); Rukkatrukk (Delicious Eating Squigs, 3″); Techmarine, Iron Priest, Iron Father Feirros (3″ repair); Marneus Calgar (9″); Guilliman (12″); Chaplain (6″); Gauntlet Captain (Damocles-class Uplink, 6″ of the transport); Custodes Inspirational Exemplar (9″)
entries.move_type: Normal (support model, at the start or end of its move), sequenced before the recipient's move
entries.rules_basis: Intimidating Motivation (once per battle round, per army): 'In your Movement phase, at the start or end of this unit's move, you can select one friendly ORKS unit within 6″ of this unit. That unit: is no longer battle-shocked; is riled up until the start of your next turn.' (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:7). Riled-up effects come from the Waaagh! army rule (orks/RULES.md:76). 01.07: a battle-shocked unit has OC '-', cannot be targeted by its own player's stratagems and cannot start actions (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:212-220). 01.04.01 'within' (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:79-81).

entries.name: Move as a mutually supporting group; do not arrive piecemeal
entries.description: Keep units within support range of each other (overlapping fire, counter-charge reach, shared auras), and time arrivals so several units reach a contested area in the same turn. Hold fast units back rather than letting them arrive alone. At plan level: overload one flank and refuse the other.
entries.when_to_use: Elite armies with few units (Custodes), any army attacking a defended area, or whenever the lead unit would be alone inside enemy threat range this turn. Relax it in rounds 4-5 and when cards pay for spreading out (table quarters, No Man's Land counts).
entries.unit_types: All; especially elite bricks and fast units that race ahead
entries.rules_basis: A tactical principle; the rules it relies on are 15.11 Heroic Intervention reach (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2734-2766) and 22.01 auras (:3407-3416).

entries.name: Park a Heroic Intervention umbrella
entries.description: End your Movement phase with an unengaged melee unit (not battle-shocked; a VEHICLE only if it is a CHARACTER or WALKER) placed so that enemies likely to charge your objective holders or gunline end within its reach. Leap to Defend charges only units that made a charge move, within the 2D6 roll; Into the Fray (+1CP) charges any enemy within 6″, with the roll capped at 6. The same unit also threatens a counter-charge in your next turn.
entries.when_to_use: The opponent's melee threats are approaching your objective holders or gunline, you will have 1CP (2CP for Into the Fray) in their turn, and the counter-punch unit is unlikely to be shot off or charged first. A unit that rapid-disembarked this turn cannot be the target.
entries.unit_types: Melee units; VEHICLES only if CHARACTER or WALKER
entries.move_type: Normal / Remain Stationary in your own Movement phase; the payoff is adjacent (15.11, end of the opponent's Charge phase)
entries.rules_basis: 15.11: target one friendly unengaged unit within 12″ of one or more enemy units; a VEHICLE only if CHARACTER/WALKER; Leap to Defend targets only units that made a charge move this phase; Into the Fray (+1CP) caps the roll at 6 and allows any enemy within 6″ (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2734-2766). 15.01 FAQ: Into the Fray costs 2CP (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:576-577). 01.07: a battle-shocked unit cannot be targeted by its own player's stratagems (:212-220). FAQ: a unit that used rapid disembark this turn cannot be targeted with Heroic Intervention (errata_faq:610-611).

entries.name: Post an Overwatch picket over the enemy's approach
entries.description: End your Movement phase with an unengaged, non-TITANIC high-volume or [TORRENT] shooter that has sight lines, within 24″, over the lanes and objectives the enemy must move into. At the end of the opponent's Movement phase it can Fire Overwatch (1CP; snap shooting at one visible, unengaged enemy within 24″, hitting only on unmodified 6s).
entries.when_to_use: The opponent must cross open ground to reach objectives or to charge, you will have 1CP in their turn, and the shooter does not rely on staying Hidden (firing removes Hidden for that turn and your next).
entries.unit_types: High shot-volume and [TORRENT] units (not TITANIC)
entries.rules_basis: 15.08 Fire Overwatch: end of the opponent's Movement phase, one friendly unengaged unit excluding TITANIC units (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2735-2748). 15.09 snap shooting: one visible enemy within 24″, unmodified 6s only, no hit re-rolls (:2749-2768). 15.01: the same stratagem once per phase (:2495-2499). 13.09: ranged attacks this turn or last remove Hidden (:2292-2303). How [TORRENT] (24.37, :3956-3962) interacts with 15.09's 'only hits on an unmodified 6' is not settled locally (unverified).

entries.errata_note: Fire Overwatch is resolved at the end of the opponent's Movement phase, so only where enemies end their moves matters: INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM models that end in a terrain area containing light or dense features (such as many terrain objectives) and did not shoot this turn or last are hidden and can only be seen from within 15″, or 12″ once they have Gone to Ground behind dense features, so the picket must be that close to those areas, not merely within 24″. FAQ 05.01 also restates that, unless a rule says otherwise, snap-shooting attacks only hit on a roll of 6; it does not name [TORRENT], but it points to [TORRENT] weapons not auto-hitting in Overwatch. — 13.09 errata (errata_faq:529); Commentary 13.11.01 Gone to Ground (:539); FAQ 05.01 Hit Roll (:344-347)

entries.name: Send OC-light or expendable units to positional cards; keep OC for objectives and actions
entries.description: Positional cards (Behind Enemy Lines, Display of Might, Centre Ground, Outflank, Engage on All Fronts) count units regardless of OC. Assign OC-0 and low-OC units, Lone Operatives and cheap units to those positions, and keep high-OC units for objectives and actions, which need OC 1+.
entries.when_to_use: Every turn in which positional and objective cards compete for the same units. Lone Operatives suit end-of-opponent's-turn positions, since they cannot be seen from beyond 12″.
entries.unit_types: OC-0 characters and vehicles, Lone Operatives and chaff for positional jobs; OC units for objectives and actions
entries.rules_basis: Card texts count 'friendly units (excluding AIRCRAFT and battle-shocked units)' (40k/data/40kdc/missionCards.json: display-of-might :2246, centre-ground :2311, outflank :2339, engage-on-all-fronts :2417, behind-enemy-lines :2679). 16.01: a unit with OC 0 or '-' cannot start an action (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2806-2814). 24.24 Lone Operative (:3813-3830). 23.02 AIRCRAFT movement (:3503-3515).

RI-QUARTER skips battle-shocked and AIRCRAFT units (_ri_quarter_vp 12894-12900).

entries.name: Re-task battle-shocked units as bodies, not scorers
entries.description: A battle-shocked unit has OC '-', cannot be targeted by its own player's stratagems, cannot start or complete actions, does not count for most positional cards, and must Desperate Escape if it falls back. Move it to jobs that need only bodies (move blocks, charge screens, deep-strike denial) or to safety, and hand its scoring job to another unit.
entries.when_to_use: After a failed battle-shock roll, a combat disembark or a Desperate Escape; also for units at or below half strength, which will test in the next Command phase.
entries.unit_types: Battle-shocked units, or units likely to become battle-shocked
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (a Fall Back would be a forced Desperate Escape)
entries.rules_basis: 01.07 battle-shocked effects (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:212-220). 08.03: a unit stays battle-shocked until it passes a roll, and units at or below half strength must roll (:1244-1256). 09.07: Desperate Escape is mandatory when battle-shocked (:1423-1426). Card exclusions 'excluding AIRCRAFT and battle-shocked units' (40k/data/40kdc/missionCards.json, e.g. behind-enemy-lines :2679).

New query: a role filter that moves battle-shocked units from capture and positional candidates to screen and block candidates and raises their screen score.
entries.value_reason: Battle-shock happens often in 11e and a shocked unit has no scoring value, so moving it onto body jobs is pure gain, but the AI already zeroes its OC.
absorbed: OBJ-18 (Use battle-shocked units as bodies, not scorers)
entries.errata_note: Per FAQ 01.07 (repeated under 16.01), a unit with a rule that lets it start actions while battle-shocked (e.g. Custodes readied with Conservai Ka'tah) can carry on with an action it started even if it becomes battle-shocked afterwards. Also count an emergency disembark as a battle-shock source (18.05): under the 18.05 errata, models that cannot be set up unengaged are now set up engaged instead of destroyed, so those battle-shocked survivors can only leave combat by a Desperate Escape. — FAQ 01.07 Battle-shock Rolls (errata_faq:141-142; repeated as FAQ 16.01 Performing Actions :593-594); 18.05 errata Emergency Disembark Move (:609)

entries.name: Pick destinations that satisfy several cards at once and split conflicting geometry
entries.description: Score each destination by the sum of the card values it satisfies: an enemy-side expansion objective can count for Forward Position, Determined Acquisition, Secure No Man's Land, Display of Might, an uncovered quarter and a flank edge at once. Also detect conflicting geometry, so different units take each side: Centre Ground needs a unit within 3″ of the centre, while quarter presence needs one more than 6″ from it, and an action actor cannot shoot while the holder keeps OC.
entries.when_to_use: Two or more cards are active; it is always worth computing.
entries.unit_types: All
entries.rules_basis: Card geometries in 40k/data/40kdc/missionCards.json (centre-ground :2311 'within 3 inches of the centre of the battlefield'; engage-on-all-fronts :2417 'wholly within it and not within 6 inches of the centre'). 01.04.05 table quarters (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:95-97). Mission zones in docs/rules/11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md.
evidence: 40k/data/40kdc/missionCards.json (centre-ground, engage-on-all-fronts, outflank, display-of-might, behind-enemy-lines texts)

entries.coverage_detail: Secondary terms are additive per objective destination (AIDecisionMaker.gd:10378-10499), alongside primary terms (10351-10376) and RI-QUARTER VP (12894-12940), so an objective that serves several cards already scores higher. But only objectives are candidates (B06), the enemy-zone centre is hard-coded to Search and Destroy corners (10394-10400), and no conflict check splits incompatible geometry across units.
entries.engine_support: _get_secondary_awareness (AIDecisionMaker.gd:24239), _get_table_quarter and _get_covered_quarters (24250, 24260), _get_deployment_zone_polygon_pixels (24856). New queries: destination candidates that are not objectives (zone, quarter, edge and centre points), scored by the sum of card predicates; and a pairwise conflict check between the card roles assigned to units.
entries.value_reason: Multi-card destinations are common and cheap to score, but most of the value is already captured by the additive objective terms.

entries.name: Push battle-shock and OC-debuff abilities onto enemy objective holders
entries.description: Move units whose abilities force battle-shock rolls or cut OC so the enemy's objective holders are inside range at the moment the ability applies, stripping their OC and setting up flips, precision kills and charges. In-engine examples: Custodes Creeping Dread (enemy PSYKER or below-starting-strength units within 12″ of an ANATHEMA PSYKANA model roll battle-shock at -1 in the opponent's Command phase), Reivers' Terror Troops (-1 OC for enemy models within 3″), and Lord of the Pyroclasts (-1 OC for the enemy engaged with his unit). The Tyranid and Death Guard examples in the corpus are factions this engine does not implement.
entries.when_to_use: Enemy holders have low Leadership, are below half strength or are PSYKERs, and the ability's range can be reached without being charged first. Time it before the scoring check (for example the end of your turn, for a test in the opponent's Command phase).
entries.unit_types: Anathema Psykana units (Null Maiden Vigil), Reiver Squads, Adrax Agatone; Tyranid synapse / Neurolictor and Death Guard aura units in other factions
entries.rules_basis: 01.07: a battle-shocked unit's OC becomes '-' (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:212-220). 08.03: units that are battle-shocked or at or below half strength roll in the Battle-shock step (:1244-1256). 14.02 level of control (:2401-2416). Creeping Dread ruling: .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/RULINGS.md:75.

entries.name: Stay engaged on purpose
entries.description: Remain stationary while engaged when staying is worth more than falling back. While engaged the unit cannot be shot by other enemies (unless it is a MONSTER/VEHICLE), it keeps a dangerous enemy shooter locked out of normal shooting and actions, a MONSTER/VEHICLE keeps shooting with close-quarters shooting, and a battle-shocked unit avoids the forced Desperate Escape.
entries.when_to_use: The unit will survive the Fight phase and is pinning something valuable (a lock-target shooter, an objective holder); falling back would cost shooting, actions or hazard rolls; or it is a MONSTER/VEHICLE with good guns.
entries.unit_types: Engaged units, especially tar-pits and MONSTER/VEHICLE units
entries.rules_basis: 04.02: targets must be unengaged (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:639-644). 10.06 close-quarters shooting: MONSTER/VEHICLE units can shoot while engaged, at -1 to hit except [CLOSE-QUARTERS] weapons against units they are engaged with (:1522-1547). 17.03 (:2898-2910; errata excludes [BLAST], 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:608). 09.07 (:1417-1442). 16.01: engaged units cannot start actions (:2810).

entries.name: Screen a key friendly with a SMOKE or cover-granting unit
entries.description: Move a SMOKE unit, or a Speed Freeks unit with Smoky Gubbinz, between the main enemy firing lanes and a key friendly unit, so the friend is not fully visible because of its models. Smokescreen (1CP, at the start of the opponent's Shooting phase) then gives the SMOKE unit and every unit it partly screens the benefit of cover: the attacker's BS is worsened by 1. This is the bucket's 'LoS-blocking for friends'.
entries.when_to_use: A key friendly unit must stand in or cross open ground inside enemy range, a SMOKE unit (not battle-shocked) and 1CP are available, or a Smoky Gubbinz unit can stand between them without becoming the easier target itself.
entries.unit_types: SMOKE units (in shipped lists: Kommandos, Infiltrator Squads, Land Raiders, Venerable Dreadnoughts, Wolf Scouts); Speed Freeks with Smoky Gubbinz (the Deffkilla Wartrike in recon_stomps.json); the units sheltering behind them
entries.rules_basis: 15.10 Smokescreen: until the end of the phase, each attack that targets your SMOKE unit, or a unit that is not fully visible to the attacking model because of one or more models in your SMOKE unit, has the target in cover (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2714-2731). 13.08: cover worsens the attack's BS by 1 (:2280-2290). 06.01: when drawing line of sight, only models in the observing unit and the observed unit are ignored, so other units' models can block it; ordinary models still give no cover unless a rule such as Smokescreen or Smoky Gubbinz says so (:1024-1033). Correction: first-principles#78 said ordinary models do not block line of sight in 11e; 06.01 says they can.
evidence: 40k/autoloads/StratagemManager.gd:5101-5108 (smokescreen_11e has covers_screened: true) and :1918-1927 (cover is applied to the SMOKE unit only; grep shows covers_screened is never read)

entries.name: End a Normal move within range of a proximity-damage ability
entries.description: Choose a Normal move (not an Advance) that ends with line of sight to a valuable target inside the trigger radius of a proximity-damage ability, often a target your guns cannot reach: EXPLOSIVES (8″, six D6, each 4+ is a mortal wound), Bomb Squigs (when the unit ends a normal move, a visible enemy within 12″ takes D3 mortal wounds on a 3+), Haywire Mine (6″), Neutronium Cascade Mine (3″).
entries.when_to_use: A high-value or damaged target is within 12″ (Bomb Squigs), 8″ (EXPLOSIVES, which needs an unengaged and visible target), 6″ (Haywire) or 3″ (Neutronium) of an end position that is safe enough; uses or CP remain; and the unit's main job does not need an Advance.
entries.unit_types: Any EXPLOSIVES/GRENADES unit; Tankbustas, Breaka Boyz, Kommandos, Squighog Boyz (Bomb Squigs); Incursors, Wolf Scouts (Haywire Mine); Venatari with Verutum Lances (Neutronium)
entries.move_type: Normal (an Advance forfeits EXPLOSIVES and Bomb Squigs)
entries.rules_basis: 15.05 EXPLOSIVES: your Shooting phase; one unengaged EXPLOSIVES/GRENADES unit that is eligible to shoot and did not advance; one unengaged enemy unit within 8″ of and visible to the chosen model; six D6, each 4+ is 1 mortal wound (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2651-2667). 15.01 errata: the Grenade stratagem is the same as Explosives (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:568). Bomb Squigs: once per turn and twice per battle, triggered when the unit ends a normal move (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/ork_abilities_audit.md:32). Haywire Mine (space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:376); Neutronium Cascade Mine (custodes/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:139).

entries.name: Clear lanes and sequence your own moves
entries.description: Order the army's moves so units do not block each other: move units out of corridors others need, let fast units through gaps before screens close, move transports and their cargo in the right order, and move screens last when they must seal around others. In 11e friendly models never block movement (only end positions cannot overlap), but this engine still blocks paths through friendly MONSTER/VEHICLE bases, so lane order matters most around friendly vehicles.
entries.when_to_use: Congested deployment zones and corridors, and armies that mix vehicles with infantry (Ork Battlewagons and Trukks); also whenever a screen must close a gap other units are using.
entries.unit_types: All
entries.move_type: other (move ordering for Normal / Advance / Disembark)
entries.rules_basis: 03.01: a model can be moved through friendly models, its base cannot be moved through enemy models, and no model may end on another model (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:386-416). 17.01 FAQ: a MONSTER/VEHICLE unit can move through friendly units on any move type (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:596-599). Correction: first-principles#76 left the friendly MONSTER/VEHICLE block as possibly 11e. Local 11e text lets every model move through friendly models; the engine block is a 10e carry-over.
evidence: 40k/phases/MovementPhase.gd:764-770, 898-903 ('10e Errata: Cannot move across MONSTER or VEHICLE models (friendly or enemy)') and 7477-7531

40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:15944-15957 comment: the friendly Battlewagon block was 'the single largest movement-staging failure in the benchmark: 50 in one 4-round game, 23 of 25 against the Battlewagon'
40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:14508 (the AI mirrors the block; FLY units are exempt)
entries.coverage_detail: Move order is fixed: engaged units first, then units that disembarked this phase, then normal units, with transport vehicles last, each tier front-to-back by board y (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7119-7147; _move_tier 7657-7665). The placement ladder retries collisions (B38, 14520-14722). The order is not intent-aware (screens are not moved last, lanes are not cleared for a specific unit) and it assumes a vertical layout with P1 at the top and P2 at the bottom.
entries.engine_support: _move_tier and _build_move_order (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7657, 7666); _path_crosses_monster_vehicle (15957). New query: a dependency order built from whether unit A's planned path or end spot overlaps unit B's current or planned footprint. Engine fix worth more than the AI change: let models pass friendly MONSTER/VEHICLE bases (03.01, 17.01 FAQ) at MovementPhase.gd:764-770 and 898-903, and drop the mirror at AIDecisionMaker.gd:14508.
entries.value_reason: The friendly-vehicle block is the largest recorded source of staging failures, but the main fix belongs in the engine; after it, sequencing matters only for end spots and screens.

entries.name: End the Movement phase Hidden to arm hidden-gated rules
entries.description: Some rules pay off only if the unit is hidden at a set moment: Vanguard Ambushers (a PHOBOS unit hidden at the end of your Movement phase re-rolls wound rolls of 1 this turn), STRIKE FROM THE SHADOWS (+1 S and [LETHAL HITS] when a hidden PHOBOS unit attacks), Kunnin' Infiltrator (if every model is hidden and unengaged at the end of the opponent's Fight phase, the unit can go to strategic reserves) and Shadow Masters (shooting does not break Hidden). End in a light or dense terrain area even when no enemy is within detection range.
entries.when_to_use: PHOBOS units that will attack this turn and can reach a light or dense terrain area; Boss Snikrot whenever he is not committed to a charge; any unit whose next activation depends on being hidden.
entries.unit_types: PHOBOS units (Infiltrators, Incursors, Eliminators, Reivers, Phobos characters), Scout Squads, Boss Snikrot
entries.rules_basis: 13.09 Hidden: INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM within a terrain area that contains light or dense features (errata, 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:529) whose unit made no ranged attacks this turn or the previous turn (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2292-2303); a unit is hidden only while every alive model is (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/RULINGS.md:357). Texts: Vanguard Ambushers, STRIKE FROM THE SHADOWS and Shadow Masters (space-marines/RULES.md:641, :626, :619); Kunnin' Infiltrator (orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:51).

The Hidden-seeking term ships at WEIGHT_HIDDEN_GAINED = 0.0 (AIDecisionMaker.gd:2633; term at 10306-10314) and is not tied to these abilities. Kunnin' Infiltrator is cancelled (6792-6801), and Shadow Masters takes 'stay hidden' only if the unit already stands where it can be hidden (SMDetachmentsA.gd:1053-1054).
entries.engine_support: TerrainManager.is_model_hidden (TerrainManager.gd:1001, errata-aware); _position_would_be_hidden and _hidden_gain_value (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28515, 28578). New query: per unit, the value of the hidden-gated abilities it holds this turn, added to the hidden bonus at destinations where every model would be hidden.
entries.value_reason: It gives a concrete, rules-backed payoff to the Hidden term the AI already has but ships switched off; it matters for Phobos-heavy Space Marine lists and Snikrot.
entries.skeptic_note: 'A unit is hidden only while every alive model is' (RULINGS.md:357) contradicts official commentary 01.02.07, Describing Units: a descriptor applies to a unit if at least one of its models meets it, and 'A hidden unit would be a unit that has a model in it that is hidden' (errata_faq:49). So Vanguard Ambushers ('if a friendly Phobos unit is hidden', SM RULES.md:641) and STRIKE FROM THE SHADOWS ('friendly hidden Phobos unit', :626) need only one hidden model. Only Kunnin' Infiltrator explicitly needs 'each model in this unit is hidden' (orks Datasheets_abilities.csv:51). The light/dense errata citation is correct. — 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:49, 529; space-marines/RULES.md:626, 641; orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:51
entries.errata_note: Per Commentary 01.02.07 a unit is hidden if at least one of its models is hidden, so Vanguard Ambushers and STRIKE FROM THE SHADOWS need only one hidden model (the RULINGS.md 'every alive model' reading is wrong); only Kunnin' Infiltrator, which says 'each model in this unit is hidden', needs all of them. Shadow Masters keeps a unit hidden after it shoots, but that unit cannot Go to Ground (Commentary 13.11.01 designer's note). — Commentary 01.02.07 Describing Units (errata_faq:49); Commentary 13.11.01 Gone to Ground (:539)

entries.name: Take to the skies with FLY units to hop terrain and screens
entries.description: Declare 'take to the skies' for a FLY unit's normal, advance, fall-back or charge move. Its maximum distance drops by 2″ (none with HOVER), but it ignores vertical distance and can move through all models and every category of terrain. Use it to cross dense ruins, reach upper floors, or hop a screen to reach an objective or target behind it.
entries.when_to_use: The direct path is blocked by dense terrain or models and the detour costs more than 2″; or a vertical climb or upper-level end spot is needed. Declare it before rolling for an Advance or charge.
entries.unit_types: FLY units (jump packs, Deffkoptas, Stormboyz, jetbikes, skimmers, flying monsters); HOVER units pay no distance
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance / Fall Back / Charge with take to the skies declared
entries.rules_basis: 21.03 Flying models: declared before moving; -2″ to the maximum distance; vertical distance ignored; can move through all types of model and all categories of terrain feature (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3358-3376). 24.17 HOVER: no -2″ (:3771-3780). 21.03 FAQ: declare before rolling for an Advance or charge (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:679-682). FAQ: vertical movement while taking to the skies does not count for [HEAVY] (errata_faq:704-705).

entries.name: Drive MONSTER/VEHICLE models straight through enemy infantry screens
entries.description: On normal and advance moves, MONSTER/VEHICLE models can be moved through friendly and enemy models that are not themselves MONSTER/VEHICLE models, so chaff screens do not stop a tank or monster from reaching its objective or firing spot. It still cannot end on a model or end engaged. Charges and fall-backs get no pass-through.
entries.when_to_use: An enemy infantry screen stands between a vehicle or monster and its objective, firing position or blocking spot, and the far side is reachable within M while ending more than 2″ from enemies.
entries.unit_types: MONSTER, VEHICLE
entries.rules_basis: 17.01: 'Each time you make a normal or advance move with a unit, MONSTER/VEHICLE models in that unit can be moved through friendly and enemy models (excluding other MONSTER/VEHICLE models)' (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2869-2874). 13.06: dense sections over 2″ still stop non-INFANTRY models moving horizontally (:2161-2180). 09.05: the unit must end unengaged (:1390-1398).
evidence: 40k/phases/MovementPhase.gd:756-762, 889-896 and 7422-7475: Normal and Advance paths crossing any enemy base are rejected unless the unit has FLY, a Shokk-boosta or Grapnel Launchers, Calistus, or is a Super-Heavy Walker. There is no MONSTER/VEHICLE exemption, so 17.01 appears unimplemented (read, not run)

entries.coverage_detail: The AI's path model checks only MONSTER/VEHICLE bases (mv_models via _get_monster_vehicle_models, AIDecisionMaker.gd:14508, 15897) and relies on engine rejection and staging retries for other enemy bases (B38). Because the engine itself rejects these drive-throughs, nothing can choose them today.
entries.engine_support: Engine fix first: exempt MONSTER/VEHICLE movers from _path_crosses_enemy_bases for non-M/V enemy models on Normal and Advance moves (MovementPhase.gd:756-762, 889-896, 7422-7475). Then let the AI treat non-M/V enemy bases as passable for M/V movers in _compute_movement_toward_target (AIDecisionMaker.gd:14212) while keeping the end-position checks.
entries.value_reason: Vehicle and monster-heavy lists (Ork Battlewagons, Custodes and Space Wolf Dreadnoughts) are often stopped by chaff, and this is a core 11e change, but it is blocked by an engine gap.
absorbed: DEN-22 (Drive a MONSTER/VEHICLE through an enemy infantry screen)
entries.errata_note: Per FAQ 17.01 a MONSTER/VEHICLE unit can move through friendly units on every move type, charges and fall-backs included (03.01 lets any model move through friendly models), so only the pass-through of enemy non-MONSTER/VEHICLE models is limited to normal and advance moves; a Desperate Escape fall-back also lets every model move through enemy models (core 09.07). — FAQ 17.01 Moving Monsters and Vehicles (errata_faq:598-599)

entries.name: Use a move-through or MOBILE grant to shortcut models and terrain
entries.description: Spend an ability-granted path, rather than detouring, to reach a hidden unit in dense terrain, an objective behind a ruin, or a target behind chaff. The SUPER-HEAVY WALKER core ability moves through models (except TITANIC) and over sections 4″ or lower, and can take the MOBILE gamble (become MOBILE for the move and pass dense terrain, but battle-shocked on a D6 roll of 1). Faction grants include STOMPING JUGGERNAUT (Ork Walkers become MOBILE), UNSTOPPABLE MOMENTUM (Custodes Dreadnoughts), FENRISIAN FEROCITY (Space Wolf Mounted and Walkers), Calistus ka'tah (through all models), Get Out da Way! (Nobz charge through non-M/V models), Grapnel Launchers (Reivers) and Shokk-boosta (Big Mek advance).
entries.when_to_use: The straight line to the objective or target crosses dense terrain or a screen, the detour costs the charge or the objective this turn, and the grant's cost (CP, a hazard roll per model for the Shokk-boosta, a 1-in-6 battle-shock for the MOBILE gamble) is acceptable. Skip the MOBILE gamble when the walker's OC is needed.
entries.unit_types: SUPER-HEAVY WALKERs (Stompa, Gorkanaut, Morkanaut), Ork Walkers, Nobz, Big Mek, Custodes with Calistus and Custodes Dreadnoughts, Space Wolf Mounted and Walkers, Reivers
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance / Fall Back (Charge for Get Out da Way!)
entries.rules_basis: 24.35 SUPER-HEAVY WALKER (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3940-3967). 13.06: only INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM/MOBILE pass dense terrain horizontally; other models only over sections 2″ or lower (:2161-2180). 03.01.02: a 'move through models' rule lets a model pass enemy models while every other restriction still applies (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:226-228). Grant texts: .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/RULES.md:134 (STOMPING JUGGERNAUT), orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:80 (Get Out da Way!), custodes/RULES.md:63, :129, space-marines/RULES.md:475, space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:607.

40k/scripts/stratagems/ork_codex/OrkCodexMovement.gd:288-291 (STOMPING JUGGERNAUT scored 0.0: 'The AI movement planner does not path through dense terrain')

docs/rules/11th_edition_delta_audit.md (24.35 row, ISS-073)

Calistus is taken only for fall-backs (CustodesKatah.gd:720-724). STOMPING JUGGERNAUT scores 0.0 (OrkCodexMovement.gd:288-291), UNSTOPPABLE MOMENTUM and INEXORABLE 0.0 (CustodesCodexMovement.gd:268-269), Shokk-boosta 0.0 (OrkAbilities11e.gd:2323-2324). New query: the AI path model per grant (SHW passes non-TITANIC models and sections 4″ or lower; MOBILE passes dense terrain), with each grant's cost compared against the detour.

entries.name: Bait and counter-punch: stage a retaliation unit behind a forward unit
entries.description: Put a tempting forward unit, cheap or durable, where the enemy wants to charge, shoot or score, and stage a hammer (melee or guns) just outside the enemy's reach but within reach of where the enemy will end up after attacking it. Whatever takes the bait is then destroyed next turn or by a Heroic Intervention. Accept losing the bait when the exchange favours you in points or primary VP.
entries.when_to_use: Against aggressive melee or reserve-heavy opponents, on contested mid-board objectives, when you have a fast hitter or a strong second line and the bait is cheap or tough.
entries.unit_types: Bait: cheap or durable scoring units. Hammer: fast melee or shooting units
entries.rules_basis: An edition-agnostic tactic. The 11e rules it uses: 11.02, a charge needs an enemy within 12″ (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1618-1622), and 15.11 Heroic Intervention (:2734-2766).
evidence: YouTube MG546BN181w @47:00 (Grimdark Breakdown, F011): 'You do not have to kill your opponent in 11th edition. A giant condition of winning was tableabling your opponent in 10th'
YouTube VqwMdS9MuIY @62:00 (TacticalTortoise 40k, F008): 'it's absolutely worth a genailer squad to eviscerate one of those ranger squads even though it's a trade down'

BoLS '40K Tactics: Maximizing your Assault' https://www.belloflostsouls.net/2010/08/40k-tactics-maximizing-your-assault.html (search snippet: put bait where you'll be able to countercharge next turn; older edition)
Wertstammer 'Hammer and Anvil' https://wertstammer40k.wordpress.com/2016/11/11/hammer-and-anvil/ (older edition)
YouTube sPWC5HujB_Y @19:00 (StrikingScorpion82): “holding objectives, picking on isolated, tying units down, blocking movements ... it's no big deal if they're slain” [F031]
YouTube VqwMdS9MuIY @62:00 (TacticalTortoise 40k): “it's absolutely worth a genailer squad to eviscerate one of those ranger squads even though it's a trade down” [F008]
entries.coverage_detail: There is no retaliation-range term. The threat dodge (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28892-28990) only moves units away from threats, and CHARGE_RETALIATION_WEIGHT (1767) is a Charge-phase term for a target fighting back, not staging.
entries.engine_support: _calculate_enemy_threat_data and _evaluate_position_threat (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28695, 28794) to predict where enemies end after attacking the bait; _estimate_melee_damage (19576) and _estimate_unit_ranged_strength (25866) for the hammer; _estimate_unit_value (28003) for the trade. New query: a paired candidate (bait B at D1, hammer H at D2) where H is outside enemy reach now but within reach of the likely end positions of B's attackers next turn.
entries.value_reason: Trading well wins 11e games (F011, tabling is not a win condition), but the pattern needs two-unit, two-turn planning the AI lacks.
absorbed: DEN-31 (Bait with an expendable unit to pull an enemy unit out of position)

entries.name: Stay within reach of a friendly enabler for reactive protection or extraction
entries.description: End a protected unit's move close to the unit that enables a reaction: a Gretchin unit within 3″ of an Orks Infantry mob (GROT SHIELDS turns hits into mortal wounds on the Gretchin), every model within 3″ of a Repulsor (Combat Embarkation pulls the charge target inside), wholly within 6″ of a transport at the end of the Fight phase (KEEP IT RUNNIN', DUTY IS NEVER DONE re-embark the unit), or Battleline units within 12″ of a Laurels of Vigilance bearer (Fire Overwatch or Heroic Intervention costs 1CP less). Keep the enabler itself out of easy reach.
entries.when_to_use: A valuable Ork mob is about to be shot; infantry next to a Repulsor faces a likely charge; a melee unit will finish its fight near its transport and should be re-delivered next turn; Battleline units are likely to need cheap Overwatch.
entries.unit_types: Gretchin with Orks Infantry (Runt Swarm), Repulsor and Adeptus Astartes cargo, Ork Infantry and transports (Blitz Brigade), Adeptus Astartes Infantry and transports (Gauntlet), Battleline near a Laurels of Vigilance bearer
entries.rules_basis: Stratagem and datasheet texts: GROT SHIELDS 'One friendly Gretchin unit within 3″ of that ORKS INFANTRY unit' (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/RULES.md:222); KEEP IT RUNNIN' 'wholly within 6″ of a friendly Transport' (orks/RULES.md:201); DUTY IS NEVER DONE (space-marines/RULES.md:613); Laurels of Vigilance, 12″ (space-marines/RULES.md:709); Combat Embarkation, 'If every model in that unit is within 3″ of this TRANSPORT' (space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:615).
evidence: 40k/scripts/stratagems/ork_codex/OrkCodexShootingReactive.gd:250-251 (GROT SHIELDS scored at use)
40k/scripts/codex/space_marines/SMAbilitiesC.gd:1928-1929 (Combat Embarkation 2.5 at use)
40k/scripts/codex/space_marines/SMCodexAMovement.gd:292-294 (DUTY IS NEVER DONE 2.0 when no enemy within 9″)
entries.coverage_detail: These reactions are scored only when offered (OrkCodexShootingReactive.gd:250-251; SMAbilitiesC.gd:1928-1929; SMCodexAMovement.gd:292-294). No movement term keeps units within these radii, and the AI never embarks during play (inventory B44 and gap 6).
entries.engine_support: The codex window predicates hold the radii (the scripts cited above); Measurement model-to-model distance; _estimate_incoming_melee_damage (AIDecisionMaker.gd:12350) for what the reaction prevents. New query: per protected unit, the enablers it could stand within X″ of, as a destination bonus equal to the expected damage prevented or the extraction value.
entries.value_reason: Each case needs a specific detachment or datasheet and the payoff depends on what the enemy does, though GROT SHIELDS can be large for Runt Swarm Orks.
entries.errata_note: Per Commentary 18.02.01 a unit is only able to embark (KEEP IT RUNNIN'; DUTY IS NEVER DONE says 'eligible to embark') if it still meets 18.02's unmodified conditions, including not having been set up on the battlefield this turn, so a unit that disembarked or arrived from reserves this turn cannot be re-embarked by these stratagems at the end of that turn's Fight phase. Neither stratagem says the unit may embark in a turn it disembarked, which per FAQ 18.02 is what lifts that restriction. — Commentary 18.02.01 Able To Embark (errata_faq:626); FAQ 18.02 Embarking (:621-622)

entries.name: Switch off enemy Overwatch with a denier during your Movement phase
entries.description: Move an Overwatch denier so that, before the end of your Movement phase, it is within range of and can see the enemy unit whose Overwatch threatens your assault lane: Drive-by Skorchin' (a visible non-MONSTER/VEHICLE enemy within 6″ cannot be targeted with Fire Overwatch this turn) or Murderous Hurricane (a visible enemy within 12″ cannot make snap-shooting attacks). The rest of the army can then cross that unit's sight lines safely.
entries.when_to_use: The opponent has CP and an unengaged high-volume shooter within 24″ of your planned destinations, your key units must cross its sight lines this turn, and the denier can reach it.
entries.unit_types: Warbuggies (Drive-by Skorchin'), Njal Stormcaller (Murderous Hurricane)
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (the denier only needs to end in range before the phase ends)
entries.rules_basis: 15.08: Fire Overwatch is used at the end of the opponent's Movement phase (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2735-2748), so it resolves after all your moves; the denier does not have to move first, only to have used its ability on the right enemy by then. Correction: factions#16 said 'move the denier first'. Texts: Drive-by Skorchin' (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:125); Murderous Hurricane (psychic, battle-shocked on a 1) (space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:301).
evidence: 40k/scripts/codex/orks/OrkAbilities11e.gd:1424 (Drive-by Skorchin' implemented) and :2321 (scored 1.5 at use)
40k/scripts/codex/space_wolves/SWAbilities11e.gd:1462, 1834 (Murderous Hurricane 12″, scored at use)
YouTube eUpeWbN7gF4 @28:00 (StrikingScorpion82, F004): 'overwatch is done at the end of the opponent's movement phase ... it's a decision we can make uh once movement's done'
entries.coverage_detail: Drive-by Skorchin' and Murderous Hurricane get flat scores of about 1.5 when offered (OrkAbilities11e.gd:2321; SWAbilities11e.gd:1834), with no link to which enemy carries the Overwatch threat. The Overwatch exposure term ships OFF and ignores denial (OVERWATCH_EXPOSURE_PENALTY = 0.0, AIDecisionMaker.gd:2662; helper 28660-28688).
entries.engine_support: _overwatch_exposure_penalty (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28660-28688) to find the enemy unit carrying the largest Overwatch threat on our destinations; _estimate_unit_overwatch_damage (19521). New query: whether a denier can end within 6″ or 12″ of that unit with visibility, and the exposure saved for the rest of the army.
entries.value_reason: Only two in-engine units can deny Overwatch, and the value depends on an exposure term that is currently switched off.

entries.name: Take the exposed direct lane with Overwatch-immune units
entries.description: Units that cannot be targeted by snap shooting can end in the open, inside enemy sight lines, at no Overwatch cost, so give them the direct exposed route and send other units through the covered one.
entries.when_to_use: A snap-immune unit (Seal of Shrouding, Linebreaker Onslaught after disembarking, Combat Deployment cargo, GOLDEN LIGHT OF THE MOIRAIDES on the turn it ingresses) must cross open ground covered by enemy Overwatch.
entries.unit_types: Phobos units with Seal of Shrouding; Gauntlet Linebreaker Onslaught and Grav-Assault Combat Deployment cargo; Dread Host reserves
entries.rules_basis: 15.08 and 15.09 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2735-2768). Texts: Seal of Shrouding, 'Enemy units cannot target this unit with snap shooting attacks' (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/RULES.md:643); Linebreaker Onslaught (space-marines/RULES.md:610); Combat Deployment (custodes/RULES.md:220); GOLDEN LIGHT OF THE MOIRAIDES (custodes/RULES.md:233).
evidence: 40k/scripts/rules/shootingtypes/SnapShooting.gd:26-28 (GOLDEN LIGHT OF THE MOIRAIDES blocks snap shooting)
40k/scripts/codex/space_marines/SMDetachmentsA.gd:60 (Seal of Shrouding: no snap shooting at this unit)
entries.coverage_detail: The Overwatch exposure term ships OFF (OVERWATCH_EXPOSURE_PENALTY = 0.0, AIDecisionMaker.gd:2662) and its helper has no immunity check (28660-28688), so immunity cannot change any choice today.
entries.engine_support: SnapShooting.target_allowed (SnapShooting.gd:22-34) and CustodesCodex11e.blocks_snap_shooting_at. New query: 'is this unit a legal snap-shooting target' inside _overwatch_exposure_penalty, zeroing the penalty when it is not.
entries.value_reason: It only matters once an Overwatch exposure term is switched on, and few units are immune.

entries.name: Arrive or disembark in sequence to share an arrival-triggered buff
entries.description: Some buffs are created by one unit's arrival or shooting and used by others that arrive or disembark the same turn, so order and spacing matter. Flyboss (when this Orks Aircraft ends an ingress move, each friendly Orks Aircraft or Deffkoptas unit within 6″ is riled up; Skyborne Loons then gives riled aircraft +1 to hit): bring the other aircraft and Deffkoptas in FIRST and land the Flyboss last, within 6″ of them. Combined Deployment: the transport shoots before its disembarked cargo, so the cargo gets [SUSTAINED HITS 1] against the assailed target. Linebreaker Onslaught and Combat Deployment: disembarked units re-roll charges, so disembark and stage for a long charge.
entries.when_to_use: Several Ork aircraft or Deffkoptas are arriving from reserves (Flyboss); a transport and its cargo can both engage the same target this turn; cargo needs the charge re-roll to make a long charge after disembarking.
entries.unit_types: Ork Aircraft and Deffkoptas (Flyboss); Adeptus Astartes transports and cargo (Gauntlet, Razorback); Custodes grav-assault transports; Kill Rig; Stompa
entries.rules_basis: Flyboss: 'When this unit ends an ingress move, each friendly Orks Aircraft/Deffkoptas unit within 6″ of this unit is riled up until the start of your next turn' (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/RULES.md:263), so only units already on the battlefield are riled; this corrects factions#21's 'bring the enabler in first'. Skyborne Loons (orks/RULES.md:261). Combined Deployment (space-marines/RULES.md:608). Linebreaker Onslaught (space-marines/RULES.md:610). Combat Deployment (custodes/RULES.md:220). 18.03 FAQ: any disembark move counts as having disembarked that turn (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md, 18.03 entry).
evidence: 40k/scripts/codex/space_marines/SMDetachmentsA.gd:37-38 (Combined Deployment implemented) and :1038-1048 (AI always assails the most expensive enemy hit)
.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:240 (Beastscent), :159 (Idol of Belligerence)
entries.coverage_detail: Reserves arrive one at a time by individual score (B42, AIDecisionMaker.gd:7728-8017), and disembarks are chosen per unit (8417-8832); none of Flyboss, Combined Deployment, Fire Support or Linebreaker Onslaught is referenced in AIDecisionMaker.gd. The Combined Deployment target is the most expensive enemy hit (SMDetachmentsA.gd:1038-1048), not the cargo's target.
entries.engine_support: _decide_reserves_arrival (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7728) and _decide_transport_disembark (8417) for ordering; the placement candidates (8019-8247). New query: a joint arrival plan that orders arrivals (Flyboss last, within 6″ of the others) and aligns the transport's shooting target with the cargo's charge or shooting target.
entries.value_reason: Each case is a niche enhancement or detachment rule with a small, conditional payoff.
entries.errata_note: FAQ 18.03 counts every disembark mode as having disembarked, but only a Tactical Disembark (made before the transport moves, or while it stays stationary) followed by a normal move leaves the unit able to charge; after a Rapid Disembark (forced once the transport has made a normal or ingress move this phase), a Combat Disembark or an Emergency Disembark it cannot declare a charge that turn (core 18.04/18.05), so the Linebreaker Onslaught / Combat Deployment charge re-roll only pays off after a Tactical Disembark. — Core 18.04 Disembark Move / 18.05 Emergency Disembark Move (After Moving); FAQ 18.03 Disembarking (errata_faq:630-631)

entries.name: Slip past screens through their engagement range
entries.description: A Normal or Advance move only has to END unengaged: models may pass within 2″ of enemy models (never through their bases) to get behind a screen, onto an objective or into the backfield, provided the gaps are wide enough for their bases.
entries.when_to_use: An enemy screen has base-sized gaps, there is a target or objective behind it, and the unit has enough movement to end more than 2″ from every enemy.
entries.unit_types: All units without FLY (FLY units can take to the skies instead)
entries.rules_basis: 03.01: bases cannot be moved through enemy models, but there is no engagement restriction while moving (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:386-404). 09.05: the unit must be unengaged after moving (:1390-1398). 03.04 FAQ: 'Does my model or unit become engaged while moving through an enemy unit's engagement range during a move? A: No' (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:265-266).
evidence: 40k/phases/MovementPhase.gd:7080-7094 (_check_engagement_range_at_position tests destinations only)
40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:28344-28365 (screen-gap notes: 11e Normal moves have no mid-move engagement restriction)

BoLS 'New Close Combat Rules Revealed' https://www.belloflostsouls.net/2026/04/warhammer-40k-new-close-combat-rules-revealed-melee-movement-made-easy.html (search snippet: you can now move through an enemy model's engagement range in the Movement phase)
entries.coverage_detail: Only by accident: the destination engine checks engagement at endpoints only (_is_position_near_enemy, AIDecisionMaker.gd:15329), so a greedy path can pass through engagement range. The planner never looks for a gap behind a screen, and its own path model checks only MONSTER/VEHICLE bases, relying on engine rejection and retries for infantry bases (B38). The gap geometry is computed only for our own screens (_screen_widest_passable_gap_inches, 28388).
entries.engine_support: _screen_widest_passable_gap_inches and _screen_max_model_spacing_px (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28388, 28380) apply the same physics in reverse; MovementPhase._path_crosses_enemy_bases (MovementPhase.gd:7422). New query: destinations behind an enemy screen reachable through a gap at least one base wide, with the path clear of enemy bases and the end more than 2″ away.
entries.value_reason: It sometimes unlocks a target or objective behind chaff, but greedy pathing already passes through engagement range when the line is clear.

entries.name: Rotate oval and FRAME bases for free reach or width
entries.description: Rotating costs no movement in 11e, so finish a move by turning oval-based or FRAME models so the long side points at the objective or charge target (extra effective reach), or lies broadside to widen a block or screen.
entries.when_to_use: Oval or FRAME models that end just short of an objective's range or a charge target, or that are forming a screen or block.
entries.unit_types: Oval-based models (bikes, Battlewagons, Knights) and FRAME models

entries.name: Route a Thunderhawk over enemy units on a bombing run
entries.description: Thunderhawk Cluster Bombs trigger when the Gunship ends a normal or advance move: pick one enemy unit it moved over during that move and roll six D6, each 3+ is a mortal wound. The path, not just the destination, has value, so route the move over the most valuable enemy unit it can cross.
entries.when_to_use: The Thunderhawk is moving anyway and a high-value or wounded enemy unit lies on or near its route; Advance only if the extra distance is needed.
entries.unit_types: Thunderhawk Gunship (FLY, VEHICLE, TITANIC, TRANSPORT; not AIRCRAFT)
entries.rules_basis: Datasheet text: 'In your Movement phase, when this unit ends a normal/advance move, you can select one enemy unit this unit moved over during that move and roll six D6: For each 3+, that enemy unit suffers 1 mortal wound.' (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:175). The Gunship's keywords are FLY, VEHICLE, TITANIC, TRANSPORT (space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_keywords.csv:237-243), so 23.02's AIRCRAFT ingress-only rule does not apply. It can cross non-M/V models under 17.01 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2869-2874), or any model by taking to the skies (21.03, :3358-3376).

entries.name: Shape the surge target with your end positions
entries.description: A surge move always goes toward the closest enemy unit, so in your own Movement phase end your units so that, for each friendly unit with a reactive surge, the enemy you want it to hit is its closest enemy; likewise keep a cheap unit closest to an enemy surge unit so its surge lands on the cheap unit. This entry was added by the bucket editor from the bucket definition ('Surge'); the surge itself happens in the opponent's turn.
entries.when_to_use: You have units with reactive surges (GOADED INTO ACTION, Vengeful Surge, Bestial Rage), or the enemy does, and the closest-enemy choice would otherwise send the surge into a bad matchup or onto a valuable unit.
entries.unit_types: Da Big Hunt Orks (GOADED INTO ACTION), Shield-Captain (Vengeful Surge), Space Wolves with Bestial Rage; cheap units as surge decoys
entries.move_type: Normal (own Movement phase positioning); adjacent: the Surge move (21.02) in the opponent's turn
