entries.name: Arrive from reserves onto an objective
entries.description: Use a strategic-reserves ingress (wholly within 6″ of a battlefield edge) or a Deep Strike (anywhere more than 8″ from all enemy units, even in the enemy deployment zone) to put a unit in range of an objective that no on-table unit can reach. Targets: an uncontrolled or lightly held marker (a high-OC unit can flip a weak hold on arrival), an edge or flank objective, a threatened home objective, or, with Deep Strike, a backfield objective. After arriving the unit cannot move again until the Charge phase, so it has to land in range.
entries.when_to_use: Battle round 2 or later (round 1 only with a first-turn grant, see TRN-22). Pick an objective that still needs OC, has a legal spot in control range more than 8″ from every enemy unit, and where the arriving OC beats what the enemy can bring back before the next scoring point (or the VP from one check is worth the unit). Skip objectives already held securely, where extra OC adds nothing.
entries.unit_types: Strategic reserves and Deep Strike units; high-OC infantry; cheap scoring units.
entries.rules_basis: 20.03: arrive from battle round 2 unless stated otherwise (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3250-3254). 20.04 ingress: wholly within 6″ of an edge, more than 8″ horizontally from all enemy units, not in the opponent's deployment zone before round 3; after moving, no other move type until the next Charge phase (:3255-3274). 24.09 Deep Strike: if every model has it, anywhere more than 8″ from all enemy units, even inside the opponent's deployment zone (:3649-3655). 09.02: units in strategic reserves are selected to move like any other (:1345-1365). Engine: IngressMove.gd:44-112 (validate_setup); GameConstants.gd:48-49 (8″ in 11e).

entries.coverage_detail: Step 1.5 calls _decide_reserves_arrival whenever PLACE_REINFORCEMENT is offered (AIDecisionMaker.gd:6815-6821). Arrival order adds the best objective the unit can help (contested / enemy_weak / held_threatened 1.5, uncontrolled 0.5, times an OC factor, plus VP x1.2). Deep strikers skip objectives with an enemy model within 9″ minus control range (7994-8015). Candidate spots: every 4″ along all edges, 3″ in (8073-8135), or 10/12/15″ rings round objectives plus a grid (8137-8170). Spots are ranked 10 − d within 6″ of an objective, otherwise 8 − 0.3d (8204-8223). FIX-HELD-DUP drops objectives that need no OC (8036-8039, 8054-8071). Limits: (1) candidates need 9″ + base radius + 0.6″ from enemy model centres (8029), while validation uses the legal 8″ (8346), so the 8-9″ band is never proposed. (2) Distance is measured to the marker centre, not to a terrain-objective's area. (3) No check that the unit survives the reply.
entries.engine_support: Reuse _decide_reserves_arrival (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7728), _compute_reinforcement_positions (8019), _is_valid_reinforcement_position (8331), _evaluate_all_objectives (8926), MissionManager.model_in_objective_range / model_gap_to_objective_range_px (MissionManager.gd:529, 569) and IngressMove.validate_setup (IngressMove.gd:44). entries.value_reason: This is the most common reason to hold reserves. The AI already does it, so what is left to gain is the 8-9″ band and terrain-objective range.

entries.name: Drive the transport first, then Rapid-disembark the cargo where it must shoot, score or act
entries.description: Give the loaded TRANSPORT a Normal move first, then disembark. The cargo is set up wholly within 3″ of the hull, so it reaches transport M + 3″ (plus the hull's length) instead of the 3″ + its own M of a tactical disembark. Afterwards the cargo cannot declare a charge or move again this phase. It can still shoot normally (without the [HEAVY] +1, because it was set up this turn) and can start an action. This is the transport version of "move toward an enemy to shoot it", and of taking a far objective with OC this turn.
entries.when_to_use: Use it when the cargo's job this turn is shooting (Melta or Rapid Fire half range, or a target beyond its own reach), objective OC, or an action, and transport M + 3″ gets there while 3″ + cargo M does not. The transport must make a Normal move: an Advance or Fall Back bars disembarking this phase. Do not use it when the cargo needs to charge; use TRN-03, or a faction assault disembark (TRN-15).
entries.unit_types: Embarked shooting, scoring and action units, and their TRANSPORT.
entries.rules_basis: 18.04 Disembark Move: only if the transport has not advanced or fallen back this phase; rapid mode is mandatory if it made a normal or ingress move; set-up wholly within 3″; afterwards the unit cannot declare a charge until the end of the turn (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3013-3052). 09.02: each unit is selected to move once, so a rapid-disembarked unit gets no further move (:1345-1356). 10.04 normal shooting only needs the unit unengaged and not to have advanced (:1489-1500). 24.16 [HEAVY]: no +1 for a unit set up this turn (:3751-3765). 16.01: a disembark is neither an advance nor a fall back, so the unit can start an action (:2808-2817). Engine: TransportManager.gd:281-295 (a disembark after the transport moved sets cannot_move and cannot_charge).

entries.coverage_detail: This only happens incidentally. Disembark is decided at Step 1.75, before any unit on the table moves (AIDecisionMaker.gd:6823-6828), and it beats the 0.0 'stay' baseline at any positive score (8444, 8475, 8488). From round 2 every embarked unit scores at least +0.3 (8563-8570). In round 1, a unit in a transport with no Firing Deck detected scores at least −0.2 + 0.4 (8603-8616). So cargo normally gets out before its transport moves (tactical mode). Drive-then-rapid only occurs when the cargo stayed in (score ≤ 0, or no legal placement) and the Step 1.75 re-run after the transport's move scores > 0, for example because the transport ended within 3″ or 6″ of an objective (+0.8 / +0.4; 8512-8527). Transports move last (tier 2, 7657-7664). Nothing compares the two reaches, and the transport's destination is planned for the transport, not for its cargo. Read from code; not validated live.
entries.engine_support: Reuse _score_disembark_benefit (AIDecisionMaker.gd:8498) and _compute_disembark_positions (8626), evaluated at the transport's projected end point; _compute_movement_toward_target (14212) for the transport leg; TransportManager.can_disembark (TransportManager.gd:173). New: a two-step candidate, 'transport Normal move to P, then rapid set-up within 3″ of P', scored by the cargo's shooting and objective value at P against the tactical alternative (TRN-03); block Advance for that transport. Caution (read from code): DisembarkMove.select_mode keys rapid mode off flags.moved_this_phase (DisembarkMove.gd:84), which only SurgeMove writes (SurgeMove.gd:113). Live, this disembark is therefore labelled 'tactical', and the rapid effects come from TransportManager via flags.moved. Plan from flags.moved, not from the mode label.
entries.value_reason: Delivery is what transports are for. Today cargo almost always gets out at the start of the phase, so the transport's move delivers nothing. This sequence is the main way shooting, scoring and action cargo gets transport M + 3″ of reach.

entries.name: Tactical-disembark before the transport moves, then make the cargo's own move (keeps the charge)
entries.description: Disembark while the transport has not yet moved, or is remaining stationary. The cargo is set up wholly within 3″ and is then selected for a Normal or Advance move. After a Normal move it can still shoot and declare a charge, so this is the transport version of "move toward an enemy to charge it" (about 3″ + hull + M, then 2D6). An Advance adds distance but bars both the charge and actions. The transport can move afterwards with any move type: the advance/fall-back bar only stops units disembarking after the transport has made such a move.
entries.when_to_use: Melee or charge-capable cargo with a target within roughly 3″ + M + 12″ (a charge target must be within 12″ and within the charge roll). Also cargo that needs its own movement, for example to reach cover or a quarter. Disembark before the transport is selected to move. If the transport is engaged but there is room for an unengaged set-up within 3″, tactical mode is mandatory; do it before the transport falls back, because a transport that fell back bars disembarking.
entries.unit_types: Embarked units (melee units especially) and their TRANSPORT.
entries.rules_basis: 18.04 Tactical Disembark: mandatory if the transport remained stationary or has not yet been selected to move, and the unit can be set up wholly within 3″; afterwards, select the unit for a normal or advance move (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3013-3054). 03.02: a set-up must be unengaged and in coherency (:491-507). 09.06 Advance: no charge and no action afterwards (:1401-1414). 11.02 charge eligibility: within 12″, no advance or fall back (:1603-1625). 11.04: targets must be within the charge roll (:1640-1650). 24.16: no [HEAVY] +1 for a unit set up this turn (:3751-3765). Correction to core-rules#70: 18.04 sets no limit on how the transport moves after its cargo has left. The advance/fall-back clause only applies to disembarking after such a move (:3024-3025), and the engine adds no restriction either (TransportManager.gd:296-300).

Step 1.75 runs before transports move (AIDecisionMaker.gd:6823-6828, commented 'so disembarked units can still move'), so the engine picks tactical mode. _score_disembark_benefit adds +0.4 for a melee unit with an enemy within M + 15″ while the transport has not moved (8546-8561), and disembarked units move first (tier 0, 7657-7664). (3) Possible bug, read from code and not validated live: the follow-up opens an active move (MovementPhase.gd:9090-9092, 8773-8846). get_available_actions then offers CONFIRM_UNIT_MOVE for it (7943-7953), and _decide_movement confirms any CONFIRM_UNIT_MOVE before planning (AIDecisionMaker.gd:6804-6814). The cargo may therefore close its follow-up move without moving at all.

entries.value_reason: It is the standard way to deliver melee out of a transport. It already happens by default, but crudely, and the follow-up move may be lost.

entries.name: Delivery run: keep the cargo aboard and drive the transport to where the cargo's next task is
entries.description: Treat the transport and its cargo as one escort pair. The cargo stays embarked this turn, and the transport's move is chosen for where the cargo needs to be when it gets out next turn: within 3″ + M of the objective it must hold, or within tactical-disembark-plus-charge reach of its target. Because nobody is getting out this phase, the transport may Advance for extra distance. Next turn, choose between parking (tactical, keeps the charge) and driving (rapid).
entries.when_to_use: The cargo has no good job at its current disembark point, would be exposed on foot, and has a defined task one turn away (an objective to hold in round 2 or 3, or a priority target). The transport can survive the approach.
entries.unit_types: TRANSPORTs and their cargo, e.g. Trukk + Boyz, Rhino/Impulsor + Marines, Raider/Venom + Drukhari.
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance (transport); the cargo stays embarked
entries.rules_basis: 09.02: an embarked unit is selected to move like any other unit and can simply not disembark (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1345-1365). 18.04: only disembarking is barred after the transport advances or falls back (:3024-3025); next turn the mode is tactical if the transport stays put, rapid if it moves (:3029-3054). Embarked units are not on the battlefield and cannot be targeted (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:36).

entries.name: Stay embarked, or embark, to protect a threatened unit and deny kills
entries.description: Keep a fragile or valuable unit inside its transport, or end its Normal, Advance or Fall Back move with every model within 3″ of a friendly transport with room, and embark. It leaves the battlefield: it cannot be shot, overwatched (Fire Overwatch happens at the end of the Movement phase, against visible units within 24″), charged, or counted by kill cards until the transport dies. The costs: while aboard it cannot shoot (except through Firing Deck), charge, hold objectives or perform actions. If the transport is destroyed, the unit makes an emergency disembark (hazard rolls, battle-shocked, models that cannot be placed are destroyed) and can then be hit by the transport's Deadly Demise.
entries.when_to_use: The unit would likely die, or give up a kill-card score, next turn; it has no objective or action job this turn; and a transport with capacity is within reach. Weight this more for armies whose infantry depend on transports (Drukhari) and under kill-based cards. Never embark the Beacon unit (it must be on the battlefield when it scores at the end of the opponent's turn), or a unit Condemned by the opponent's Punishment card (leaving the battlefield pays them). A unit set up this turn (disembarked or arrived from reserves) cannot embark.
entries.unit_types: Characters, glass-cannon infantry, damaged units: anything that fits a friendly TRANSPORT.
entries.move_type: Embark (after a Normal / Advance / Fall Back move), or stay embarked
entries.rules_basis: 18.02 Embarking: after a normal, advance or fall-back move; every model within 3″; not set up this turn; enough capacity; the unit is then not on the battlefield (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2981-2997). 15.08 Fire Overwatch: end of the opponent's Movement phase, one visible enemy unit within 24″ (:2735-2760). Not on the battlefield means not visible and not measurable (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:36). 18.05 emergency disembark, with errata (:3061-3078; errata_faq:609). 24.08 Deadly Demise resolves after the emergency disembark (:3670-3699). 24.14 Firing Deck (:3705-3730). Beacon card (engine data): a unit may be designated while embarked, but it scores only 'if the beacon unit is on the battlefield' (40k/data/40kdc/missionCards.json:2850; the full card is unconfirmed per docs/rules/11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:4). Punishment: a Condemned unit that leaves the battlefield pays the card's owner (missionCards.json:467; MissionManager.gd:1772-1780, 1955-1965). Correction to first-principles#10: an embarked Beacon does not score.

entries.coverage_detail: The AI never embarks during play. EMBARK_UNIT never appears in AIDecisionMaker.gd or AIPlayer.gd, and MovementPhase._check_embark_opportunity returns early for AI players (MovementPhase.gd:8306-8311). Staying embarked only happens when every disembark score is ≤ the 0.0 baseline (AIDecisionMaker.gd:8444, 8475). The only negative term is round 1's −0.2 (8563-8567), and no Firing Deck adds +0.4 (8603-8616), so cargo stays in essentially only in round 1, in a Firing Deck transport. No term looks at the cargo's exposure, kill cards, or Beacon / Condemned status. Adjacent: faction end-of-Fight-phase embarks are scored. DUTY IS NEVER DONE scores 2.0 when no enemy is within 9″ and the unit is off objectives (SMCodexAMovement.gd:292-294); MOUNT UP, LADZ resolves at StratagemManager.gd:2788-2806.
entries.engine_support: Reuse TransportManager.can_embark (TransportManager.gd:107) and is_unit_within_embark_range (:784). The action validator, _validate_embark_unit (MovementPhase.gd:9120-9150), checks neither the 3″ range nor engagement range, so the AI must check them itself. Reuse _calculate_enemy_threat_data / _evaluate_position_threat (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28695, 28794) for exposure, and MissionManager card state for Beacon / Condemned. New: an 'embark' destination in the movement plan (within 3″ of a friendly transport with room), followed by EMBARK_UNIT; and a real valued 'stay embarked' option in _decide_transport_disembark.
entries.value_reason: Saving a key unit or denying a kill-card score is worth several VP, and today the AI unloads nearly every transport in round 1.

entries.name: Arrive from reserves to charge the same turn (move toward an enemy to charge it)
entries.description: Land a melee unit just over 8″ from an unscreened priority target and charge it in the same turn. An ingress move only bars other moves until the next Charge phase. The charge target must be within 12″ and within the 2D6 roll, so landing at 8″+ needs a 9+ (about 28%). The odds improve with a Command Re-roll (re-rolls the whole charge), a charge bonus (e.g. FURY OF THE EMPEROR, +2 for Custodes Terminators that made an ingress move), or several targets in range. In 11e, Fire Overwatch happens at the end of the Movement phase, after the unit arrives, not during the charge.
entries.when_to_use: Rounds 2-3. A high-value target (character, scoring unit, artillery) has open ground more than 8″ from every enemy unit and within 12″ of it. The unit has a charge re-roll or bonus, or a failed charge still leaves it somewhere useful (on an objective, or in cover). Deep Strike can land in the backfield, even in the enemy deployment zone; strategic reserves need the target near an edge.
entries.unit_types: Melee units with Deep Strike or in strategic reserves: assault Terminators, jump infantry, Custodes Terminators, Ork deep strikers.
entries.move_type: Reserves arrival, then a charge in the Charge phase
entries.rules_basis: 20.04: more than 8″ from all enemy units; after moving, no other move type until the start of the next Charge phase (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3264-3273). 24.09 Deep Strike (:3649-3655). 11.02 charge eligibility: within 12″, unengaged, no advance or fall back (:1603-1625). 11.04: each charge target must be within the maximum distance, i.e. the charge roll (:1640-1650). 15.02 Command Re-roll: charge rolls are re-rolled in full (:2651-2680). 15.08 Overwatch timing (:2735-2737). FURY OF THE EMPEROR text (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/custodes/RULES.md:118). Engine: IngressMove.gd:138-146 (no_moves_until_charge_phase; the unit can still charge).

entries.coverage_detail: Melee units get +1.5 in the arrival order (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7967-7968). Every candidate spot gets +3 when the nearest enemy centroid is 10-15″ away, or +2 at 9-10″ (8226-8239); the code's own comment calls that band 'hard to charge immediately'. The 9″ + buffer candidate filter (8029) also removes the 8-9″ band. So arrivals are placed to threaten next turn, not to charge this turn. There is no charge-odds, target-value, re-roll or bonus term, and FURY OF THE EMPEROR and the other arrival buffs never appear in AIDecisionMaker.gd.

entries.errata_note: Holds for most units. But if a non-AIRCRAFT model is too large to set up wholly within 6″ of the battlefield edge, it must be set up touching the edge, and its unit then cannot make a normal, advance, fall-back or charge move that turn. So it cannot charge on arrival from an edge ingress. Deep Strike set-ups have no edge distance and are not affected. — Commentary 03.02.02 Setting Up Large Models (From Strategic Reserves)

entries.name: Arrive from reserves to shoot (move toward an enemy to shoot it)
entries.description: Deep Strike or ingress a shooting unit where its guns work best this turn: within half range for [MELTA] or [RAPID FIRE]; within detection range of a Hidden priority target (15″, or 12″ against a model that has gone to ground); or on a flank or backfield angle the army on the table cannot see. The unit can use normal shooting (it did not advance) but never gets the [HEAVY] +1, because it was set up this turn. Faction arrival buffs make the arrival turn the best shooting turn: Inceptor Meteoric Descent (+1 to hit), Deffkoptas Deff from Above (+1 to hit), Venatari Strike from the Skies (re-roll hits).
entries.when_to_use: Rounds 2-3, or later for repositioned units. A valuable target is reachable from more than 8″ away and visible from the landing spot, and the unit's damage is concentrated at short range or it has an arrival buff. Accept that it faces Overwatch at the end of this Movement phase and then the opponent's next Shooting phase (see TRN-10).
entries.unit_types: Shooting units in reserves: melta, plasma and rapid-fire squads, Inceptors, Deffkoptas, Venatari. AIRCRAFT: see TRN-17.
entries.rules_basis: 20.04 / 24.09 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3255-3274, 3649-3655). 10.04: normal shooting only requires no advance (:1489-1500). 24.16 [HEAVY]: no bonus for a unit set up this turn (:3751-3765; engine ModifierStack.gd:168-172). 24.25 [MELTA] and 24.30 [RAPID FIRE] half range (:3833-3845, 3896-3905). 13.09 Hidden, 15″ detection range (:2292-2302), as errata'd to light/dense terrain (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:529); gone to ground −3″ (errata_faq:539). entries.name: Bring every strategic-reserves unit in by the end of battle round 3
entries.description: Strategic reserves that have not made an ingress move by the end of round 3 are destroyed. The exceptions are units inside a transport that has made an ingress move, and repositioned units. Treat round 3 as the last own-turn arrival. For a unit that still could not be placed, the last chance is a Rapid Ingress at the end of the opponent's round-3 Movement phase. Plan arrivals so the deadline never forces a bad spot (or leaves no spot), and keep CP for that last Rapid Ingress.
entries.when_to_use: Any unit still in strategic reserves at the start of round 3. Also round 2, when legal space is scarce: enemy screens, or the 12″ zones around Omni-scrambler / Arae-Shrike units.
entries.unit_types: Strategic reserves units, including reserve TRANSPORTs with cargo and units with Deep Strike. Not repositioned units.
entries.move_type: Reserves arrival (adjacent: Rapid Ingress at the end of the opponent's round-3 Movement phase)
entries.rules_basis: 20.03 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3250-3254). 20.04: destruction at the end of round 3, with its exceptions (:3276-3283). 20.02 repositioned units (:3219-3240). 15.07 Rapid Ingress: end of the opponent's Movement phase; not in round 1; not AIRCRAFT (:2714-2731). entries.coverage_detail: The deadline is usually met by default, because every reserve arrives at its first legal chance (Step 1.5, AIDecisionMaker.gd:6815-6821; there is no hold-back option). But the urgency is 10e-shaped. Arrival order adds +2.0 in round 3 and +5.0, commented 'last chance on Round 5', from round 4 (7974-7978; constants 2060-2061). Rapid Ingress declines with 1 CP before round 4 and adds urgency only in round 3+ / 4+ (28143-28146, 28167-28173). The 9″ + buffer filter (8029) can leave a unit with no candidate in a crowded round 3, and nothing relaxes it. The plan's RESERVE_UNTIL arrival_round is recorded at formations (1058, 1172-1218) but never read when units arrive.
entries.engine_support: Reuse _score_reserves_deployment (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7949), evaluate_rapid_ingress (28121) and GameState.get_battle_round. New: a hard 'must arrive this turn' flag in round 3 (and for the opponent's round-3 Rapid Ingress) that relaxes the spot filter to the legal 8″ and keeps 1 CP for the Rapid Ingress fallback.
entries.value_reason: Missing the deadline loses the whole unit, and any hold-back logic (TRN-11) depends on getting this right.

entries.name: Set up out of sight, in cover or Hidden when arriving or disembarking (move into cover)
entries.description: An arrival or a disembark is a set-up the unit cannot move away from this turn: an ingress bars other moves, and a rapid disembark ends the unit's move. The unit will face the opponent's Fire Overwatch at the end of this Movement phase and their whole next turn; a Rapid Ingress arrival faces their Shooting phase straight away. So pick a spot out of enemy line of sight (behind Solid or obscuring terrain) or inside a terrain area for the benefit of cover. INFANTRY / BEASTS / SWARM can instead set up with every model inside a terrain area containing light or dense features: they are then Hidden, visible only within the 15″ detection range (−3″ if gone to ground), because the unit has not shot this turn or last. This is the transport/reserves version of "move into cover".
entries.when_to_use: Every arrival or disembark near enemy shooters, especially for fragile or high-value units, or when the unit's job (objective, action, next-turn charge) does not need it to shoot this turn. Weigh it against TRN-07: shooting gives up Hidden for this turn and the next.
entries.unit_types: All arriving and disembarking units. Hidden applies to INFANTRY / BEASTS / SWARM only.
entries.move_type: Reserves arrival / Disembark (where to set up)
entries.rules_basis: 20.04: no other move until the next Charge phase (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3271-3273). 18.04 rapid: no further move (:3029-3052). 15.08 Overwatch: end of the opponent's Movement phase, one visible unit within 24″ (:2735-2760). 15.07 Rapid Ingress timing (:2714-2731). 13.08 cover (:2278-2290). 13.09 Hidden (:2292-2302), errata'd to 'light/dense terrain features' (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:529), with the first-turn note (:533) and gone to ground (:539). 13.10 obscuring (:2305-2311). 13.11 Solid (:2313-2318). Correction to core-rules#78: Hidden needs a terrain area with light OR dense features (errata), not dense only.

entries.name: Hold a unit in reserve this turn (keep the Rapid Ingress threat or a reactive answer)
entries.description: Choose not to make an ingress move, so the reserve unit remains stationary and stays a live threat. At the end of the opponent's Movement phase it can Rapid Ingress (1CP) behind whatever they committed: onto an objective they left, behind units that advanced, or on a flank they overloaded. Meanwhile the opponent has to keep screening during their own turn. Against very fast, high-pressure armies, bring everything on instead.
entries.when_to_use: Round 2 (rarely round 3). You have a punishing reserve unit and at least 1-2 CP to spare, the opponent's screens are thin, and no spot this turn is clearly better than the expected Rapid Ingress spot. Never let the unit miss the round-3 deadline (TRN-09). Not for AIRCRAFT, which cannot Rapid Ingress.
entries.unit_types: Strategic reserves and Deep Strike units (not AIRCRAFT); melee or melta units that punish an exposed backline.
entries.move_type: Remain Stationary (in strategic reserves); adjacent: Rapid Ingress at the end of the opponent's Movement phase
entries.rules_basis: 09.02: every unit, including those in strategic reserves, is selected to move and may remain stationary (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1345-1365; 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:458: units with no move type selected remain stationary). 15.07 Rapid Ingress: end of the opponent's Movement phase; a strategic-reserves unit excluding AIRCRAFT; not in battle round 1 (:2714-2731). 20.04 deadline (:3276-3283).

entries.name: Disembark to add a scoring or action unit
entries.description: A transport and its cargo are separate units, and many cards pay per unit or need distinct units: Behind Enemy Lines (per unit in the enemy deployment zone), Gather Intel (7 VP per unit that completes Extract Intelligence), Sabotage (one objective per saboteur), Booby Trap (one area per unit), Engage on All Fronts (quarter presence), Display of Might (units in No Man's Land), Outflank (two units on opposite edges). Disembarking puts a second unit on the board. A rapid disembark (the transport has moved) can still start actions. A tactical disembark followed by a Normal move keeps action eligibility; an Advance loses it. Do not use a combat disembark for this: it battle-shocks the unit (OC '-', no actions, no positional cards). A transport parked near a quarter line can drop its cargo wholly into the next quarter.
entries.when_to_use: Count-based or one-per-unit cards are active, a loaded transport is near the target geometry, and the cargo will survive to the scoring point.
entries.unit_types: TRANSPORTs and their cargo.
entries.rules_basis: 18.04 modes (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3013-3057). 16.01 action eligibility (:2808-2817). Battle-shocked: OC '-', no actions (:213-221). entries.name: Combat-disembark out of an engaged or boxed-in transport
entries.description: When the transport has not moved (it is engaged and staying put, or ringed so tightly that no unengaged 3″ set-up exists), the cargo must use combat mode. It is set up wholly within 6″, may be set up engaged with units the transport is engaged with, and makes one hazard roll per model (D6: 1-2 is a mortal wound). It is then battle-shocked (OC '-', no actions, no friendly stratagems on it) and cannot charge this turn. Uses: escaping a transport about to die (the alternative, an emergency disembark, also battle-shocks the unit, loses any models that cannot be placed, and then Deadly Demise can hit it); getting bodies into a fight (an engaged unit fights, and can use close-quarters shooting with [CLOSE-QUARTERS] weapons); or tying up the units attacking the transport. It cannot add OC. Disembark before the transport falls back, because a transport that fell back bars every disembark.
entries.when_to_use: The transport is locked in combat or surrounded and staying stationary; the cargo is worth more outside (it fights well, or the transport will probably die); and the expected hazard losses (about 1 mortal wound per 3 models) are acceptable. If an unengaged 3″ set-up exists, tactical mode is mandatory instead (TRN-03).

Battle-shock effects (:213-221). 10.06 close-quarters shooting (:1522-1545). 18.05 with errata, and 24.08 ordering (:3061-3078; errata_faq:609; :3670-3699). Corrections: first-principles#82's 'add OC to an objective' is impossible (battle-shocked OC '-'); web#52's 'if the transport is engaged ... combat disembark' only holds when no unengaged tactical set-up exists.

entries.name: Drive first, then assault- or shock-disembark (faction transport grants)
entries.description: Some transports change the trade so that moving first no longer costs the charge. Assault disembarks (18.06: 3″, no charge ban) after the transport's Normal move: the Land Raider family's Assault Ramp, the Morkanaut/Gorkanaut Gut Hatch, Blitz Brigade READIED BRAWLERS (Wagons), MEKANISED BRUTALITY (Ork rig), Thunderhawk Aerial Assault, and Drop Pod / Termite Assault. These give transport M + 3″ + 2D6. The Impulsor's Rapid Disembarkation allows a shock disembark (18.07: 3″, no charge) after the transport ADVANCED, a fast gunline delivery. Gauntlet AGGRESSIVE DISEMBARKATION sets models up within, rather than wholly within, the set-up distance. With the Orion Assault Dropship, cargo can tactical-disembark, advance and still charge.
entries.when_to_use: Assault grants: the transport's move + 3″ + a charge reaches a target the cargo cannot reach on foot. Shock disembark: shooters need transport M + D6 + 3″ to get in range this turn. Either way, the transport must survive the approach and end somewhere the cargo can be placed.
entries.unit_types: Land Raiders (including Crusader, Redeemer, Venerable), Morkanaut/Gorkanaut, Ork Wagons and rigs (Blitz Brigade), Thunderhawk, Drop Pods / Termites, Impulsor, Orion Assault Dropship, Gauntlet Task Force transports, and their cargo.
entries.rules_basis: 18.04 baseline (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3013-3057). Faction move types: 18.06 ASSAULT DISEMBARK (3″; no charge restriction afterwards; transport not advanced or fallen back) and 18.07 SHOCK DISEMBARK (3″; no charge) (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/SPACE_MARINES_GENERIC.md:16-19). RULINGS.md:423 (Assault Ramp / Rapid Disembarkation), :501 (Drop Pod Assault). entries.skeptic_note: Assault Dropship (custodes Datasheets_abilities.csv:90) is not a drive-first grant. entries.name: Drive a Firing Deck transport into firing position
entries.description: A TRANSPORT with Firing Deck X lends itself one ranged weapon each from up to X embarked models (no [ONE SHOT] weapons) in your Shooting phase, and the passengers then cannot shoot. Move it to where those borrowed weapons have range and line of sight to good targets, while the passengers stay protected inside. The borrowed guns are fired by the transport: if it advanced, only [ASSAULT] weapons can fire, and the passengers' own abilities do not boost them.
entries.when_to_use: Embarked shooters have targets within reach of the transport's move but would be exposed on foot, or the cargo is waiting to disembark later (TRN-04).

entries.name: AIRCRAFT: choose a fresh ingress spot every turn
entries.description: AIRCRAFT start in strategic reserves and can only make ingress moves: wholly within 6″ of an edge, more than 8″ from enemies, and outside the enemy deployment zone before round 3. They go back into reserves at the end of the opponent's turn, so each turn is a fresh edge set-up, chosen for firing lanes and limited exposure. They cannot charge, start actions, count for most positional cards, or use Rapid Ingress. Other units can move through them, Plunging Fire does not apply to attacks by or against them, and only FLYING units can choose them as charge targets. A large aircraft that cannot fit wholly within 6″ may be set up touching the edge and may overhang it.
entries.when_to_use: Every own Movement phase from round 2 (round 1 with Impulsive Recon).
entries.unit_types: AIRCRAFT.
entries.rules_basis: 23.01-23.04 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3499-3531). 20.04 (:3255-3274). 16.01: AIRCRAFT cannot start actions (:2811-2812). 15.07 excludes AIRCRAFT (:2724). Setting up large models from strategic reserves (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:244). Positional cards exclude AIRCRAFT (missionCards.json: outflank, engage-on-all-fronts, behind-enemy-lines, display-of-might).

entries.coverage_detail: Aircraft arrive through the generic reserve path every turn (Step 1.5, AIDecisionMaker.gd:6815-6821). Edge candidates are ranked by objective proximity and the 10-15″ enemy-centroid band (8073-8135, 8204-8240), with +1.0 for ranged units in the arrival order (7971-7972). There is no aircraft-specific term: nothing for firing lanes, line of sight to targets, anti-air threats or exposure. Objective proximity is worthless for a unit that cannot score positional cards or start actions.
entries.engine_support: Reuse the arrival generators (AIDecisionMaker.gd:8073), _is_valid_reinforcement_position (8331), RulesEngine.get_eligible_targets on a board copy (RulesEngine.gd:7137) or TerrainManager.model_visible_11e (TerrainManager.gd:1209) for lanes, and _calculate_enemy_threat_data (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28695) for exposure. Engine notes (read from code, not validated): (1) TurnManager returns the ending player's own aircraft at the end of that player's turn (TurnManager.gd:76-83 calls GameState.return_aircraft_to_reserves(get_active_player())), whereas 23.02 says the end of the opponent's turn. entries.value_reason: Matters every turn for armies with aircraft, but few lists field them.

entries.name: Arrive in the enemy backfield (deployment zone) where reserves normally cannot
entries.description: Strategic reserves cannot set up in the opponent's deployment zone before round 3, but Deep Strike ignores that (anywhere more than 8″ from enemies). Faction rules also lift it: the Scout Bike Squad's Outflank (its ingress may set up in the opponent's deployment zone); Logan Grimnar's High King of Fenris (one Space Wolves unit treats the round as one higher, so it can arrive in round 1, or in the deployment zone in round 2); and the Terminators' Teleport Homer (a Rapid Ingress within 3″ of a token placed at the start of the battle, at −1 CP). The aim: threaten the enemy home objective, backline artillery and characters, or Behind Enemy Lines from round 2.
entries.when_to_use: Round 2, or round 3 for plain strategic reserves. The enemy home objective or backline is lightly screened (a legal spot more than 8″ from every enemy unit exists), and the unit can survive, or the score or kill is worth losing it.
entries.unit_types: Deep Strike units; Scout Bike Squad; Space Wolves reserves with Logan; Terminator Squad / Terminator Assault Squad (homer).
entries.move_type: Reserves arrival (Teleport Homer: adjacent, via Rapid Ingress)
entries.rules_basis: 20.04: 'before the third battle round ... no models can be set up within your opponent's deployment zone' (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3267-3269). 24.09: 'even if that is within your opponent's deployment zone' (:3649-3655). Outflank datasheet text (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:161); Teleport Homer (:108; RULINGS.md:502); High King of Fenris (RULINGS.md:317). entries.name: Transport strike: deliver the cargo to kill a key target, accepting the squad's loss
entries.description: Keep a lethal squad aboard until the strike turn, then drive the transport in and disembark it to remove one key enemy piece (an enabler, character or scoring unit), expecting the squad not to survive the reply. The disembark can be tactical then charge, rapid then shoot, or a faction assault disembark. Judge the trade on what the kill is worth against what the squad is worth.
entries.when_to_use: A key target is within transport move + disembark + weapon or charge reach, and the trade is worth it (the target is an enabler, character or scoring unit). Rounds 1-3; be cautious again in rounds 4-5. Avoid it against an opponent on a kill-based primary such as Purge the Foe, where losing the squad feeds their score.
entries.unit_types: Glass-cannon squads that ride in transports: Drukhari Incubi / Wyches / Kabalites, Ork Boyz / Tankbustas, Marine melta or assault teams.
entries.rules_basis: 18.04 modes (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3013-3057). 18.06 assault disembark through faction grants (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/SPACE_MARINES_GENERIC.md:16-19). 11.02 / 11.04 charge rules (:1603-1650). The trade judgement itself is player opinion (YouTube finding F025: medium confidence, 4 channels).

entries.name: Ingress a loaded transport and Rapid-disembark the cargo the same turn
entries.description: Units inside a TRANSPORT in strategic reserves arrive with it; they cannot make an ingress move themselves. After the transport's ingress move, the cargo may disembark in rapid mode in the same phase. Every model must obey the transport's ingress restrictions (more than 8″ from all enemy units; not in the opponent's deployment zone before round 3), and the cargo cannot charge. Cargo inside a transport that has made an ingress move is also safe from the end-of-round-3 reserves destruction.
entries.when_to_use: Rounds 2-3, to put scoring or action units onto an edge or flank objective, or to deliver two units with one arrival.
entries.unit_types: A TRANSPORT in strategic reserves, and its cargo.
entries.rules_basis: 20.04 eligibility excludes units embarked in transports that are themselves in reserves (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3258-3260). 18.04: rapid mode after an ingress move; the models follow the transport's ingress rules; they cannot charge afterwards (:3030-3052, with its sidebar; 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:635). 20.04: end-of-round-3 exception (:3276-3281). 20.01: the 50% points cap counts embarked units (:3205-3216).

entries.name: Relocate a unit through strategic reserves (Da Jump, Teleport-shunter, Shokk Attack Engine)
entries.description: Use an own-turn ability that puts a unit into strategic reserves so it can arrive somewhere else. Weirdboy Da Jump: a psychic roll in the Movement phase, once per army per battle round; the unit goes into reserves with Deep Strike, and on a 1 it is also battle-shocked. Shield-Captain in Allarus, Archeotech Teleport-shunter: once per battle, if unengaged and not yet selected to move; it goes into reserves and must ingress this phase. Wazdakka Gutsmek, Shokk Attack Engine: Command phase, if unengaged. With Deep Strike the unit can drop anywhere more than 8″ from enemies, even in the enemy deployment zone, leaving a dead-end position without a Fall Back. A unit relocated after it was already selected to move cannot ingress again this phase (each unit is selected once). Repositioned units are exempt from the round-3 destruction.
entries.when_to_use: The unit is 15″ or more from every useful objective or target, or would be charged or shot off with no other escape, and a better spot more than 8″ from all enemies exists. Avoid it when: the unit's OC is holding a contested objective (it stops scoring where it was, which costs most under Take and Hold-style cards); the unit is Condemned by the opponent's Punishment card (leaving the battlefield pays them); or it is round 1 (strategic reserves cannot arrive until round 2).
entries.unit_types: Weirdboy (and its attached unit), Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, Wazdakka Gutsmek. Chapter-only equivalents are out of scope.
entries.move_type: other (ability: place in strategic reserves), then Reserves arrival
entries.rules_basis: 20.02 repositioned units: such rules can be used on units that already moved; a unit set up again the same turn still counts as having made its advance, fall-back or disembark move (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3219-3235). 20.03 (:3250-3254). 20.04, including the repositioned-unit exemption (:3276-3283). 24.09 (:3649-3655). 09.02: each unit is selected once per phase (:1345-1356). entries.name: Drop in during battle round 1 with a first-turn ingress grant
entries.description: Strategic reserves cannot normally arrive in round 1, but some rules allow an ingress in your first Movement phase: Ork aircraft with Impulsive Recon; Space Marine Terminators with the Corporeum Reliquary; the Custodes Shield-Captain in Allarus with Lightning Descent; Drop Pod / Termite Assault (the cargo must disembark more than 8″ from enemies when it lands); and Logan Grimnar's High King of Fenris (one unit treats the round as one higher). Boss Snikrot's Deff from the Shadows (end of the opponent's Movement phase, from round 1) is not implemented. The aim is to take a far objective or hit an exposed backline unit before the opponent's screens and Rapid Ingress denial are in place. A round-1 ingress still cannot enter the enemy deployment zone unless the unit has Deep Strike.

entries.name: Embark a slow unit to taxi it (ride the transport this phase or next)
entries.description: Use a transport to move a unit that is badly out of position. The unit makes its Normal or Advance move so that every model ends within 3″ of a transport that has not yet been selected to move, and embarks; the transport then makes its own move carrying it. Next turn it tactical-disembarks (3″ + M, keeps the charge) or rapid-disembarks after another transport move. Total reach: its own move plus the transport's move this turn, then 3″ + M (or transport M + 3″) next turn. It cannot disembark again in the phase it embarked, and a unit set up this turn (disembarked or arrived from reserves) cannot embark.
entries.when_to_use: Slow infantry is far from the objective or fight it is needed at within 1-2 turns, and a transport with capacity is within reach and not needed for anything else. Unlike TRN-05, the purpose is distance, not protection.
entries.unit_types: Slow infantry, and a friendly TRANSPORT with capacity.
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance, then Embark (the transport then makes a Normal / Advance move)
entries.rules_basis: 18.02 Embarking: after a normal, advance or fall-back move; all models within 3″; not set up this turn; enough capacity (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2981-2997). 18.04 eligibility: 'did not embark within that TRANSPORT this phase' (:3023) is the only same-phase restriction. No 11e text bars the transport from moving after a unit embarks, and 09.02 lets the transport, not yet selected, be selected afterwards (:1345-1356). FAQ: a rule letting a unit embark in the turn it disembarked overrides 18.02 (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:621-622). Engine: DisembarkMove.gd:49-51 (embarked_this_phase only blocks disembarking); MovementPhase.gd:9176-9182. first-principles#84 marked this unconfirmed; the local text has no restriction.

entries.name: Fall back and embark to pull a unit out of combat
entries.description: An engaged unit makes a Fall Back move (Ordered Retreat, or Desperate Escape with hazard rolls if it is battle-shocked) that ends with every model within 3″ of a friendly transport with room, and then embarks. entries.name: Arrive as a blocker or denial screen
entries.description: Bring a cheap reserve unit in to plug a gap. Its 8″ no-arrival zone denies the opponent's own reserves (their ingress, Deep Strike and Rapid Ingress must all be more than 8″ from our units), and it can body-block an objective approach or block a movement lane. A unit that arrives in our Movement phase is already in place when the opponent's Rapid Ingress window opens at the end of that phase.
entries.when_to_use: The enemy still has units in reserves (or CP for Rapid Ingress) and our screen has a hole, for example after casualties; or an objective approach needs blocking for a turn.
entries.unit_types: Cheap reserve units (single models or small units, where OC does not matter).
entries.rules_basis: 20.04: 'more than 8″ horizontally from all enemy units' also binds the opponent's arrivals (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3264-3266). 24.09 (:3649-3655). 15.07 Rapid Ingress timing (:2714-2731). Engine: GameConstants.gd:44-49.

entries.name: Park loaded transports where an emergency disembark is survivable
entries.description: If a loaded transport is destroyed, each passenger makes a hazard roll and must be set up within 6″ of it, as close as possible. Per the errata, a model is set up engaged only if no unengaged spot exists, and models that still cannot be placed are destroyed. The unit is battle-shocked and cannot charge. The transport's Deadly Demise (on a 6) then hits every unit within 6″, passengers included, and in the Fight phase overrun fights can catch them. So avoid ending a loaded transport's move against board edges, impassable or Solid terrain, or where enemies can surround it, and keep it out of reach of enemy melee and anti-tank fire where you can.
entries.when_to_use: Every move of a loaded transport that ends within enemy charge or anti-tank range.
entries.unit_types: TRANSPORTs carrying cargo.
entries.rules_basis: 18.03 / 18.05 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2999-3007, 3061-3078), with the 18.05 errata (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:609). 06.03 hazard rolls (:1067-1072). 24.08 Deadly Demise: resolved after the emergency disembark; hits each unit within 6″ (:3670-3699). The core-rules Fight phase example shows an overrun fight on a unit that has just emergency-disembarked (:1880-1916). Correction to core-rules#75: under the errata, models are set up engaged before any are destroyed.

entries.name: Stage within 6″ or 9″ of an edge, unengaged, to keep an end-of-turn extraction
entries.description: Several rules put a unit back into strategic reserves at the end of the opponent's Fight phase, so it can drop again next turn, but only if it is unengaged, and some also need it near an edge or Hidden. Gated: Da Big Hunt INSTINCTIVE HUNTERS (Beast Snagga within 6″ of an edge), Saga of the Beastslayer CO-ORDINATED STRIKE (Blood Claws / Thunderwolf Cavalry / Wulfen within 9″ of an edge), Boss Snikrot's Kunnin' Infiltrator (hidden). Ungated, but still needing the unit unengaged: TACTICAL WITHDRAWAL (Phobos / Scouts), On Gilded Wings (Custodes Terminators), Deffkoptas' Aerial Manoover, Inceptors' Parabolic Jetleap, Venatari's Take Wing, Kayvaan Shrike's Echo of the Ravenspire. End this Movement phase's move, and later moves, where the gate will be met and the enemy cannot easily lock the unit in combat. Repositioned units are not destroyed at the end of round 3.
entries.when_to_use: A fast or expensive unit will be exposed after it acts, dropping in again next turn reaches a better target or objective, and CP for the stratagem is available.
entries.unit_types: Beast Snagga, Blood Claws / Thunderwolf Cavalry / Wulfen, Boss Snikrot, Deffkoptas, Inceptors, Venatari, Custodes Terminators, Kayvaan Shrike, Phobos / Scout squads.

entries.name: Counter-drop with Rapid Ingress into the gap the opponent's move left
entries.description:
At the end of the opponent's Movement phase (battle round 2+), spend 1CP to make an ingress move with a strategic-reserves unit after seeing every enemy move. Land on or next to an objective they vacated or left lightly held, behind their advance, within next-turn shooting or charge reach of a priority target, or in a hole in your own denial screen. The unit is set up more than 8″ from every enemy unit: wholly within 6″ of an edge and outside their deployment zone before round 3, or anywhere with Deep Strike. Their Shooting and Charge phases come next, so prefer spots out of sight or Hidden and outside likely charge reach. The ingress no-move restriction ends at the start of their Charge phase, so the unit moves, shoots and charges normally in your turn. A unit landing 8-12″ from an enemy can even Heroic Intervene at the end of that Charge phase. Faction rules change the price and anchor point:
- Swift Ruin and Leonine Ferocity: -1CP and outside the once-per-phase limit, so two units can drop.
- Grimnar's Mark: -1CP.
- Teleport Homer: -1CP, set up within 3″ of its token.
This needs a unit still in reserve. As the second player in round 2, this window comes before your own first arrival.
entries.when_to_use:
All of these apply:
- Round 2 or later.
- A non-AIRCRAFT, non-battle-shocked unit is still in strategic reserves.
- You have 1CP to spare.
- After the opponent's moves there is an empty or weakly held objective, an exposed enemy unit, or a hole in your screen.
- A legal landing spot covers that opportunity without being exposed to heavy shooting or likely charges in their remaining phases.
entries.unit_types: Strategic-reserves units, best with Deep Strike: Terminators, jump-pack and bike units, Inceptors, Venatari, Deffkoptas, Stormboyz. Never AIRCRAFT.
entries.move_type: Ingress move (20.04) via the Rapid Ingress stratagem. Adjacent: end of the opponent's Movement phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- 15.07 Rapid Ingress: WHEN end of your opponent's Movement phase; TARGET one strategic-reserves unit (excluding AIRCRAFT); not in the first battle round (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2714-2729).
- 20.04 ingress: wholly within 6″ of an edge; more than 8″ from all enemy units; no models in the opponent's DZ before round 3; no other move until the start of the next Charge phase (:3255-3273).
- 24.09 Deep Strike: anywhere more than 8″ away, even in the opponent's DZ (:3649-3662).
- 15.01: the same stratagem once per phase, and one stratagem per unit per phase (:2498-2501).
- 01.07: battle-shocked units can't be targeted by stratagems (:216-217).
- 13.09 Hidden: light/dense terrain after the errata (:2292-2302; 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:529).
- Engine: StratagemManager.gd:5068-5076 (end_of_phase, not_battle_round 1). Placement is validated at the 11e 8″ (MovementPhase.gd:2340-2452, via GameConstants.reinforcement_min_enemy_distance_inches, GameConstants.gd:49-50).
- The delta audit's notes 'start of any opponent phase' and 'Rapid Ingress still 9″' (11th_edition_delta_audit.md:141, :159) are stale: 15.07's WHEN and the current validator contradict them.

entries.coverage_detail:
What exists: evaluate_rapid_ingress (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28121-28334, called from AIPlayer.gd:1306).
- It declines below 1CP, or with the last CP before round 4 (:28139-28147).
- It scores each reserve with the own-turn arrival scorer _score_reserves_deployment (:7949-8017: points, deep strike, melee/ranged, one best objective), then adds +3 in R4+, +1 in R3 and -1 for the CP (:28164-28172). It uses Rapid Ingress at a score of 3.0 or more.
- Placement reuses _compute_reinforcement_positions (:8019+). Its candidate filter is 9″ + base + 0.6″ (:8027-8029), and it ranks objective proximity plus an enemy 10-15″ away.
What is missing:
- Nothing diffs the board before and after the opponent's move (vacated objectives, exposed units, screen holes).
- Nothing weighs exposure to the opponent's Shooting and Charge phases.
- Double drops and faction discounts are unknown to the AI: Swift Ruin, Leonine Ferocity and Grimnar's Mark have 0 grep hits, and Teleport Homer scores 0.0 at SMAbilitiesB.gd:1827-1828.
- Own-turn arrival always lands reserves at the first chance (_decide_reserves_arrival :7728), so a unit is rarely still held for this window.
entries.engine_support:
Reuse:
- _score_reserves_deployment (:7949) and _compute_reinforcement_positions / _generate_strategic_reserves_candidates (:8019, :8073).
- _evaluate_all_objectives (:8926).
- _calculate_enemy_threat_data and _evaluate_position_threat (:28695, :28794).
- _position_would_be_hidden (:28515) and _charge_success_probability (:18928).
New:
- Snapshot the board at the start of the opponent's Movement phase, to diff objective states and exposed units against it.
- A next-turn reach term: targets shootable or chargeable from the landing spot.
- Drop the 9″ filter to GameConstants.reinforcement_min_enemy_distance_inches.
- A keep-in-reserve option in _decide_reserves_arrival.
entries.value_reason: The corpus treats keeping a Rapid Ingress answer in reserve as standard 11e play (F013, F029). It is the only arrival made after seeing the opponent's whole move, and it costs 1CP. The AI's version is a generic arrival score that ignores what the opponent's move just changed.
absorbed: OBJ-36 (Rapid Ingress onto an open objective (adjacent: end of the opponent's Movement phase))

entries.name: Infiltrate or Scout forward onto objectives that score in round 1
entries.description:
Use either pre-battle option to start in range of a non-home objective:
- The Scout move: up to X″, starting wholly within your deployment zone and ending more than 8″ from all enemy units. A DEDICATED TRANSPORT whose passengers all have Scouts can make it instead.
- Infiltrators set-up: anywhere more than 8″ from the opponent's deployment zone and all enemy units.
The objective is then yours at the first end-of-phase, end-of-turn or Command-phase check, and the early cards pay. Per missions#67 these include:
- Central holds (Immovable Object, Search and Scour).
- Non-home holds (Outmanoeuvre).
- Majorities (Battlefield Dominance, Inescapable Dominion).
- Round-1 actions (Secure Asset, Sabotage, Death Trap, Smoke and Mirrors, Vanguard Operation).
- Tactical cards: Display of Might, Centre Ground, Outflank, Plunder, Cleanse, Engage on All Fronts.
Pre-battle rules alternate starting with the first-turn player, so the turn order is already known. When going second, choose spots the opponent can't wipe out on turn 1.

entries.name: Wrap engaged enemies so their only way out is Desperate Escape
entries.description:
When charging, piling in and consolidating, place models all around the enemy unit, far side included, so no Ordered Retreat path exists. Bases can't move through enemy models, and a fall-back must end unengaged (more than 2″ from all your models). The enemy then has two choices:
- Stay locked. It loses normal shooting: MONSTER/VEHICLE units keep close-quarters shooting at -1, and other units can only use [CLOSE-QUARTERS] weapons against units engaged with them. It also can't start actions or walk onto objectives.
- Desperate Escape. It makes a hazard roll per model (a 1-2 inflicts 1 mortal wound, or 3 if every model is MONSTER/VEHICLE) plus a battle-shock roll, and still can't shoot, charge or start actions afterwards.
MONSTER/VEHICLE models pass through enemy models only on normal and advance moves, so wrapped vehicles pay the full Desperate Escape price. FLY units (taking to the skies on the fall-back) and Super-Heavy Walkers get out, so don't spend models wrapping them.
entries.when_to_use: Your multi-model melee unit is engaged, or about to be, with a valuable non-FLY unit you want stuck or hurt by hazard rolls: an infantry shooter, an objective holder or a vehicle. You need enough models and pile-in or consolidation reach to close its perimeter.
entries.unit_types: Multi-model melee units (Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Gretchin, Assault Intercessors, Blood Claws, Wulfen). Best targets are non-FLY vehicles and gunlines.
entries.move_type: Charge move (11.04), pile-in (12.03), consolidation (12.08). Adjacent: Charge and Fight phases.
entries.rules_basis:
- 03.01: a base can't be moved through enemy models (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:388).
- 09.07: Ordered Retreat vs Desperate Escape. Only Desperate Escape moves through enemy models; the move ends unengaged; no shooting, charging or actions afterwards; Desperate Escape adds a battle-shock roll (:1417-1442).
- 06.03 hazard rolls (:1067-1074). 03.04 engagement range 2″ (:539-541).
- 10.04 normal shooting needs an unengaged unit (:1489-1491); 10.06 close-quarters shooting (:1522-1547).
- 17.01: MONSTER/VEHICLE models pass through models only on normal and advance moves (:2869-2874). FAQ: other move types pass through friendly models only (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:598).
- 21.03: take to the skies on a fall-back (:3358-3373). 24.35 Super-Heavy Walker (:3940-3960).
- Constraints on the wrapping moves: 11.04 (:1640-1665), 12.03 (:1737-1766), 12.08 Engaging mode (:1947-1975).

It takes the first legal slot and never checks whether the enemy's retreat is actually closed. Charge placement only covers the declared targets (_compute_charge_move :19797-20324), and pile-in moves each model straight at the closest enemy model (_compute_pile_in_movements :21352). The lock does less against MONSTER/VEHICLE shooting, because close-quarters shooting still works at -1.

entries.name: Consolidate into a fresh enemy unit to lock it (Engaging Consolidation)
entries.description:
A unit that fought may end unengaged but within 3″ of other enemy units. If it moves, it must use Engaging Consolidation: up to 3″, each moved model ends closer to the closest selected unit, and the unit must end engaged with every selected unit. Selected units that have not fought must then fight it at once.
Pick targets your unit survives and that lose the most from being locked into their next turn:
- Non-MONSTER/VEHICLE shooters. They can then only use [CLOSE-QUARTERS] weapons against units engaged with them, and a fall-back means no shooting.
- Action or objective units. Engaged units can't start actions, and neither can a unit that falls back.
Locked MONSTER/VEHICLE units still shoot (close-quarters, at -1) and can still be shot by your army, so they are weaker lock targets. TACTICAL FOCUS (consolidate D3+3″) extends the reach; target-selection distances don't change.
entries.when_to_use:
At the end of any Fight phase (both players consolidate), when all of these apply:
- An enemy infantry shooter, actor or objective holder is within 3″ of your unengaged unit.
- Your unit survives its attacks.
- The lock lasts into the enemy's next turn.

entries.move_type: Consolidation move, Engaging mode (12.08). Adjacent: Fight phase.

- 12.08 Engaging mode and the forced fights (:1947-1989). The errata extends the forced fight to Ongoing consolidations (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:492). Distance FAQs (:493-498).
- 16.01: engaged units, and units that fell back, can't start actions (:2807-2815).
- 09.07: no shooting or charging after a fall-back (:1437-1439).
- 10.06 close-quarters shooting (:1522-1547); 17.03 shooting at engaged MONSTER/VEHICLE units (:2898-2908).
- TACTICAL FOCUS: .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/RULES.md:635.

entries.name: Make a reactive move into cover or out of sight before their shooting (move into cover)
entries.description:
Reactive moves trigger when an enemy ends a move within 8″ (RESPONSIVE TACTICS, SWIFT AS THE EAGLE, SCARPER! ...) or when an enemy unit shoots your unit (BATTLE INSTINCTS). Use the normal move to do one of these:
- Put an obscuring terrain area between your unit and the enemy shooters that haven't fired yet.
- Step inside a terrain area for cover.
- Become Hidden: INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM inside a terrain area with light or dense terrain can be seen only within 15″ detection range.
Hidden also needs no ranged attacks this turn or last turn. A unit that shot in your turn gets only the line-of-sight and cover benefit. The move must end unengaged, it is the unit's one normal move this phase, and it cancels any action the unit is performing.
entries.when_to_use: A reactive trigger fired for an unengaged unit and enemy shooting that hasn't fired yet can see it. A spot within the move cap breaks line of sight, or gives cover or Hidden, without giving up an objective needed at the end of their turn or an action in progress.

entries.coverage_detail:
Each codex ai_score decides use or decline (decide_window_stratagem, AIDecisionMaker.gd:26859), and none of them looks at line of sight:
- RESPONSIVE TACTICS / TRANSHUMAN REACTIONS pay only when an objective is reachable (SMCodexAMovement.gd:271-278).
- SCARPER! / WHIRLIGIG EVASION pay only against a live charge threat, and never from an objective (OrkCodexMovement.gd:300-309).
- BATTLE INSTINCTS pays only when an objective is within 4″ (SWCodexMovement.gd:164-167).
- SWIFT AS THE EAGLE scores 0.0 (CustodesCodexMovement.gd:255-256), and the post-shooting window version is always declined (AIDecisionMaker.gd:16397-16416).
- Supreme Kunnin' scores a flat 1.5 (OrkAbilities11e.gd:2327-2328).
- Evade and Survive, Predatory Instinct and Knight Champion score 0.0 (SMAbilitiesA.gd:2284-2285, SWAbilities11e.gd:1839-1840, SMAbilitiesC.gd:1930-1931).
Placement is the engine's auto-solver. It translates the unit straight away from the trigger, or toward the nearest objective the player doesn't control (MovementPhase.gd:6439-6525). The 'normal' solver in ReactiveMove11e only targets objectives (ReactiveMove11e.gd:315-358).

entries.name: Consolidate onto an objective (Objective Consolidation) in either player's Fight phase
entries.description:
This applies to a unit that fought, is unengaged, has no enemy within 3″ and is within 3″ of an objective. If it moves, it must use Objective Consolidation: up to 3″, each moved model ends in range of the selected objective if possible (closer if not), and the unit must end in range. It adds OC just before the end-of-phase and end-of-turn checks:
- In your Fight phase: for end-of-turn holds and Command-phase scoring. Pile-in and consolidation moves don't cancel an action in progress.
- In the opponent's Fight phase: to stand on an objective at the end of THEIR turn. This feeds Burden of Trust, Defend Stronghold and Display of Might's opponent-turn tier, contests their scoring or action completion, or claims the objective for your next Command phase.
With several objectives within 3″, pick by value, not distance. Set it up earlier by finishing charges and pile-ins within 3″ of the target objective and more than 3″ from other enemies (ADJ-19). TACTICAL FOCUS (D3+3″) extends the reach.
entries.when_to_use: At the end of every Fight phase, for each unit that fought, when an objective is within 3″ and no enemy is within 3″. It matters most just before an end-of-turn scoring check.
entries.unit_types: Any unit that was eligible to fight this phase.
entries.move_type: Consolidation move, Objective mode (12.08). Adjacent: Fight phase, yours or the opponent's.
entries.rules_basis:
- 12.07: both players consolidate, active player first, optional per unit (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1934-1941).
- 12.08: modes in order Ongoing, Engaging, Objective. Objective mode applies within 3″ of objectives, and the unit must end within range of the selected one (:1942-1989).
- 14.02: control is checked at the end of each phase and turn; being within range of a terrain objective means being within its area (:2401-2423).
- 16.01: pile-in and consolidation moves don't cancel actions (:2824-2828).
- Card timing: missionCards.json burden-of-trust (:2225), display-of-might (:2246) and defend-stronghold (:2706) score at the end of the opponent's turn.
- TACTICAL FOCUS: space-marines/RULES.md:635.

entries.name: Infiltrate or Scout a forward screen against enemy infiltrators, scouts and deep strikers
entries.description:
Every model on the table makes an 8″ zone where enemy units can't be set up or end certain moves:
- Enemy Infiltrators must set up more than 8″ from all enemy units.
- Enemy scout moves must end more than 8″ away.
- Ingress and deep strike must be more than 8″ away.
Put a cheap Infiltrators or Scouts unit forward, spread with 2″/9″ coherency, to push enemy infiltrators and scouts back from your lines and to deny landing spots near your objectives and backfield. The screen keeps working through the opponent's Rapid Ingress window as long as it survives.
entries.when_to_use:
When all of these apply:
- The opponent fields Infiltrators, Scouts or deep strikers (for example Emperor's Children).
- You have a cheap forward-capable unit.
- Your near objectives or a flank would otherwise be open.
Pre-battle rules alternate starting with the first-turn player, so a screen placed first also shapes their scout moves.
entries.unit_types: Cheap Infiltrators or Scouts units: Gretchin with Minefield Detail, Scout Squads, Incursors, Kommandos.
entries.move_type: Infiltrators set-up (24.20) / Scout move (24.32). Adjacent: pre-battle.
entries.rules_basis:
- 24.20 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3754-3762) and 24.32 (:3884-3901): more than 8″ from enemy units.
- 20.04: ingress more than 8″ away (:3255-3273). 24.09: deep strike more than 8″ away (:3649-3662).
- 03.03: coherency 2″ and 9″ (:514-537).
- FAQ: pre-battle rules alternate starting with the first-turn player (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:696-697).
- Engine: GameConstants.reinforcement_min_enemy_distance_inches / infiltrators_min_enemy_distance_inches (GameConstants.gd:49-61); ScoutPhase._scout_min_enemy_distance_inches (ScoutPhase.gd:182-184).

entries.name: Decline consolidation when the forced mode would hurt you
entries.description:
Consolidation is optional per unit, but once a unit moves its mode is forced:
- Within 3″ of an enemy, it must Engaging-consolidate. It ends engaged with every selected unit, and unfought units fight it now.
- Otherwise, within 3″ of an objective, it must move into that objective's range.
Stay put when the forced move would get the unit killed, release a dangerous enemy's attacks, pull it off an objective it already holds, or move it out of the cover or terrain area that keeps it Hidden.
entries.when_to_use: At the end of the Fight phase, when the forced mode would engage a unit that out-fights you, or drag you off an objective or out of cover, and staying still keeps OC or protection.
entries.unit_types: Any unit that fought.
entries.rules_basis:
- 12.07: players consolidate 'with all of their eligible units they choose to move' (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1934-1941). The Fight-phase sidebar says 'you don't have to pile in or consolidate with a unit if you don't want to' (:1720-1727).
- 12.08: the mandatory mode order and the forced fights (:1947-1989). Errata: 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:492.
- Selecting modes commentary (errata_faq:462).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1720-1727, 1934-1989
Web search snippet: 'skipping consolidation matters more in 11th edition, because an unengaged unit with enemies inside 3″ is forced into an Engaging Consolidation if it moves at all'
docs/rules/11th_edition_delta_audit.md §3 (12.07-12.08: one move per unit, optional per unit)
40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd:20530-20549 (CONSOLIDATE taken whenever offered)
entries.coverage_detail: The Fight AI takes every CONSOLIDATE offer (AIDecisionMaker.gd:20533-20539) and moves in whatever mode the range gates give (:21861-21966). It sends END_CONSOLIDATION only once nothing is left (:20541-20549). No branch ever declines. An empty-movements CONSOLIDATE is already used as a skip for AIRCRAFT (:21748-21756), so a decline is mechanically available.
entries.engine_support:
Reuse _estimate_incoming_melee_damage (:12350), _estimate_melee_damage (:19576), _unit_has_model_in_control_range (:13269) and TerrainManager.is_model_hidden (TerrainManager.gd:1001).
New: a consolidate-vs-stay comparison in _compute_consolidate_action that emits the empty CONSOLIDATE when staying is better.
entries.value_reason: It prevents self-inflicted losses (forced engagements, lost objectives), and it is cheap to add once consolidation options are scored.
entries.errata_note: An engaged unit that consolidates must use Ongoing Consolidation, and under the errata any enemy unit it is then engaged with that hasn't been selected to fight this phase must fight it now. So declining applies to engaged units too, and Engaging mode is only for unengaged units within 3″ of an enemy. — 12.08 errata, Ongoing Consolidation (errata_faq:492)

entries.name: Heroic Intervention (Leap to Defend) into a unit that just charged
entries.description:
At the end of the opponent's Charge phase, for 1CP, an unengaged unit within 12″ of enemies resolves a charge whose targets can only be units that made a charge move this phase and are within the 2D6 roll. Use it to join a fight the enemy started: counter-hit the charger now, since it fights in their Fight phase as well as yours, and protect or add OC around the friend or objective it charged.
The charge gives your unit Fights First. The active player starts the Fights First alternation, though, so their chargers usually still swing first.
Costs: the unit may leave an objective (control is checked at the end of every phase and turn), and it starts your turn engaged, so it can only Fall Back or stay, and can't charge.
Faction discounts: Countercharge (AA CHARACTER, -1CP), Laurels of Vigilance, Celeritous Sentries, Grimnar's Mark.
entries.when_to_use:
When all of these apply:
- An enemy charge landed within 12″ of your unengaged melee unit.
- The trade is good and you have 1CP.
- The unit isn't needed on an objective at the end of their turn.
- It didn't rapid-disembark this turn.
entries.unit_types: Unengaged melee-capable units within 12″ of the charger, not battle-shocked. A VEHICLE only if it is a CHARACTER or WALKER.
entries.move_type: Charge move (11.04) via Heroic Intervention (15.11). Adjacent: end of the opponent's Charge phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- 15.11: WHEN end of your opponent's Charge phase. TARGET an unengaged unit within 12″ of enemy units; a VEHICLE only if CHARACTER/WALKER. Leap to Defend: only units that made a charge move this phase (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2734-2766).
- 11.02 / 11.04 charge: targets within 12″ and within the roll; models that can engage must; Fights First until end of turn (:1603-1665).
- 12.04: the Fights First alternation starts with the active player (:1830-1832).
- 15.01 limits (:2498-2501). 01.07: no stratagems on battle-shocked units (:216-217).
- FAQ: a unit that rapid-disembarked this turn can't be targeted (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:610-611).
- Discounts: space-marines/RULES.md:366 (Countercharge), :709 (Laurels of Vigilance); custodes/RULES.md:165 (Celeritous Sentries); space-marines/SPACE_WOLVES.md:50 (Grimnar's Mark).
- Correction: first-principles#103 and web#75 say Heroic Intervention gives no Fights First. 15.11 resolves a charge, and 11.04 grants Fights First (:1664-1665). The engine withholds it 'Per 10e rules' (ChargePhase.gd:4092-4099).

entries.coverage_detail:
What exists: evaluate_heroic_intervention (AIDecisionMaker.gd:27770-27976, called at :18277).
- It scores eligible melee units by unit value x0.5, +2 for CHARACTER, +1 for MONSTER, then x1.3 / x0.7 by target value.

entries.name: Counter-charge to lock a dangerous shooter or action unit before your turn (Into the Fray, NO ESCAPE)
entries.description:
Into the Fray (+1CP, 2CP total; roll capped at 6; targets any enemy within 6″) lets an unengaged unit charge a unit that did NOT charge: a shooter, objective holder or actor that crept close. The target fights now and stays engaged into its next turn. Then it must Fall Back, which means no shooting, charging or actions afterwards unless a rule allows it, or stay locked. While engaged it can't Fire Overwatch or Heroic Intervene, and non-MONSTER/VEHICLE units can only shoot [CLOSE-QUARTERS] weapons at units engaged with them.
Shadowkeepers NO ESCAPE (2CP, opponent's Movement phase) does the same to a unit that just fell back within 6″.
Costs:
- In your turn you can't shoot a locked non-MONSTER/VEHICLE target.
- Your unit starts your turn engaged.
- Locking a MONSTER/VEHICLE barely reduces its shooting: close-quarters shooting works at -1.
entries.when_to_use:
At the end of the opponent's Charge phase (NO ESCAPE: right after an enemy fall-back), when all of these apply:
- A high-output non-vehicle shooter, actor or objective holder is within 6″ and within the capped roll.
- You have 2CP.
- Your unit survives the target's attacks.
entries.unit_types: Durable melee units (a VEHICLE only if CHARACTER/WALKER); Custodes Infantry for NO ESCAPE.
entries.move_type: Charge move (11.04) via Heroic Intervention Into the Fray (15.11) or NO ESCAPE. Adjacent: opponent's Charge or Movement phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- 15.11 Into the Fray: +1CP, roll capped at 6, targets within 6″ (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2756-2765). FAQ: a +1CP section makes the original cost 2CP (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:576-577).
- 09.07: after a fall-back, no shooting, charging or starting actions (:1437-1439).
- 15.08 Fire Overwatch and 15.11 both need an unengaged unit (:2741-2742, :2745-2746).
- 16.01: engaged units can't start actions (:2807-2815).
- 10.06 close-quarters shooting (:1522-1547); 17.03: only engaged MONSTER/VEHICLE units can be shot (:2898-2908).
- NO ESCAPE: .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/custodes/RULES.md:141.
- Correction: the engine and the AI price Into the Fray at 1CP (StratagemManager.gd:5110-5118; ChargePhase.gd:3858-3898; AIDecisionMaker.gd:27785-27790).

entries.name: Rapid Ingress to score or deny at the end of the opponent's turn
entries.description:
Land where scoring at the end of the opponent's turn is decided, whether it is their card or one of your own opponent-turn cards:
- Wholly in no-man's-land, for Display of Might's 5VP opponent-turn tier.
- Within 6″ (or 3″) of the centre, more than 8″ from their units, to break their Centre Ground.
- Inside the terrain area in your territory where their Vanguard Operation actor stands, which voids 'no enemy units within that terrain area'.
- On your home objective and in your deployment zone, for Defend Stronghold or Burden of Trust.
- In range of an objective they are about to score.
entries.when_to_use: From round 2, when you hold a reserve unit and an end-of-turn award (theirs or one of your opponent-turn cards) hinges on a zone a legal ingress spot reaches: more than 8″ from their units, and within 6″ of an edge unless the unit has Deep Strike.
entries.unit_types: Strategic-reserves units, best with Deep Strike; never AIRCRAFT.
entries.move_type: Ingress move (20.04) via Rapid Ingress (15.07). Adjacent: end of the opponent's Movement phase.
entries.rules_basis:

- 14.02: control at the end of each phase and turn (:2401-2423).
- Card timings in missionCards.json: display-of-might (:2246; 5VP at the end of the opponent's turn), centre-ground (:2311; enemy within 3″ or 6″ of the centre denies), vanguard-operation (:1597; completes if no enemy units are within the terrain area), defend-stronghold (:2706), burden-of-trust (:2225), beacon (:2826).

entries.name: Heroic Intervene onto the objective or terrain area the enemy is scoring from
entries.description:
Use Heroic Intervention so your unit ends engaged with, and usually within range of, the objective or area the opponent needs at the end of THEIR turn. Per missions#64 this can:
- Contest their OC, so actions that complete 'if it controls the objective' fail: Secure Asset, Sabotage, Cleanse, Decoy, Triangulate, Extract Intelligence, Maintain Control, Sensor Sweep.
- Break their end-of-turn holds (Outmanoeuvre, Immovable Object, Inescapable Dominion).
- Void Vanguard Operation's 'no enemy units within this terrain area'.
- Enter the centre against Centre Ground.
- Move your own unit into no-man's-land, or out of your territory, for your own opponent-turn cards.
entries.when_to_use:
In the opponent's turn, when all of these apply:
- Their end-of-turn award or action completion hinges on an objective or area within your Heroic Intervention reach: within 12″ of an enemy, and Into the Fray targets within 6″.
- You have the CP.
- Your unit's OC will count, because it isn't battle-shocked.
