entries.name: Make a reactive move out of the triggering enemy's charge reach
entries.description: An enemy that can still declare a charge this turn may end a move within 8″ of your unit. Use the reactive normal move to open the gap beyond its likely charge (targets must be within 12″ and within the 2D6 roll), or to put terrain or friendly units in its path. Don't do it when the unit is needed on an objective at the end of their turn.
entries.when_to_use: The triggering enemy is melee-capable and didn't Advance or Fall Back, your unit fights poorly, and the move doesn't leave an objective you need or break an action.
entries.unit_types: Reactive-move units, as in ADJ-05: Gretchin (SCARPER!), Deffkoptas (WHIRLIGIG EVASION), Gladius units, Phobos units, Trusted Sentinels, and others.
entries.move_type: Normal move (09.05) granted reactively. Adjacent: opponent's Movement phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- 09.05 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1390-1399); one normal move per phase (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:470).
- 11.02 charge eligibility: within 12″, not advanced or fallen back (:1603-1629).
- 11.04: targets within 12″ and within the roll (:1640-1661). FAQ: targets must be within the roll including modifiers (errata_faq:161).
- Rule texts: SCARPER! (orks/RULES.md:223), WHIRLIGIG EVASION (orks/RULES.md:268).
evidence: YouTube TacticalTortoise 40k VqwMdS9MuIY @60:00 — “it has the ability to reactive move to enemies going close to it ... it may be able to jump away” [F014]
https://www.tabletopbattles.com/40k-11th-edition-force-disposition-review-reconnaissance/ (search summary: reactive moves used to run away from charges)
40k/scripts/stratagems/ork_codex/OrkCodexMovement.gd:300-309; 40k/phases/MovementPhase.gd:6443-6510
entries.coverage_detail:
Only the Ork units do this today. SCARPER! and WHIRLIGIG EVASION pay 2.0 only when the triggering enemy could still charge this unit, and never from an objective (OrkCodexMovement.gd:300-309, _charge_threat). The engine's AI solver then moves the unit straight away from the trigger ('away' goal, MovementPhase.gd:6503-6510), trying headings up to 180° at 100/75/50/25% of the cap (:6443-6500).
The other armies' reactive moves never use this purpose:
- RESPONSIVE TACTICS / TRANSHUMAN REACTIONS are objective-only (SMCodexAMovement.gd:271-278).
- SWIFT AS THE EAGLE, Evade and Survive and Predatory Instinct score 0.0 (CustodesCodexMovement.gd:255-256).
The resulting gap is never checked against charge odds or terrain.
entries.engine_support:
Reuse _charge_success_probability and _charge_roll_needed (:18928, :18840), TerrainManager.calculate_charge_terrain_penalty (TerrainManager.gd:509) and _evaluate_position_threat (:28794).
New: a charge-odds term in the shared reactive-move destination scorer (ADJ-05).
entries.value_reason: It saves fragile units from charges using information only available mid-turn. Several armies have the tool, but only the Orks use it, and crudely.

entries.name: Make a reactive move onto an objective (grab it, or retake it after they disengage)
entries.description: Use an out-of-turn normal move to step into range of an objective before the opponent's end-of-phase or end-of-turn control check: one the mover just left, or one nobody holds. Taktikal Brigade WHILE THEIR BACKS ARE TURNED (end of their Movement phase, 6″) lets a unit that was engaged at the start of the phase walk back onto the contested objective after the enemy fell back. Control is recalculated at the end of every phase, so arriving in their Movement phase also changes who controls the objective during their Shooting phase.
entries.when_to_use: A reactive trigger fires, and an objective you need at the end of their turn (Burden of Trust, Defend Stronghold) or at your next Command phase is within the move. The enemy can't easily push you off before their turn ends.
entries.unit_types: Reactive-move units (the ADJ-05 list), plus Boyz, Kommandos and Stormboyz (WHILE THEIR BACKS ARE TURNED).
entries.move_type: Normal move (09.05) granted reactively. Adjacent: opponent's Movement or Shooting phase.

entries.name: Make a reactive move to body-block the mover's route
entries.description: Use the reactive move to spread the unit across the triggering enemy's route to an objective or to a soft friendly unit. Its later moves and charges must then go around, or end up charging the blockers: enemy bases can't pass through your models, so leave gaps narrower than their base. The move must still end unengaged and in coherency (2″, and 9″ across the unit). Trukk Pilin' Out (a reactive rapid disembark when an enemy ends within 8″) could drop a blocking unit, but the engine hasn't implemented it.
entries.when_to_use: The enemy still has phases to move toward an objective or unit (their Charge phase, their next turn), your multi-model unit has a reactive move, and it has enough models to make a wall within the cap while ending more than 2″ from enemies.
entries.unit_types: Multi-model units with reactive moves (Gretchin, Gladius Infantry, Phobos squads); Trukk passengers (Pilin' Out).
entries.move_type: Normal move (09.05) granted reactively, or a reactive rapid disembark (18.04). Adjacent: opponent's Movement phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- 03.01: bases can't move through enemy models (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:388).
- 09.05: ends unengaged (:1390-1399). 03.03: coherency 2″ and 9″ (:514-537).
- 11.04: a charging unit can't end engaged with non-targets (:1662-1663).
- Pilin' Out: .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:96. FAQ: a unit that rapid-disembarked can't be Heroic Intervention's target (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:610-611).
- Gap physics: 11e normal moves only need to END unengaged, so a gap seals when it is narrower than the enemy base (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28388).

entries.name: Shape the charge move's end positions for what comes next
entries.description:
Within the charge-move rules, choose where around the targets your models land. The rules: each model ends closer to a charge target, models that can end within 1″ of a target or engaged with it must do so, and the unit can't end engaged with non-targets. Useful choices:
- The far side, to start a wrap (ADJ-03).
- Inside the objective's range, so the fight ends with OC there and Objective Consolidation is available.
- More than 3″ from other enemy units you don't want to be forced into on consolidation.
- Inside a terrain area, for cover.
- Spread out, to maximise pile-in reach.
FLY units may take to the skies on a charge (-2″, declared before the roll) to land over terrain or models.
entries.when_to_use: After a successful charge roll, in your own Charge phase or a Heroic Intervention, when there's spare distance or placement freedom.
entries.unit_types: Charging units.
entries.rules_basis:
- 11.04: each model ends closer to a charge target; models that can end within 1″, or engaged, must; the unit must be engaged with all targets and with no others (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1640-1665).
- 12.08: Engaging and Objective consolidation gates at 3″ (:1947-1958).
- 14.02 (:2401-2423).
- 21.03 take to the skies (:3358-3373); FAQ: declare it before rolling (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:681-682).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1640-1665, 1947-1958
missions#65 movement precursor: plan charge and fight end positions within 3″ of the target objective and more than 3″ from other enemies

entries.coverage_detail: _compute_charge_move (AIDecisionMaker.gd:19797-20324) covers every declared target (uncovered targets first, nearest first), then fixes missed close-in obligations and coherency. There is no term for objectives, wraps, cover or consolidation set-up. FLY units never take to the skies (SET_TAKE_TO_SKIES is never emitted).

entries.value_reason: It sets up wraps and objective consolidation on every successful charge.

entries.name: Overrun slingshot: extra pile-in into a second enemy when your target dies before you fight
entries.description: A unit can be eligible to fight but unengaged: its charge target died to Crushing Impact or to earlier fights, or everything it was engaged with died before it fought. It then makes an Overrun fight: one additional 3″ pile-in toward enemy units within 5″, which must end engaged, and then it fights. Sequence your fights so a shared target dies first, then slingshot into a second unit. If no enemy is within 5″ yet, pass (allowed when all your eligible units are more than 5″ from enemies) and wait for an enemy pile-in to come close. Extended pile-ins (6″, D3+3″) raise the distance but not the 5″ target-selection range.
entries.when_to_use:
When all of these apply:
- Two of your units share a target, or Crushing Impact may kill it.
- A second enemy is within 5″ plus reach.
- The unit is still eligible to fight: it charged this turn or was engaged at the start of the Fight step.
entries.unit_types: Melee units that charged, or were engaged, and lost their target.
entries.move_type: Pile-in move (12.03) as part of an Overrun fight (12.06). Adjacent: Fight phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- 12.04 eligibility (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1819-1825). 12.06 Overrun fight (:1866-1877).
- 12.03: an unengaged unit picks pile-in targets within 5″; moved models end closer to the closest target; the unit must end engaged (:1737-1766).
- FAQ: an overrun needs eligibility to fight (:4111-4119).
- Pass when more than 5″ away (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:505-507). Extended pile-in distance FAQs (errata_faq:493-498).
- Corrections: youtube#61's 'or toward an objective' is illegal, because the pile-in must end engaged. The web preview's 'up to 6″' is 3″ unless an ability extends it.
evidence: https://www.tabletopbattles.com/11-on-11th-recapping-the-new-warhammer-40k-rules-reveals-through-5-1/ (search snippet: an 'Overrun Fight' with an extra Pile In, described as a slingshot)

The AI always takes it and moves models at the nearest enemy model (AIDecisionMaker.gd:20381-20391, then _compute_pile_in_action :21317). _pile_in_targets_11e (:21669) is gated off (FIX_PILEIN_TARGETS_11E = 0.0, :1988). entries.value_reason: It turns overkill into a second combat, a trick the community highlights for 11e. It needs several units in the same fight.
entries.errata_note: Destroyed models awaiting a Fight On Death effect (e.g. A WORTHY DEATH, ORKS IS NEVER BEATEN, DUTY UNTO DEATH) stay on the battlefield, still engaged with your unit, until their unit has attacked or the phase ends. So the slingshot only opens once they are removed, and they can restrict the overrun pile-in. — FAQ 05.04 Inflict Damage, models awaiting Fight On Death (errata_faq:376-377)

entries.name: Use Objective Consolidation to slide out of sight or charge reach while staying on the objective
entries.description: 11e has no free 'step back' consolidation: with no enemy within 3″ and no objective within 3″, the unit can't consolidate at all. Objective mode, though, only requires each moved model to end within range of the selected objective. Models already in range can move up to 3″ to another point still in range, for example the far side of a terrain objective or behind its walls. With several objectives within 3″, you may pick the one whose range lies behind cover. Use this to dodge the enemy's next shooting or charges while keeping OC.
entries.when_to_use: The unit fought, is unengaged, has no enemy within 3″ and has an objective within 3″, and enemy shooters or chargers will act before you move again.
entries.unit_types: Any unit that fought.
entries.move_type: Consolidation move, Objective mode (12.08). Adjacent: Fight phase.
entries.rules_basis:

- 14.02: within range of a terrain objective means within its area (:2401-2406).
- 13.08 / 13.10 cover and obscuring (:2278-2311).
- Engine: the player's pick wins, and the default is the closest objective (ConsolidationMove.gd:110-126).
- Correction: youtube#59 and the F016 quote 'consolidate backwards' are legal only through Objective mode.

entries.name: Scout or Infiltrate into a Hidden or obscured forward post (move into cover, pre-battle)
entries.description: Put INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM Scouts or Infiltrators inside a forward terrain area with light or dense terrain, so they start the battle Hidden: visible only within 15″ detection range, and 3″ less when dense terrain conceals them (gone to ground). Alternatively, put them behind obscuring terrain. This gives safe forward pressure, early scoring for terrain-area cards and actions (Plunder, Death Trap, Vanguard Operation), and a launch point for turn-2 charges or actions. In the first turn a unit counts as not having shot in the previous turn.
entries.when_to_use: A forward terrain area is reachable within Scouts X″ (or anywhere, for Infiltrators) and is more than 8″ from enemies. This matters most when you go second (the turn order is known at this step) or face a shooting army.
entries.unit_types: INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM with Scouts or Infiltrators (Phobos squads, Scout Squads, Kommandos, Wolf Scouts, Fenrisian Wolves with a grant).
entries.move_type: Scout move (24.32) / Infiltrators set-up (24.20). Adjacent: pre-battle.

- 13.09.01: Hidden in the first turn (errata_faq:533). 13.11.01: gone to ground (errata_faq:539).

entries.name: Scout or Infiltrate within turn-1 reach of the enemy (charge staging or aura range: move toward an enemy to charge it, pre-battle)
entries.description: End the scout move (more than 8″ from all enemy units), or set up Infiltrators, where taking the first turn lets a normal move or Advance plus the 2D6 charge reach a priority target. Charge targets must be within 12″ and within the roll. Alternatively, put an aura or ability carrier, such as a battle-shock aura, where it covers enemy units on turn 1. The turn order is known at this step, so push hard only when going first. Going second, stage at the same distance behind obscuring terrain.
entries.when_to_use: Fast melee units or aura carriers have Scouts or Infiltrators, a priority enemy deployed within reach, and you take the first turn (or have a safe screened spot).
entries.unit_types: Fast melee units with Scouts (Wolf Scouts, Scout Bike Squad, Kommandos with Snikrot); aura or ability carriers with Infiltrators (Neurolictor-style battle-shock auras).
entries.move_type: Scout move (24.32) / Infiltrators set-up (24.20). Adjacent: pre-battle.

entries.name: Shoot, then move out of sight or out of charge reach (post-shooting move)
entries.description:
Several rules give a normal move right after the unit shoots in your Shooting phase:
- Purgation Run (Land Speeders, D6″).
- Mobile Hunter (Pallas Grav-attack, D6″).
- Shadow Masters (Phobos and Scout Squads: D6″, or stay Hidden instead).
- Execute and Redeploy (Phobos, 6″).
- Tactical Fluidity (Captain in Phobos Armour, D6″).
Use the move to shoot and scoot: break line of sight from the enemy's best guns, leave the charge reach of nearby melee, or step into a terrain area. These moves usually cost the unit its charge this turn.
entries.when_to_use: The unit has shot and is exposed to return fire or charges, and a line-of-sight blocker, terrain area or out-of-reach spot is within the move distance.
entries.unit_types: Land Speeders, Pallas Grav-attack, Phobos units, Scout Squads, Captain in Phobos Armour.
entries.move_type: Normal move (09.05) granted after shooting. Adjacent: your own Shooting phase.
entries.rules_basis:

- Reactive normal moves are 09.05 normal moves (ReactiveMove11e.gd:3-25; 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1390-1399).
- 13.08-13.10 (:2278-2311).

entries.name: Remove casualties (and coherency breakers) to improve the unit's position
entries.description:
You choose which models leave the board in two situations: when you allocate damage, you pick which model in the current allocation group dies (wounded models first), and at each end of turn you pick which models to remove to restore coherency. Pick models so the survivors:
- Stay coherent. A bad pick costs an extra model at the end of the turn, and models removed for coherency still count as destroyed for mission cards.
- Keep the models that are in an objective's range, a terrain area or cover.
- Lengthen the enemy's next charge, by removing the closest models.
- End unengaged, by removing every model within 2″ of the enemy, so the unit can move and shoot normally next turn.
entries.when_to_use: Every allocation of attacks or mortal wounds to your unit, and every end-of-turn coherency check.
entries.unit_types: Multi-model units.

entries.coverage_detail:
Allocation: CasualtyPreference.gd (:4-63) is the defender's automatic allocation for AI players. Coherency dominates its order, then it protects objective OC, removes front-rank models first by proximity, and adds charge-denial. It is applied wherever the engine auto-allocates (RulesEngine.gd:16663-16690; ShootingPhase.gd:3572-3580, 3772-3776).
End-of-turn coherency: AI owners fall through to the PhaseManager auto-pick of the most isolated offender (PhaseManager.gd:576-616). ScoringPhase.gd:51-58 offers the choice only to humans.
Missing: no cover or Hidden term, no explicit 'become unengaged' goal, and the coherency pick ignores objectives.
entries.engine_support:
Reuse CasualtyPreference.compute_preferred_targets / engine_auto_preference, MissionManager.model_in_objective_range (:529), TerrainManager.area_at (:847) and is_model_hidden (:1001).
New:
- A cover/Hidden keep term and a 'remove all engaged models' option.
- Route PhaseManager's coherency auto-pick through CasualtyPreference.
entries.value_reason: It happens constantly and is mostly handled. The remaining gains are cover/Hidden preservation and smarter coherency removals.

entries.name: Pull a doomed unit off the board into strategic reserves (escape)
entries.description:
Some rules place a unit into strategic reserves outside the Movement phase:
- At the end of the opponent's Fight phase: On Gilded Wings, TACTICAL WITHDRAWAL, Kunnin' Infiltrator (all models Hidden), Aerial Manoover, INSTINCTIVE HUNTERS, CO-ORDINATED STRIKE, GUNSHIP EXTRACTION, Echo of the Ravenspire, Take Wing, Parabolic Jetleap.
- At the end of your turn: From Golden Light.
Use them to save a badly hurt or about-to-be-charged unit from the next turn's shooting and charges, then bring it back by an ingress move later. Repositioned units are exempt from the end-of-round-3 destruction, but units still in reserve at the end of the battle are destroyed. Leaving also gives up the unit's OC immediately.
entries.when_to_use: The unit is unengaged (as required), at low wounds or below half strength, with enemies that can reach it. It isn't needed for OC at the next check, and there are rounds left to arrive again (battle round below 5).
entries.unit_types: Custodes Terminators (On Gilded Wings), Phobos and Scout Squads (TACTICAL WITHDRAWAL), AA Terminators (GUNSHIP EXTRACTION), Blood Claws, Thunderwolf Cavalry and Wulfen (CO-ORDINATED STRIKE), Beast Snagga (INSTINCTIVE HUNTERS), Boss Snikrot, Deffkoptas, Kayvaan Shrike, Venatari, Inceptors.
entries.move_type: Repositioned to strategic reserves (20.02), later an ingress move (20.04). Adjacent: end of the opponent's Fight phase, or end of your turn.
entries.rules_basis:
- 20.02 repositioned units (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3219-3245).
- 20.03: the round-3 wipe exempts repositioned units (:3276-3283). 20.04 ingress (:3255-3273).
- FAQ: in-battle reserves may exceed the 50% cap (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:662-665). Units in reserves at the end of the final turn are destroyed (errata_faq:673).
- Rule texts: On Gilded Wings (custodes/RULES.md:113; RULINGS.md:72), TACTICAL WITHDRAWAL (space-marines/RULES.md:624), GUNSHIP EXTRACTION (:659), CO-ORDINATED STRIKE (space-marines/SPACE_WOLVES.md:44), Kunnin' Infiltrator (orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:51).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3219-3245, 3276-3283
.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/custodes/RULES.md:113; space-marines/RULES.md:624, 659; space-marines/SPACE_WOLVES.md:44; orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:51

YouTube Warpbane Tactics veM7sLjtdIw @01:00 — “being careful about when we use our teleportation. Picking a unit up is incredibly useful, but under Take and Hold, that decision becomes more costly” [F027]
entries.coverage_detail:
Each ability has its own heuristic:
- From Golden Light escapes at 50% wounds or less with an enemy within 12″, and never leaves an objective (AIDecisionMaker.gd:22496-22536, :22575-22600).
- On Gilded Wings: below half strength, or off an objective with an enemy within 9″ (CustodesDetachments.gd:1165-1174).
- INSTINCTIVE HUNTERS / KEEP IT RUNNIN' score 2.5 with an enemy within 12″ when not holding an objective (OrkCodexFight.gd:990-1002).
- TACTICAL WITHDRAWAL, CO-ORDINATED STRIKE, GUNSHIP EXTRACTION and Echo of the Ravenspire fire only for idle units with no enemy within 12″, so never as an escape (SMCodexAMovement.gd:298-305; SWCodexMovement.gd:175-183; SMCodexBAction.gd:279-285; SMAbilitiesC.gd:1922-1927).
- Kunnin' Infiltrator, Aerial Manoover, Take Wing and Parabolic Jetleap score 0.0 (OrkAbilities11e.gd:2329-2330; CustodesAbilities.gd:1329-1330; SMAbilitiesA.gd:2284-2285).
None estimates the incoming damage, or where the unit could arrive again.
entries.engine_support:
Reuse _estimate_incoming_melee_damage (:12350), _evaluate_position_threat (:28794), _evaluate_end_turn_redeploy as the template, and _compute_reinforcement_positions (:8019) to check that an arrival spot exists.
New: one shared extraction scorer (expected loss if the unit stays vs the OC lost), called by all these codex hooks.
entries.value_reason: It saves points that would otherwise die, and several armies in the project have it. The heuristics are inconsistent and mostly blind to the threat.
entries.skeptic_note: Every cited extraction triggers at the end of the opponent's Fight phase: On Gilded Wings (custodes/RULES.md:113), TACTICAL WITHDRAWAL (SM RULES.md:624), GUNSHIP EXTRACTION (SM RULES.md:659), CO-ORDINATED STRIKE (SPACE_WOLVES.md:44), Kunnin' Infiltrator (orks Datasheets_abilities.csv:51). None triggers at 'end of your turn', so drop that timing. Kunnin' Infiltrator also needs every model hidden and unengaged. The 20.02/20.03 exemptions and the FAQs are correct. — custodes/RULES.md:113; space-marines/RULES.md:624, 659; space-marines/SPACE_WOLVES.md:44; orks/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:51; 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3219-3245, 3276-3283

entries.name: Declare formations and deploy so the army works whether it goes first or second
entries.description: Before the battle, choose what starts embarked, what goes into strategic reserves (AIRCRAFT must; at most 50% of points) and what starts on the table. Then deploy fragile and key units out of line of sight or in terrain, and threats where they can act on turn 1. The deployment must survive the opponent taking the first turn, because the first turn appears to be decided after deployment. Keep one Rapid Ingress answer in reserve unless the opponent's turn-1 threat range forces everything onto the table (F013).
entries.when_to_use: The Declare Battle Formations and deployment steps.
entries.unit_types: All units.
entries.move_type: Deployment set-up and formation declarations (18.01, 20.01, 23.01). Adjacent: pre-battle.
entries.rules_basis:
- 18.01: units can start embarked (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2975-2978).
- 20.01: strategic reserves are capped at 50% of points (:3205-3216).
- 23.01: AIRCRAFT must start in reserves (:3499-3501).
- 07.02: the mission says who takes the first turn (:1133-1138). The local missions summary doesn't state the method.
- So 'decided after deployment by a roll-off with no choice' rests on the engine (FirstTurnRollOffPhase.gd:6-21, labelled 10th edition), on F019, and on third-party 11e guides: the first-turn roll-off is its own step, and pre-battle rules alternate from the first-turn player, which matches 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:696-697.
evidence: YouTube MiniWarGaming dy1zEFAKLzk @03:00 — “This is the nice thing about the whoever rolls highest has to go first. I do not have to sweat about who gets first turn” [F019, rules_status unverified]
YouTube Exile Wargaming mbNWzDn6Pu4 @10:00 — “we did win the dice roll and had to go first, which I don't really like in recon” [F019]

YouTube Art of War 40k ym0SnzF2ydg @162:00 — “maybe they should have just started the game in reserve so they could be a little bit more of a reactive answer” [F013]; Happy Krumping pAk1YiuioNQ @09:00 — “If you're ever going to play against it, don't start things in reserves. You need everything on the table” [F013]

entries.coverage_detail:
What exists:
- _evaluate_reserves_declarations / _score_unit_for_reserves (AIDecisionMaker.gd:4737-5033) send deep-strike melee and short-range units to reserves, with penalties for long-range, cheap-screen and vehicle units.
- _evaluate_transport_embarkation (:4439-4705).
- _decide_deployment (:5055-5797) uses _classify_deployment_role and _score_terrain_for_role, where characters and fragile shooters prefer line-of-sight blockers and cover and melee prefers forward blockers, plus _apply_counter_deployment.
- Plans can hand-author placements (PLAN_FORMAT.md:110-112).
Missing: no explicit 'if we go second' test of enemy turn-1 threat ranges against our deployment, and no rule to keep one Rapid Ingress answer.
entries.engine_support:
Reuse _score_terrain_for_role (:5594), _apply_counter_deployment (:5421), _get_deployed_enemy_analysis (:5565) and _calculate_enemy_threat_data (:28695).
New:
- An 'opponent goes first' threat pass over candidate deployments.
- A reserve-keeping rule conditioned on the opponent's turn-1 threat range (F013's resolving variable).
entries.value_reason: Deployment decides early survival. The AI already has terrain-aware deployment, so the missing pieces are turn-order robustness and a reserve answer.

entries.name: Pile in to bring more models into the fight
entries.description: In the shared Pile In step at the start of every Fight phase, both players may pile in, active player first. Move models not in base contact up to 3″ so each ends closer to the closest pile-in target, and engaged with it if possible, keeping every existing engagement. More models end up fighting. Extensions such as LIGHTNING WRATH (D3+3″) raise the maximum distance but not target selection.
entries.when_to_use: Every Fight phase in which your unit is engaged or charged this turn.
entries.unit_types: Engaged units and units that charged.
entries.move_type: Pile-in move (12.03). Adjacent: Fight phase, yours or the opponent's.
entries.rules_basis:
- 12.02: both players pile in, active player first, optional (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1729-1735).
- 12.03: targets, the closer-and-engaged-if-possible rule, and keeping engagements (:1737-1766).
- FAQs on pile-in distance (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:493-498).
- LIGHTNING WRATH: .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/custodes/RULES.md:235.

entries.coverage_detail: _compute_pile_in_action / _compute_pile_in_movements (AIDecisionMaker.gd:21317-21710) move each model up to 3″ toward the closest enemy model, into base contact where possible. They keep base-contact models in place, keep coherency and move attached characters too. LIGHTNING WRATH is paid when models are 3-6″ from an enemy (CustodesCodexFight.gd:314-317). Caveat: FIX_PILEIN_TARGETS_11E is OFF (:1988), so the target is the closest enemy model rather than the 11e closest pile-in target unit.
entries.engine_support: Existing: PileInMove template (PileInMove.gd) and _pile_in_targets_11e (:21669). To finish 11e fidelity: turn on FIX_PILEIN_TARGETS_11E.
entries.value_reason: The core default, needed every Fight phase, and already covered.

entries.name: Decline or limit the pile-in to keep objective range or avoid a second engagement
entries.description:
Pile-in is optional per unit, and only the models you choose to move must end closer to the target. Don't pile in, or move only the models that add attacks, when moving would:
- pull models out of an objective's range or a terrain area's cover, or
- bring them into engagement with an extra enemy unit, which then becomes eligible to fight you.
entries.when_to_use: The unit is already doing enough damage, or the extra models' attacks are worth less than the objective control, cover or safety they would give up.
entries.unit_types: Engaged units and units that charged.
entries.move_type: Pile-in move (12.03), declined or partial. Adjacent: Fight phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- 12.02: 'all of their eligible units they choose to move', plus the sidebar 'you don't have to pile in or consolidate with a unit if you don't want to' (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1720-1735).
- 12.03: only moved models must end closer (:1757-1761).
- 12.04: engaged units are eligible to fight (:1821-1823).
- 14.02: control at the end of each phase (:2401-2423).

entries.name: Pull an idle or stranded unit into reserves to re-drop where it matters (reposition)
entries.description: The extraction rules in ADJ-26, and Grey Knights-style teleports, can also move a unit that is far from every objective and fight to a new arrival point next turn. They can also reset a unit for buffs that apply when it arrives (Meteoric Descent, Deff from Above, FURY OF THE EMPEROR). Weigh the OC and the turn of board presence it gives up: under Take and Hold this is costly (F027).
entries.when_to_use: The unit is unengaged, holds nothing, and is 15″ or more from useful objectives or fights. A legal arrival spot near a valuable objective or target will exist next turn, and it is before round 5.
entries.unit_types: The same units as ADJ-26.
entries.move_type: Repositioned to strategic reserves (20.02), then an ingress move (20.04). Adjacent.
entries.rules_basis:
- 20.02 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3219-3245); 20.03 exemption (:3276-3283).
- FAQ: in-battle reserves may exceed 50% (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:662-665). End-of-battle destruction (errata_faq:673).
- .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/RULINGS.md:72 (On Gilded Wings).

entries.coverage_detail:
What exists:
- From Golden Light's reposition branch fires when the unit is more than 15″ from every objective in rounds 1-3 (AIDecisionMaker.gd:22532-22534).
- TACTICAL WITHDRAWAL, CO-ORDINATED STRIKE and GUNSHIP EXTRACTION score 2.1, and Echo of the Ravenspire 1.5, when no enemy is within 12″, the unit is off objectives, and it is before round 5 (SMCodexAMovement.gd:298-305; SWCodexMovement.gd:175-183; SMCodexBAction.gd:279-285; SMAbilitiesC.gd:1922-1927).
- Kunnin' Infiltrator, Aerial Manoover, Da Jump and Take Wing score 0.0 (OrkAbilities11e.gd:2325-2330; CustodesAbilities.gd:1329-1330).
Nothing checks where the unit could arrive, or which arrival buffs it would gain.
entries.engine_support:
Reuse _compute_reinforcement_positions (:8019) and _score_reserves_deployment (:7949) to value next turn's arrival.
New: a value comparison of staying vs re-dropping in the shared extraction scorer (ADJ-26).
entries.value_reason: Occasionally strong (arrival buffs, stranded units), but it gives up OC and tempo. Partly covered.

entries.name: Redeploy after both armies are set up, to answer the opponent's deployment
entries.description:
Several enhancements let you redeploy up to three units after both armies have deployed, and put them into strategic reserves however many units are already there: Wreckas Kaptin's Hat (Ork Infantry), Hunter's Guile (Blood Claws, Thunderwolf Cavalry, Wulfen), Chariots of the Storm (any AA units), Castellan's Mark (Custodes), Cyber-familiar (AA Infantry), Strategium Command. A redeployed unit is deployed again with all the normal rules, including Infiltrators. Uses:
- Pull units out of the enemy's firing lanes.
- Move to the flank where the enemy is weak.
- Shift into reserves to answer their deep strikers.
entries.when_to_use: The opponent deployed into a lopsided position, a unit is exposed to an alpha strike, or reserves are needed as a reactive answer (F013).
entries.unit_types: Ork Infantry (Kaptin's Hat), Blood Claws, Thunderwolf Cavalry and Wulfen, AA units, Custodes units.
entries.move_type: Redeployment set-up (deployment rules re-applied). Adjacent: pre-battle.
entries.rules_basis:
- Enhancement texts: .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/RULES.md:208 (Kaptin's Hat); space-marines/SPACE_WOLVES.md:40 (Hunter's Guile), :51 (Chariots of the Storm); space-marines/RULES.md:731 (Cyber-familiar); space-marines/wahapedia/Datasheets_abilities.csv:862 (Strategium Command); custodes/RULES.md:150 (Castellan's Mark).
- Redeploying uses the normal deployment rules, including Infiltrators (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:248).

entries.name: Hold Scouts in reserve and set them up in your zone after seeing the enemy deployment
entries.description: The first Scouts option: a Scouts unit placed in strategic reserves can, in the Resolve Pre-battle Abilities step, be set up anywhere wholly within your deployment zone. That makes it the last deployment drop, after the opponent has finished deploying, and with the first-turn player known. Use it to counter-deploy against the side they loaded, to screen, or to put a unit exactly where the opponent's alpha strike can't reach.
entries.when_to_use: During Declare Battle Formations, the army has Scouts units it can afford to place in reserve (within the 50% cap), and counter-deployment matters: the opponent deploys second, or has asymmetric threats.
entries.unit_types: Units with Scouts X″.
entries.move_type: Set-up from strategic reserves under 24.31. Adjacent: pre-battle.
entries.rules_basis:
- 24.31: if the unit is in strategic reserves, set it up anywhere wholly within your deployment zone (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3859-3880).
- 20.01: the 50% cap applies at the formations step (:3205-3216).
- FAQ: pre-battle rules alternate (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:696-697).
- Engine: SCOUT_RESERVES_DEPLOY (ScoutPhase.gd:151, 172, 837); delta audit row 24.31/24.32 (windowed scenario iss067_scout_reserves_deploy_11e).

entries.coverage_detail: SCOUT_RESERVES_DEPLOY is never emitted: _decide_scout (AIDecisionMaker.gd:5831-5918) handles only CONFIRM, BEGIN and SKIP scout moves. _evaluate_reserves_declarations (:4737) never reserves Scouts units for this purpose.
entries.engine_support:
Reuse the deployment-role scoring (:5594) and counter-deployment (:5421).
New:
- A formations-step choice that reserves Scouts units for a late drop.
- A Scout-phase placement that emits SCOUT_RESERVES_DEPLOY.
entries.value_reason: A free information edge for armies with Scouts. It is niche, and the on-table scout move usually matters more.
entries.errata_note: The set-up comes after deployment with the first-turn player known, but pre-battle rules alternate starting with the first-turn player, so the opponent's scout moves and other pre-battle rules can still answer it. It is the last placement only if they have none left to resolve after it. — FAQ, Scouts: players alternate pre-battle rules starting with the first-turn player (errata_faq:696-697)

entries.name: Shoot, then step onto an objective (post-shooting move)
entries.description: Some moves after shooting must end in objective range: GRAB IT (Wreckas: a 6″ normal move, no charge afterwards) and PURGATION PUSH (Gravis Linebreaker: 5″). Execute and Redeploy (Phobos, 6″) and the free D6″ moves of ADJ-24 also allow it. The unit shoots from where it stands and still adds OC at the end-of-phase and end-of-turn checks. Weigh the lost charge.
entries.when_to_use: The unit has shot, an objective is within the move, and the OC is worth more than the charge it gives up.
entries.unit_types: Breaka Boyz, Flash Gitz, Tankbustas (GRAB IT); Gravis units (PURGATION PUSH); Phobos units.
entries.move_type: Normal move (09.05) granted after shooting. Adjacent: your own Shooting phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- GRAB IT: .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/orks/RULES.md:212. PURGATION PUSH: space-marines/RULES.md:681. Execute and Redeploy: :622.
- 09.05 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1390-1399). 14.02 (:2401-2423).

entries.coverage_detail:
What exists:
- GRAB IT is scored when an objective is reachable and no charge is forfeited (OrkCodexShootingReactive.gd:669-690).
- PURGATION PUSH scores 2.2 when the gap is 5″ or less (SMCodexBAction.gd:292-294).
- Execute and Redeploy is used when its 6″ reaches an objective (SMDetachmentsA.gd:1056-1058).
- The solver translates the unit to the nearest reachable objective (ReactiveMove11e.gd:318-358).
Missing: the free D6″ moves (Purgation Run, Mobile Hunter, Tactical Fluidity, Shadow Masters' move) are never used for this. They score 0.0, or the AI picks the other option.
entries.engine_support: Already reusable. To extend it, route the free post-shooting moves through the same objective check, and choose the objective by value (_estimate_objective_vp_value :22928).
entries.value_reason: Mostly covered. The remaining gain is extending it to the free post-shooting moves.

entries.name: Move again at the end of the Fight phase: leave a losing fight or reposition
entries.description:
Some end-of-Fight rules give a second move:
- WIND-SWIFT EVASION (Stormlance Mounted units that were eligible to fight): a normal move if unengaged, a fall-back move if engaged.
- Sweeping Advance (Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike, once per battle): the same split.
- Tactical Fluidity (Captain in Phobos Armour): if engaged at the end of the opponent's Fight phase, a 6″ fall-back.
- EMPEROR'S DOMAIN (Trusted Sentinels): Objective Consolidation even while engaged, to step out of combat onto an objective.
Use them to leave a fight you're losing, reach the next objective, or get out of next turn's charges and shooting.
entries.when_to_use: At the end of any Fight phase in which the unit was eligible to fight, when a better position exists within M (normal move) or the fight isn't worth staying in.
entries.unit_types: AA Mounted (Stormlance), Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike, Captain in Phobos Armour, Trusted Sentinels.

What exists:
- WIND-SWIFT EVASION scores 2.1 to leave a fight against a higher-points foe, or to reach an objective (SMCodexAMovement.gd:279-288; solver :754-811).
- Sweeping Advance is always taken via _compute_sweeping_advance_action (AIDecisionMaker.gd:20563-20569, :28996-29078). Each model moves straight away from its nearest enemy model if engaged, or straight to the nearest objective if not, with no collision, terrain or coherency planning.

entries.name: Re-embark outside your Movement phase for protection or redelivery
entries.description:
KEEP IT RUNNIN' (Blitz Brigade) and DUTY IS NEVER DONE (Gauntlet: an unengaged AA Infantry unit that was eligible to fight, wholly within 6″ of a TRANSPORT) let a unit embark at the end of the Fight phase. It is then safe from the next turn's shooting and ready to be driven to the next objective.
By RAW, 18.02 also lets a unit embark after any normal move: it has no phase restriction, and the moving player is the active player. So a reactive normal move ending within 3″ of a transport could embark. No local FAQ confirms this, and the engine's reactive-move path never offers embarking.
entries.when_to_use: The unit has no fight left, a transport with capacity is within 6″ (stratagems) or 3″ (embark), and the unit isn't holding an objective needed at the next check.
entries.unit_types: Ork Infantry near a Trukk or Battlewagon (KEEP IT RUNNIN'), AA Infantry near a TRANSPORT (DUTY IS NEVER DONE), reactive-move units near a transport.
entries.move_type: Embark (18.02) granted at the end of the Fight phase, or after a reactive normal move. Adjacent.
entries.rules_basis:
- 18.02 embarking: after a normal, advance or fall-back move; every model within 3″; not set up this turn; capacity available (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2981-2996).
- 01.03 (:137-158).
- FAQ: a rule letting a unit embark in a turn it disembarked overrides the core restriction (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:621-622).
- Rule texts: DUTY IS NEVER DONE (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/RULES.md:613), KEEP IT RUNNIN' (orks/RULES.md:201).
- The reactive-move embark is my reading of the RAW and is unconfirmed.

entries.coverage_detail:
What exists:
- DUTY IS NEVER DONE scores 2.0 when no enemy is within 9″ and the unit is off objectives (SMCodexAMovement.gd:292-294).
- KEEP IT RUNNIN' scores 2.5 with an enemy within 12″ and no objective held, else 0.5 (OrkCodexFight.gd:270-271, :990-1002).
What the AI never does:
- It never emits EMBARK_UNIT in play, because MovementPhase._check_embark_opportunity skips AI players (MovementPhase.gd:8306-8311).
- The reactive-move confirm path returns before the embark check (MovementPhase.gd:3803-3825).
entries.engine_support:
Reuse TransportManager.is_unit_within_embark_range / can_embark (TransportManager.gd:107, 173) and _estimate_incoming_melee_damage (:12350).
New:
- An embark-value scorer (damage avoided plus next-turn delivery value, minus OC lost).
- Engine support for embarking after reactive moves, if the RAW reading is accepted.
entries.value_reason: Situational, and limited to a few detachments.
entries.errata_note: KEEP IT RUNNIN' and DUTY IS NEVER DONE only change the timing and distance; the unit must still meet the other 18.02 conditions (capacity, datasheet eligibility, not set up on the battlefield this turn). So a unit that disembarked or arrived this turn can't re-embark with them, since neither rule says it may embark in a turn it disembarked. — Commentary 18.02.01 Able To Embark (errata_faq:626); FAQ 18.02 (errata_faq:621-622)

entries.name: Use rule-granted surge moves on your terms (and pre-position so the closest enemy is the right target)
entries.description:
Surge moves include IMPETUOSITY (Blood Claws, Thunderwolf Cavalry and Wulfen, after being shot), GOADED INTO ACTION (Beast Snagga, after losing a wound to shooting), Vengeful Surge (Custodes, D6+2″), Bestial Rage (D6+1″) and Glory of Ultramar. They have fixed rules:
- They go toward the CLOSEST enemy unit.
- They must end engaged with it if possible, otherwise as close as possible.
- They can't end engaged with any other unit.
- The unit must be unengaged, not battle-shocked, and not have moved this phase.
Because the target is forced, decide in your own Movement phase which enemy will be closest to your surge-capable units. Decline the surge when the closest enemy is a fight you lose, or when it drags you off an objective. AIRCRAFT are ignored as 'closest' unless the surging unit can FLY.
entries.when_to_use: A surge trigger fires and the closest enemy is a target you want. Plan ahead in your own Movement phase.
entries.unit_types: Blood Claws, Thunderwolf Cavalry and Wulfen (IMPETUOSITY), Beast Snagga (GOADED INTO ACTION), Custodes with Vengeful Surge, Fenrisian Wolves (Bestial Rage), Ultramarines (Glory of Ultramar). No shipped datasheet carries 'Surge X″'.
entries.move_type: Surge move (21.02). Adjacent: usually the opponent's Shooting phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- 21.01-21.02 surge move (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3297-3325).
- 23.02: AIRCRAFT are ignored when finding the closest unit unless the surging unit can FLY (:3512-3515).
- Rule texts: IMPETUOSITY (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/SPACE_WOLVES.md:45), GOADED INTO ACTION (orks/RULES.md:111), Bestial Rage (RULINGS.md:321).
- Engine: SurgeMove.gd:1-33; RulesEngine.get_surge_move_inches (RulesEngine.gd:9865). BEGIN_SURGE_MOVE is offered for 'Surge X' datasheets (MovementPhase.gd:8043), and none ship (docs/rules/11th_edition_doc_change_audit.md:188, 292).

What exists:

Missing: no check of who the closest enemy is or how dangerous its melee is, no objective cost, and no own-turn pre-positioning. BEGIN_SURGE_MOVE is never emitted (AIDecisionMaker.gd:6831).

entries.name: Place emergency-disembarked passengers where they survive
entries.description:
When your loaded transport is destroyed, each passenger makes a hazard roll. Each model is set up wholly within 6″ of the transport and as close as possible to it. Under the errata, a model that can't be placed unengaged may be set up engaged; models that still can't be placed are destroyed. The unit is then battle-shocked: its OC is '-', it can't be targeted by stratagems or start actions, and it can't charge this turn.
Within 'as close as possible' you still choose which side of the hull. Pick the side in cover or a terrain area, out of the killers' line of sight, toward next turn's objective, and away from enemy melee. The Deadly Demise roll (on a 6, mortal wounds to every unit within 6″) comes after the disembark and can't be avoided at that distance.
entries.when_to_use: Whenever a loaded transport is destroyed, in any phase.
entries.unit_types: Embarked units.
entries.move_type: Emergency disembark move (18.05), forced. Adjacent: any phase.
entries.rules_basis:
- 18.05 emergency disembark (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3061-3078), with the errata's engaged fallback (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:609).
- 01.07 battle-shock: OC '-', no stratagems, no actions (:197-221).
- 24.08 Deadly Demise: resolved after emergency disembarks, against units within 6″ (:3670-3699).
- FAQ: an emergency disembark counts as disembarking (errata_faq:630-631).
- Corrections: core-rules#109's 'keep clear of the Deadly Demise blast' is impossible at that distance. 'Choose objective range' gives no OC this turn, because the unit is battle-shocked.

Neither implements the errata's engaged fallback.

entries.name: Take the firing spot that sees the target but few enemy guns
entries.description: Among the endpoints from which the unit's firing models can see and reach its chosen target, pick the one that the fewest dangerous enemy shooters can see. For INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM, prefer one inside a terrain area so the unit keeps the benefit of cover while it fires. In 11e an obscuring terrain area blocks a sight line completely unless one of the two models is within it, and a unit is visible as soon as any one of its models is, so where the unit ends decides who can see it. Practical shapes: shoot from the corner of a ruin footprint that opens only the target's angle; stand just inside the edge of a terrain area (that area then stops blocking your own lines out, and infantry gain cover); keep every model that does not need the line behind the footprint. This is the exposure half of OFF-01/OFF-03: they ask 'can I hurt it from here', this asks 'who hurts me back from here'. A unit that fires loses Hidden this turn and next (13.09), so for shooters sight-line exposure is the main defence left.
entries.when_to_use: A ranged unit has a target worth shooting this turn and more than one endpoint gives it range and sight. Strongest for MONSTER/VEHICLE shooters (they are never Hidden), infantry that will forfeit Hidden by firing, and long-range units that can trade a few inches for a narrow angle. Little value against [INDIRECT FIRE] or [IGNORES COVER] return fire, or for units already outside most enemy ranges.
entries.unit_types: Ranged infantry squads, battle tanks, artillery, monsters, shooting characters; [HEAVY] units within 3″
entries.move_type: Normal (3″ or less for [HEAVY], see OFF-06); Advance with [ASSAULT]; a short shift instead of Remain Stationary
entries.rules_basis: 06.01 visibility per model pair: a unit is visible if any model is, and only the observing and observed units' own models are ignored (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1024-1035, 1100-1117). 04.02 the target must be visible and in range (:628-636). 13.10 Obscuring: areas that either model is within are excluded (:2305-2311). 13.11 Solid blocks enclosed gaps 3″ or less from ground level (:2313-2318). 13.08 cover is judged per attacking model (:2278-2290; FAQ 13.08, 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:522-525). 13.09 firing forfeits Hidden this turn and next (:2292-2303).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1024-1035 (06.01) and :2305-2311 (13.10 Obscuring)

[Warhammer Community #New40k terrain preview](https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-gb/articles/xlppkx5s/new40k-take-cover-with-updated-terrain-rules/) (WebSearch snippet only, page not fetched): units can stay out of line of sight just behind the footprint of a terrain area
