entries.coverage_detail: Firing-position logic only checks range. _get_enemies_in_weapon_range (AIDecisionMaker.gd:13760) compares unit centroids. _find_firing_position_toward_objective (:13848) and _clamp_move_for_weapon_range (:13780) never test line of sight. _find_cover_path (:14817) only tries ±15/30° using the polygon proxy _position_has_cover (:14858). Nothing counts how many enemy units could see the endpoint, and the F004 Overwatch term (:28660) is explicitly range-only.
entries.engine_support: TerrainManager.model_visible_11e and model_fully_visible_11e (TerrainManager.gd:1209/1215), unit_has_cover_11e(unit, attacker_model) (:1388) and hidden_model_visible_to (:1055) all take model dicts, so probe models at a hypothetical position work. That is the same pattern as _position_would_be_hidden (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28515). New query needed: _probe_exposure(unit, dests, enemy_units) returning {sees_target, enemy_shooters_seeing, weighted_incoming}, sampling 3-5 models per unit and memoised per candidate (the RulesEngine LoS memo is at RulesEngine.gd:6825).
entries.value_reason: In 11e line of sight is all-or-nothing per obscuring area, so the endpoint decides most of the return fire. It applies to every ranged unit every turn, and the current range-only scorer cannot see it.

entries.name: Tarpit a dangerous enemy melee unit with a durable cheap unit
entries.description: Charge, or set up a charge on, an enemy melee threat with a cheap but durable unit purely so the threat starts its next turn engaged. Durable means high T/Sv/InSv, many wounds, Feel No Pain, or simply a big expendable blob. An engaged unit cannot make a Normal or Advance move and cannot declare a charge, and if it falls back it cannot charge or shoot either. So for one turn the threat cannot reach the gunline, characters or objective holders it was heading for; it can only pile in and fight the tarpit. Keep other friendly units more than 3″ away so it has no consolidation target (SUR-25), and prefer a tarpit that survives both our Fight phase (the enemy fights back) and theirs. This is the melee mirror of DEN-03/OFF-08, which only lock shooters and action units.
entries.when_to_use: An enemy melee unit will reach a high-value friendly unit or key objective holder next turn (charge reach is M + 12″ by 11.04, more with advance-and-charge rules), nothing can kill it this turn, and a cheap durable unit is within charge reach. Skip it when the threat has a fall-back-and-charge rule, could consolidate into another unit within 3″, or would simply kill the tarpit and be free.
entries.unit_types: Cheap durable infantry blobs (Gretchin, Boyz, Poxwalkers, Cultists), Terminators, Custodian Guard, Plague Marines, walkers and vehicles with good saves
entries.move_type: Normal move to set up the charge; then Remain Stationary while engaged next turn
entries.rules_basis: 09.05 a Normal move is allowed only if unengaged (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1390-1399). 09.06 Advance likewise (:1401-1415). 09.07 a fall-back bars shooting and charging (:1417-1446). 11.02 an engaged unit, or one that fell back, cannot declare a charge (:1603-1625). 12.03 pile-in targets only enemies already engaged (:1737-1760). 12.08 Engaging Consolidation reaches only units within 3″ (:1942-1990).
evidence: [1d6chan 11th Edition Tactics/World Eaters](https://1d6chan.miraheze.org/wiki/Warhammer_40,000/11th_Edition_Tactics/World_Eaters) (WebSearch snippet only): 'the enemy can't fall back without making a Desperate Escape test, so the melee unit can tie an enemy up while other units do the damage'
YouTube F031, video sPWC5HujB_Y at 19:00: 'holding objectives, picking on isolated, tying units down, blocking movements ... it's no big deal if they're slain'
YouTube F024, video u8fm403MGtg at 08:00: 'Plague Legion it gets stuck in combat a lot and it's really hard to get out of combat'
entries.coverage_detail: _build_phase_plan lock_targets (AIDecisionMaker.gd:3789-3806) only collects dangerous SHOOTERS (_estimate_unit_ranged_strength >= PHASE_PLAN_RANGED_STRENGTH_DANGEROUS). charge_intent is scored as melee damage × target value plus PHASE_PLAN_LOCK_SHOOTER_BONUS (:2692). _melee_chase_gate (:2947) chases the nearest enemy. No term values 'this enemy melee unit cannot charge next turn' or the tarpit's durability. Worse, the next turn _decide_engaged_unit makes an off-objective engaged unit fall back (:12123), so even an accidental tarpit is released.
entries.engine_support: Charges, fights and fall-backs are fully implemented. Reuse _calculate_enemy_threat_data (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28695) to find enemy melee units whose reach covers our valuable units, and _estimate_incoming_melee_damage (:12350) plus _assess_engaged_unit_survival (:12373) to price whether the tarpit survives. New: a melee-lock entry in phase_plan.lock_targets, with a charge score based on durability rather than damage.
entries.value_reason: Directly protects the AI's gunline and scoring units from the commonest 11e killers (Orks, World Eaters, Custodes bricks), at the cost of chaff the AI already owns.

entries.name: Wall enemy MONSTER/VEHICLE lanes with your own MONSTER/VEHICLE models
entries.description: When the enemy movers you need to stop are MONSTER/VEHICLE models, build the move-block (DEN-04/DEN-05) from your own MONSTER/VEHICLE models and dense terrain, not infantry. On normal and advance moves, MONSTER/VEHICLE models can move straight through enemy models other than MONSTER/VEHICLE models. An infantry wall is therefore transparent to a tank's or monster's normal move; only other MONSTER/VEHICLE bodies and dense sections over 2″ high stop it. Infantry screens still work against their charges, because the 17.01 exemption covers only normal and advance moves. So split the job: hulls across movement lanes to objectives, infantry across charge lanes.
entries.when_to_use: The threats approaching an objective or backline lane are enemy MONSTER/VEHICLE units (Knights, tanks, gargantuan creatures, Battlewagons), and the AI has spare MONSTER/VEHICLE models nearby (empty transports, cheap walkers).
entries.unit_types: As blockers: empty transports, walkers, monsters, tanks. Used against enemy MONSTER/VEHICLE movers.
entries.rules_basis: 17.01 (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2870-2875). 03.01 bases cannot move through enemy models (:379-395). FAQ 17.01: other move types pass through friendly units only (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:596-599). 11.04 the charge move has no 17.01 exemption (:1640-1665). 13.06 dense sections over 2″ high (:2163-2183).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2870-2875 (17.01)
DEN-22/COO-28 in this catalogue already record the attacker's side of 17.01; this entry is the defender's side
entries.coverage_detail: Screen and blocker selection is cost-based. _is_screening_candidate (AIDecisionMaker.gd:14911) takes units of 100 pts or less with OC 2 or less. _calculate_corridor_blocking_positions (:15092) places them without checking whether the threatening enemies are MONSTER/VEHICLE models that ignore infantry on normal and advance moves.
entries.engine_support: The AI's planner already models pass-through for its own movers (_get_monster_vehicle_models :15897, _path_crosses_monster_vehicle :15957); reuse them on the enemy's projected path. New: a blocker-type filter in the corridor-block pass, keyed on the enemy movers' keywords.
entries.value_reason: Only matters against MONSTER/VEHICLE-heavy lists, but without it the AI's corridor blocks against those lists are wasted units.

entries.name: Play the last battle round by turn order
entries.description: In round 5, decide by who moves last. If you are the second player, no enemy turn follows: Command-phase rows score at the end of your turn and end-of-battle rows are checked right after it. So drop survival, screens, Hidden and Overwatch exposure entirely: Advance everything, charge onto objectives, contest with every body, and bring reserves in (strategic reserves are destroyed at the end of the final turn). If you are the first player, the opponent still has a full, all-in turn. Your end-of-your-turn rows still pay, but every end-of-battle row must survive that turn (Vital Link, Vanguard Operation, Inescapable Dominion and Punishment for the enemy home; Triangulation; Search and Scour's 'no enemies in your territory'). So must every end-of-opponent-turn row (Defend Stronghold, Display of Might's 5VP tier, Beacon). Hold with depth, screen the objectives they need, keep Rapid Ingress and Heroic Intervention answers.
entries.when_to_use: Battle round 5 (MAX_BATTLE_ROUNDS_AI). The switch is the first_turn_player flag. For the first player, also round 4, when planning which units must still be alive for the last turn.
entries.unit_types: Whole army; especially reserves, screens, objective holders and fast scorers
entries.move_type: Second player: Advance / Normal / Reserves arrival. First player: Remain Stationary / Normal / screening.
entries.rules_basis: 07.02 the same player takes the first turn in every battle round (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1135-1146). Mission timing key 'C = your Command phase (switches to end of turn in Round 5)' and the end-of-battle rows (docs/rules/11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:7, 13-38, 41-62). 20.01.02 strategic reserves are destroyed at the end of the final turn (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:671-673).
evidence: docs/rules/11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:7 (Round 5 timing switch)

[Tabletop Battles: 11e Force Disposition Review, Priority Assets](https://www.tabletopbattles.com/40k-11th-edition-force-disposition-review-priority-assets/) (WebSearch snippet only): Round 5 moves scoring to the end of each turn; 'the end game condition is a lot easier if you're going second, but either way you'll just need to put every body you've got left on objectives'
YouTube F011, video MG546BN181w at 47:00: 'You do not have to kill your opponent in 11th edition'
entries.coverage_detail: _get_round_strategy_modifiers (AIDecisionMaker.gd:17421) treats rounds 4 and 5 identically and raises survival (STRATEGY_LATE_SURVIVAL 1.4, :2724) even when the AI moves last. _enemy_next_turn_round (:9812) knows the turn order but feeds only one holder-loss check (:11073). End-of-battle rules are released only in the last round (FIX_EOG_TIMING, :22830-22834). _decide_engaged_unit holds objectives in rounds 4-5 regardless of turn order (:12050).
entries.engine_support: snapshot.meta.first_turn_player (read at AIDecisionMaker.gd:9813), MAX_BATTLE_ROUNDS_AI (:2213), and the primary vp_rules with their 'when' field. New: a moves_last_in_battle flag passed into _get_round_strategy_modifiers and into the objective and threat scoring.
entries.value_reason: The final turn carries the end-of-battle bonuses (5-10 VP), and today's late-game weights point the wrong way for the player who moves last.

entries.name: Anchor one model on the objective and stretch the rest toward the next job
entries.description: A unit only needs enough models inside the objective's terrain area to win the OC count. Coherency only requires each model to be within 2″ of one other model and within 9″ of every model. So leave one or two models in the area and move the rest to the edge of that envelope toward the next task: a charge (charge eligibility is measured from the closest model), a firing lane, the approach to a second objective, a screening line or a table-quarter boundary. This differs from OBJ-15, which toes in from the safe side to minimise exposure, and from OBJ-01, which holds. The per-model obligations of a later charge move are not verified here.
entries.when_to_use: A multi-model unit holds an objective with spare OC, a second job lies within about 9″ of the area, the stretched models are not needed for the OC count, and the anchor models are not left exposed alone.
entries.unit_types: Large infantry units (Boyz, Intercessors, Termagants) and units with high OC per model
entries.move_type: Normal (per model; only some models move)
entries.rules_basis: 03.01 you may move one or more of a unit's models (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:379-387). 03.03 coherency: 2″ to one model plus a 9″ envelope (:518-530). 14.02 a model within the terrain area is in range and adds its OC (:2401-2420). 11.02 'within 12″' is measured from the closest part of the base (01.04, :163-170).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:518-530 (03.03 coherency)
entries.coverage_detail: The executor either moves every model by one vector (rigid-block and formation passes, AIDecisionMaker.gd:14527-14600 and :15714) or holds the whole unit (REMAIN_STATIONARY at :7194 and :7350). There is no partial-unit stretch.
entries.engine_support: MovementPhase validates per-model destinations and coherency (MovementPhase.gd:1017-1072), so a subset move is legal. _ai_model_in_objective_range (AIDecisionMaker.gd:13145) tests each model. New: a stretch-formation generator that pins k models in the area and translates the rest within the 9″ envelope.
entries.value_reason: Gives big units extra reach and charge tempo, but the 9″ envelope keeps the gain small.
entries.errata_note: Coherency also requires the unit to be a single contiguous group. Each stretched model must link back to the anchor models through a chain of models each within 2in horizontally and 5in vertically of the next, as well as being within 9in of every model, so a detached sub-group is illegal even if each of its models has a 2in partner. — FAQ 03.03 Coherency

entries.name: Straddle two objectives with one unit
entries.description: Where two objectives lie within one unit's 9″ coherency envelope (two terrain areas, or a marker and an area), put models in both. A model's OC counts toward every objective it is within range of, and the unit counts as controlling each one. One cheap unit can then hold or contest two objectives for threshold rows (OBJ-19), or deny two at once.
entries.when_to_use: The layout puts two objective areas or markers less than about 9″ apart edge to edge (layout dependent, e.g. 6-objective maps), and the unit has enough OC per model to matter on both.
entries.unit_types: Multi-model infantry with OC 1-2 per model
entries.rules_basis: FAQ 14.02: 'can the same model's OC count towards more than one objective that model is within range of? Yes' (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:550-553). 03.03 9″ envelope (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:518-530). 14.01.01 objective markers have 3″ range (errata md:546-548).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:550-553 (FAQ 14.02)
MissionManager computes each objective's level of control independently over all units (MissionManager.gd:863-905), so a model in two ranges already counts twice in-engine
entries.coverage_detail: _assign_units_to_objectives (AIDecisionMaker.gd:9834) scores (unit, objective) pairs and gives each unit exactly one objective; there is no candidate for a pair of objectives.
entries.engine_support: MissionManager.model_in_objective_range (MissionManager.gd:529). New: a candidate type for objective pairs that fit inside one unit's envelope.
entries.value_reason: Layout dependent: a big payoff when two objectives are close, none otherwise.
entries.errata_note: The models in the two objectives must form one contiguous chain (each within 2in of the next) as well as staying inside the 9in envelope; two separate clumps are not legal. The gap a unit can straddle therefore depends on its model count and base size (e.g. two 32mm-based models can bridge only about 4.5in), not just on the 9in envelope. — FAQ 03.03 Coherency

entries.name: Line up the turn's easiest kill when a card pays for kill count
entries.description: Several cards pay for how many units die, not which ones. Unstoppable Force, Meatgrinder and Destroyer's Wrath pay 3VP at end of turn for destroying 1+ unit, and Meatgrinder and Destroyer's Wrath also pay 4VP for killing more than the opponent did last turn. Delaying Action pays 2VP per unit, Reconnaissance Sweep 1VP per unit, Vanguard Operation 2VP for any kill, and No Prisoners 2VP per unit up to 10. Before other moves are committed, move one or two units to where they can almost certainly finish the weakest reachable enemy unit this turn: a wounded unit, a lone character, isolated chaff, a damaged vehicle. If the 'kill more' row is live, add units toward the next-easiest kills too. Value targets by kill probability, not points.
entries.when_to_use: Our primary or secondary has a destroy-1+, per-kill or kill-more rule active this turn, and the AI has no kill banked yet this turn (or is below the opponent's last-turn count).
entries.unit_types: Any shooter or charger; cheap units for finishing blows
entries.rules_basis: Primary rows in docs/rules/11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:20-21, 24-25, 32, 36 (destroy 1+, kill more than the opponent's last turn, per-unit kills) and the No Prisoners secondary (:50); these score at the End of Turn step (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1202-1212). The missions doc itself labels card values approximate.
evidence: docs/rules/11th_edition_missions_gdm2026.md:20-25, 32, 36, 50

[Tabletop Battles: 11e Force Disposition Review, Purge the Foe](https://www.tabletopbattles.com/40k-11th-edition-force-disposition-review-purge-the-foe/) (WebSearch snippet only): 'going second tends to be better here as it allows you to react to your opponent when it comes to scoring kill more'
YouTube F010, video D5XVd0FRgK8 at 02:00: 'unit left alive on one wood can still hold an objective, block our movement'
entries.coverage_detail: _build_primary_awareness sets kill_pressure for destroyed_min, per-unit and killed_more rules (AIDecisionMaker.gd:22866-22870), but _calculate_target_value only multiplies target value by 1.15 (:17879-17880). No Prisoners gets a generic proximity bonus (:10468-10481). Nothing knows whether a kill is already banked this turn, and movement never prefers the most killable target.
entries.engine_support: MissionManager already tracks kills: _kills_this_turn_11e(player) (MissionManager.gd:3270) and the rule evaluation at MissionManager.gd:2706-2712. New query: expose kills_this_turn and opponent_kills_last_turn to the AI, and rank reachable targets by kill probability using the existing expected-damage and kill-threshold helpers (_calculate_marginal_value, after AIDecisionMaker.gd:17895).
entries.value_reason: Purge the Foe primaries pay 3-4 VP every turn for one cheap kill, while the AI currently spends its moves on high-value targets it may not finish.

entries.name: Choose where the Advance goes after seeing the roll
entries.description: In 11e the advance roll is made before any model moves, and once rolled the unit has made an Advance: no charge, no actions, only [ASSAULT] shooting, whatever distance it then uses. So plan the Advance as a contingent move. A high roll reaches the objective, action site, quarter or staging spot. A low roll should switch to the best fallback within the actual distance: the nearest Hidden, cover or out-of-sight spot, a screening line, or a position outside enemy charge reach. It should not stop short in the open on the original heading. Also decide before rolling whether a bad result is worth a Command Re-roll, and declare take to the skies before the roll (FAQ 21.03).
entries.when_to_use: Any Advance whose payoff depends on distance (reaching an objective, action area, quarter or charge reach) and where a short roll would leave the unit exposed.
entries.unit_types: Any unit that Advances: fast infantry, Orks with advance re-rolls, transports
entries.rules_basis: 09.06 'BEFORE MOVING: Make an advance roll by rolling one D6' and the after-moving restrictions (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1401-1415). 15.02 Command Re-roll on an advance roll (:2651-2670). FAQ 21.03 declare take to the skies before rolling (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:679-682).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1401-1415 (09.06)
AIPlayer.gd:1674-1693 already pauses after the roll and recomputes destinations, so the hook exists
entries.coverage_detail: AIPlayer.recompute_destinations_for_cap (AIPlayer.gd:1697-1716) re-plans for the rolled distance but keeps the pre-roll heading (_advance_heading_target), so a roll of 1-2 stops short on the same line. The Advance was planned at M+2 (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7205, :7244; AIPlayer.gd:1678), while assignment scoring uses ADVANCE_EXPECTED_EXTRA_INCHES = 3.5 (AIDecisionMaker.gd:2256).
entries.engine_support: MovementPhase pauses after the roll for the Command Re-roll decision. AIPlayer already hooks in at AIPlayer.gd:1670-1693. _advance_reach_chance (AIDecisionMaker.gd:13247) and _prob_sum_d6_at_least (:12788) price roll outcomes. New: re-run the unit's own move choice with the rolled distance (single-unit focus, as _suggest_focus_unit_id does at :7158-7166), plus a fallback-spot generator (cover, Hidden, out of reach) for when the main target is out of reach.
entries.value_reason: Every Advance currently stakes a whole turn of exposure on one D6; choosing after the roll removes the worst outcomes cheaply.

entries.name: Keep your own shooters' sight lines clear of your other units
entries.description: In 11e only the models of the observing unit and of the observed unit are ignored for line of sight, so every other model blocks sight, including your own tanks, monsters and blobs. When moving a unit that will not shoot through the gap (a screen, transport, melee unit or objective holder), do not end it across the lanes your gunline needs this Shooting phase or next turn, and move it out of them if it is already there. Order the moves so the shooters' lanes are known first (COO-22).
entries.when_to_use: A large-footprint friendly unit (vehicle, monster, big blob) is about to end between a friendly shooting unit and that shooter's likely targets.
entries.unit_types: Potential blockers: vehicles, monsters, transports, large infantry blobs
entries.rules_basis: 06.01 'other models in the observing model's unit and in the observed model's unit are ignored' (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1024-1031), so models of any other unit block line of sight. Models never grant cover except through SMOKESCREEN 15.10 (:2714-2733).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1024-1031 (06.01)
SUR-31/COO-19 in this catalogue rely on the same rule from the sheltered unit's side
entries.coverage_detail: No AI term treats friendly models as sight-line blockers. COO-22's lane clearing deals only with movement corridors (move-order sort at AIDecisionMaker.gd:7124-7148).
entries.engine_support: None today. Engine line of sight is terrain-only (EnhancedLineOfSight.check_enhanced_visibility, EnhancedLineOfSight.gd:27; TerrainManager.gd:1221-1224 says 'only terrain blocks these lines'). Model occlusion has to be added to the LoS module before this intent has any in-engine payoff.
entries.value_reason: Correct 11e play, but it has zero in-engine effect until line of sight models occlusion.

entries.name: Bail out of a transport before it is destroyed
entries.description: If the loaded transport will probably die before your next Movement phase, disembark now while you still choose the mode and the spot. An emergency disembark is much worse. Every model makes a hazard roll (a 1-2 inflicts a mortal wound). Models are set up as close as possible to the wreck: engaged if no unengaged spot exists, destroyed if neither fits. The unit is battle-shocked and cannot charge. And it happens before the hull's Deadly Demise roll, so the survivors sit inside its 6″ radius. A Tactical Disembark before the transport moves keeps the unit's own Normal move and charge; afterwards the empty hull can still act (block, screen, ram).
entries.when_to_use: The transport has few wounds left, or faces enough anti-tank to kill it next turn (expected damage at least its remaining wounds), and the cargo has a useful job within 3″ plus its M. Strongest when the transport has Deadly Demise or is engaged.
entries.unit_types: Transports and their passengers (Rhinos, Trukks, Raiders, Wave Serpents, Impulsors)
entries.move_type: Disembark (Tactical, then a Normal move) / Disembark (Rapid, after the transport moves)
entries.rules_basis: 18.04 disembark eligibility and modes (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3013-3058). 18.05 emergency disembark, with its errata (:3061-3086; 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:609-611). 06.03 hazard rolls (:1067-1074). 24.08 Deadly Demise resolves after emergency disembarks (:3670-3700).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3061-3086 (18.05) and errata md:609-611
AIDecisionMaker.gd:8572-8587: the existing disembark trigger fires on any S7+ gun within 24″, whatever the hull's state
entries.coverage_detail: _score_disembark_benefit Factor 5 (AIDecisionMaker.gd:8572-8587) adds DISEMBARK_TRANSPORT_THREATENED whenever any enemy ranged weapon of S7+ is within 24″, regardless of the hull's remaining wounds or the expected incoming damage. Nothing prices the cost of an emergency disembark (hazard rolls, battle-shock, as-close-as-possible placement, the Deadly Demise radius).
entries.engine_support: AIAbilityAnalyzerData.is_unit_doomed (AIAbilityAnalyzer.gd:595, used at AIDecisionMaker.gd:7472), _estimate_unit_remaining_wounds (:12362), and AIAbilityAnalyzerData.has_deadly_demise / get_deadly_demise_value (AIAbilityAnalyzer.gd:546/559). New: the expected ranged damage on the hull in the next enemy turn (reuse the shooting-phase damage estimator against the transport), compared with its remaining wounds.
entries.value_reason: Saves whole squads, and their OC, from hazard rolls, battle-shock and Deadly Demise; the current trigger fires on any S7 gun within 24″.

entries.name: Stay more than 6″ from enemy Deadly Demise models you are about to destroy
entries.description: Before shooting or charging a wounded enemy DEADLY DEMISE model, end the moves of your fragile units more than 6″ from it: lone or attached characters, small elite squads, objective holders. Let durable or expendable units do the close work. When the model is destroyed, a 6 on one D6 inflicts X mortal wounds on every unit within 6″ of it, friend or foe, and a unit that kills it in melee is always inside the radius. The catalogue has the mirror (SUR-26, our own Deadly Demise models); the enemy side is missing.
entries.when_to_use: A wounded enemy model with Deadly Demise X (X = D3, D6 or more: tanks, Knights, big monsters) is likely to die this turn or in the enemy turn, and a fragile friendly unit could end within 6″ of it. Ignore it for Deadly Demise 1 or when only expendable units are near.
entries.unit_types: Characters, low-wound elite units and objective holders near enemy vehicles or monsters; melee units deciding whether to charge a doomed enemy vehicle
entries.move_type: Normal / Advance end position, plus the choice of which unit charges the vehicle
entries.rules_basis: 24.08 Deadly Demise: each time a model is destroyed, after any embarked units' emergency disembark, roll one D6; on a 6, each unit within 6″ suffers X mortal wounds (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3670-3700).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3670-3700 (24.08)
SUR-26 in this catalogue covers only the friendly-model side of the same rule
entries.coverage_detail: Deadly Demise logic exists only for the AI's own doomed vehicles: the movement ram at AIDecisionMaker.gd:7466-7490 and the charge bonuses at :18629-18636 and :19397-19405. No movement or charge-target term prices ending within 6″ of an enemy Deadly Demise model the AI is about to kill.
entries.engine_support: RulesEngine.resolve_deadly_demise (RulesEngine.gd:16929) resolves it. AIAbilityAnalyzerData.has_deadly_demise, get_deadly_demise_value and is_unit_doomed (AIAbilityAnalyzer.gd:546, 559, 595) work on enemy unit dicts too. New: a destination penalty of about (1/6) × E[X] × P(model dies this turn) for each friendly unit ending within 6″, weighted up for characters.
entries.value_reason: A 1-in-6 event, but it can kill a character or strip an objective's OC, and it is cheap to price once the Deadly Demise values are read.

entries.name: Keep an escape lane open behind units that may be charged
entries.description: End units that are likely to be charged (shooters, transports, characters, vehicles) with clear ground behind them. Do not back them against the board edge, against a dense ruin wall that a non-INFANTRY model cannot cross, or against your own blob, where a fall-back cannot end. A fall-back must end unengaged, and an Ordered Retreat cannot pass through enemy models. So a unit boxed in by terrain and the charge cannot fall back at all, or only by Desperate Escape: a hazard roll per model plus a battle-shock roll.
entries.when_to_use: A unit that does not want to stay in combat ends inside an enemy unit's charge reach, and the ground behind it is restricted by the board edge, dense terrain (for MONSTER/VEHICLE models) or tightly packed friendly units.
entries.unit_types: Vehicles and monsters (cannot cross dense terrain), gunline infantry, characters
entries.move_type: Normal / Remain Stationary (choice of end position)
entries.rules_basis: 09.07 a fall-back must end unengaged; Desperate Escape costs hazard rolls plus a battle-shock roll (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1417-1446). 03.01 bases cannot move through enemy models or cross the battlefield edge (:379-395). 13.06 movement limits in dense terrain (:2163-2183).
evidence: 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1417-1446 (09.07)
YouTube F017, video aQsog-fkQJ8 at 98:00: 'no, we'll fall back and we'll take our hazardous roles. Ones and twos, they die'
entries.coverage_detail: Fall-back space is searched only after the unit is engaged (_compute_fall_back_destinations AIDecisionMaker.gd:12185, trying 12 directions from _build_fall_back_directions :12501). No destination term in _assign_units_to_objectives or _find_safer_position (:28892) prices escape lanes.
entries.engine_support: _try_fall_back_positions (AIDecisionMaker.gd:12517) and _move_path_blocked (:15244) can be reused as a probe. New: a count of escape lanes from point P (fall-back directions clear of the edge, terrain and friendly units), used as a small destination term for units inside enemy charge reach.
entries.value_reason: Prevents rare but expensive traps, such as a tank stuck in combat for the rest of the game; a small term.

rejected.name: Bait Fire Overwatch with a cheap model or unit moved first (a sub-intent mentioned inside youtube#3, web#5 and first-principles#6)
rejected.reason: This is a 10e-only trick from the Balance Dataslate's per-move Overwatch timing. In 11e Fire Overwatch is used once, at the end of the opponent's Movement phase, after every move has been made (15.08, docs/rules/40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2735-2747; the engine offers no per-move Overwatch at 11e, 40k/phases/MovementPhase.gd:1745-1749), so a bait move draws nothing. All three raw candidates say not to generate it. The surviving intent is SUR-04.

rejected.name: Sacrificial Overwatch soak: move a cheap unit first to draw out the enemy's Overwatch
rejected.reason: Illegal premise in 11e. FIRE OVERWATCH (15.08, 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2735-2768) is used only at the END of the moving player's Movement phase, by one unengaged unit that snap-shoots one visible enemy unit within 24″ of the overwatching player's choosing; there is no per-move trigger to bait, so the overwatcher waits and picks the best target after every move (once per phase, 15.01 :2495-2500; engine note StratagemManager.gd:5077-5080: “exactly one timing at 11e (no per-move / set-up / charge-declaration offer; those were 10e Balance Dataslate wording)”). The corpus agrees: “You can't play around it any more — big squads just get overwatched” (ai_learnings.json disagreements[2], Deploy on the Line 40K FT5JoL5Myis @05:00). The legitimate remainder, ending out of sight or beyond 24″ of enemy Overwatch units, belongs to survival (B37 Overwatch exposure). Listed because the bucket definition names it; first-principles#71 itself flagged it as impossible in 11e (its reactive-move bait half is DEN-23).

rejected.name: Bait out the enemy's Fire Overwatch with a cheap unit before the real threat moves
rejected.reason: Illegal premise in 11e. Fire Overwatch is used at the END of the opponent's Movement phase against any visible, unengaged enemy within 24″ (15.08/15.09, 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2735-2768), and each stratagem can be used only once per phase (15.01, :2495-2499). The opponent chooses after seeing every move, so the order of your moves cannot draw it out. The corpus agrees: YouTube qahZnQPN8a8 @27:00 (Vanguard Tactics, F004): 'Overwatch is so powerful in this game now because you can't ... put one model out ... you can't bait them out anymore'. web#10 itself flagged this. The legal variant, baiting a once-per-phase reactive MOVE, is kept as COO-35.

rejected.name: Combat-disembark to add OC to an objective
rejected.reason: Illegal in effect. A combat disembark leaves the unit battle-shocked (18.04 AFTER MOVING, 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3055-3056), and a battle-shocked unit's OC is '-' and it cannot start actions (:213-221). It cannot add OC. The rest of the candidate (escape, or join the fight) is kept in TRN-14.

rejected.name: Embark the Beacon unit and keep scoring it
rejected.reason: The Beacon card lets a unit be designated while embarked, but it scores only 'if the beacon unit is on the battlefield' (40k/data/40kdc/missionCards.json:2850). Embarked units are not on the battlefield (40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:36; engine MissionManager.gd:1772-1780). The protect-by-embarking intent is kept in TRN-05, with the Beacon exclusion.

rejected.name: Consolidate straight back out of line of sight (free step-back consolidation)
rejected.reason: Illegal as a free move in 11e. 12.08's modes are mandatory and assessed in order (Ongoing, Engaging, Objective). With no enemy and no objective within 3″, the unit has no consolidation mode and can't move (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1942-1958; ConsolidationMove.gd:1-20, :126). The legal version, moving within the selected objective's range, is kept as ADJ-21.

rejected.name: Overrun slingshot toward an objective
rejected.reason: Illegal. The overrun fight's extra move is a pile-in. Its moved models must end closer to the closest pile-in target, and the unit must end engaged (12.03 AFTER MOVING, 40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:1737-1766; 12.06 :1866-1877). Only the slingshot into a second enemy unit (ADJ-20) is legal.

rejected.name: Set emergency-disembarked passengers outside the transport's Deadly Demise radius
rejected.reason: Not possible. 18.05 and its errata require each model to be wholly within 6″ of the destroyed transport and as close as possible to it (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3061-3078; 40k_11th_edition_errata_faq_commentary.md:609). 24.08 resolves Deadly Demise after the emergency disembark, against every unit within 6″ of that model (:3670-3699). The placement intent itself is ADJ-37.

rejected.name: Make a reactive move with a stratagem, then Fire Overwatch with the same unit
rejected.reason: Illegal within one phase. Under 15.01, unless otherwise stated, a player can't target the same unit with more than one stratagem in the same phase (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:2500-2501). RESPONSIVE TACTICS-style moves and Fire Overwatch are both used in the opponent's Movement phase, and its end is part of that phase (09.03, :1368-1370). Reactive moves granted by datasheet abilities are not stratagems, so that variant is kept in ADJ-11.

rejected.name: Shoot the unit that just fell back (RAPID REACTIONS)
rejected.reason: Not a movement decision. It is a reactive shooting stratagem (.llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/custodes/RULES.md:211) and belongs to shooting target selection. The AI scores it 2.2 (CustodesCodexMovement.gd:259-260). The movement parts of factions#50 are kept in ADJ-17 (WHILE THEIR BACKS ARE TURNED) and ADJ-10 (NO ESCAPE).

rejected.name: Snare the objective the enemy must step onto (MORTIS SNARES) [DEN-29]
rejected.reason: Commentary 01.02.02 says a rule that specifies when it is triggered but not how long it is active is only active for that period. MORTIS SNARES (WHEN: end of your Movement phase) prints no duration, as RULINGS.md:402 itself notes and unlike stratagems that state one (e.g. DEATH BEGETS VENGEANCE: 'hated until the end of the battle'). The snare therefore lapses at the end of your Movement phase and cannot catch next turn's contester; at most it catches an opponent's Rapid Ingress arrival in that same end step, which must still be more than 8″ from your units. The engine's 'lasts until triggered' ruling contradicts the commentary; it holds only if 'That objective is no longer snared' is deliberately read as a duration. — Commentary 01.02.02 Persisting Rules Effects (errata doc :28); MORTIS SNARES text at .llm/codex_11e_wahapedia/space-marines/wahapedia/Stratagems.csv:92

merged.name: Pick the Hidden spot behind a dense wall and beyond each shooter's detection range
merged.reason: SUR-11 refines SUR-01: it picks which spot inside the Hidden area to use (Gone to Ground −3″, outside the shooters' detection range). That is a scoring detail of the same 'end Hidden' generator, not a separate purpose.

merged.name: Stage the charge out of sight to avoid Overwatch
merged.reason: Both end the Movement phase where no eligible enemy can Fire Overwatch on the unit. OFF-05 only adds the constraint 'stay inside charge reach of the target'.

merged.name: Kite: shoot from outside the enemy's charge reach
merged.reason: Same purpose: end beyond enemy charge reach. OFF-20 only adds the constraint 'keep a target in weapon range'.

merged.name: Stage for next turn's strike: end out of the enemy's reach and sight but inside your own next-turn reach
merged.reason: Both stage forward, out of enemy sight and reach, but inside our own reach for next turn.

merged.name: Keep Lone Operative spacing while staying in your own range
merged.reason: Both keep an unattached Lone Operative beyond the 12″/X″ range it can be seen from. COO-32's 'stay in own weapon range' is a constraint on the same move.

merged.name: Escape a wrap by falling back through enemy models
merged.reason: Same fall-back choice: when wrapped, use Desperate Escape or take to the skies to pass through enemy models.

merged.name: Stay engaged as a shield from enemy shooting (decline to fall back)
merged.reason: All are one decision: Remain Stationary while engaged. They differ only in the value term: shield from shooting, falling back forfeits the turn, keep the enemy locked, M/V keeps close-quarters shooting. COO-18 already lists these. The merged entry should also state 'stay to finish a fight you are winning'. OBJ-34 stays separate because its trigger is objective OC and it is already implemented.

merged.name: Stay locked in combat when falling back would forfeit the turn
merged.reason: All are one decision: Remain Stationary while engaged. They differ only in the value term: shield from shooting, falling back forfeits the turn, keep the enemy locked, M/V keeps close-quarters shooting. COO-18 already lists these. The merged entry should also state 'stay to finish a fight you are winning'. OBJ-34 stays separate because its trigger is objective OC and it is already implemented.

merged.name: Stay engaged to keep an enemy unit locked (decline to fall back)
merged.reason: All are one decision: Remain Stationary while engaged. They differ only in the value term: shield from shooting, falling back forfeits the turn, keep the enemy locked, M/V keeps close-quarters shooting. COO-18 already lists these. The merged entry should also state 'stay to finish a fight you are winning'. OBJ-34 stays separate because its trigger is objective OC and it is already implemented.

merged.name: Stay engaged with a MONSTER/VEHICLE and keep shooting
merged.reason: All are one decision: Remain Stationary while engaged. implementation_order.mechanism: Override in _decide_engaged_unit (AIDecisionMaker.gd:11958), before the default 'Not on objective or better to fall back — fall back' branch (:12123). Compare staying with leaving. Stay value: melee damage the unit deals in our own Fight phase (finish the enemy); lock value if the engaged enemy is in phase_plan.lock_targets or is an action/objective unit; shield value for non-MONSTER/VEHICLE units that would otherwise sit in many enemy weapon ranges; close-quarters shooting value for MONSTER/VEHICLE units (10.06). Leave value: what the unit can still do after falling back (no shooting, charge or actions unless it has a Fall Back and X rule), minus Desperate Escape hazards if it is battle-shocked. Feed in the already computed survival.recommendation (:12410-12416), which nothing reads today.
implementation_order.why: Off an objective the AI always falls back when it can. It abandons fights it is winning and releases its own lock charges (F015/F017), and every input the fix needs already exists in this function.

implementation_order.mechanism: New override in _select_movement_action next to the T7-26 Heavy check (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7419). If a ranged weapon's special_rules contains 'indirect fire' (the same string parse _get_unit_heavy_weapon_data uses for 'heavy', :13571) and its best target is not visible, return REMAIN_STATIONARY unless an objective is reachable this move. Give units that can see that target a spotter bonus in _assign_units_to_objectives, and move them before the battery in _build_move_order (:7666). Shooting side: stamp shooting_type 'indirect' (RulesEngine.gd:6560 notes that no AI path does).
implementation_order.why: RulesEngine already applies the 10.07 rule: a stationary unit with a friendly spotter fails only on 1-3 instead of 1-5 (RulesEngine.gd:6594-6604). The AI has zero references to indirect fire, so one override roughly triples the battery's hits on targets it cannot see.

implementation_order.mechanism: In the T7-26 branch (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7419-7430; _should_hold_for_heavy_bonus :13618), generate a 3″-or-less alternative with _compute_movement_toward_target(unit, …, 3.0, …) toward cover, the objective area's edge or a sight line, counting vertical distance. Take it when it gains cover, OC or line of sight without losing the Heavy targets; otherwise REMAIN_STATIONARY as today.
implementation_order.why: The AI already decides to keep [HEAVY] but then freezes. 24.16 allows a 3″ move (40k_11th_edition_core_rules.txt:3751-3765), often enough to reach cover or the objective footprint.

implementation_order.mechanism: Give _get_round_strategy_modifiers (AIDecisionMaker.gd:17421) a moves_last_in_battle flag from snapshot.meta.first_turn_player, the same source _enemy_next_turn_round uses (:9812). Last mover in round 5: survival about 0, threat, Overwatch and Hidden terms off, Advance freely, force reserve arrivals. First mover in round 5: keep survival and add weight to end-of-battle and end-of-opponent-turn rows (already released by FIX_EOG_TIMING, :22830), plus screening of the objectives those rows need.
implementation_order.why: Rounds 4 and 5 share one profile that raises survival to 1.4 (:2724) for both seats, yet the player who moves last is the one for whom survival is worth nothing.

implementation_order.mechanism: Replace _position_has_cover (AIDecisionMaker.gd:14858), which only asks whether any enemy-to-position line crosses any terrain polygon, with a probe-formation call to TerrainManager.unit_has_cover_11e(probe_unit, attacker_model) (TerrainManager.gd:1388) against the 2-3 strongest enemy shooters in range. Widen _find_cover_path (:14817) beyond ±15/30°. Add a cover_gain term next to the F001/F004 terms in _assign_units_to_objectives (:10290-10313), scaled by incoming ranged threat and zeroed against [IGNORES COVER].
implementation_order.why: Benefit of cover (-1 BS on every incoming ranged attack, F030) is the most frequent defensive gain in 11e, and the current check is not the 13.08 rule.

implementation_order.mechanism: In the hold paths of _select_movement_action, HOLD DECISION (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7187) and OBJ-GAP-1 'already on it' (:7346), sample short repositions inside the hosting terrain area that keep the unit's OC in range (_ai_model_in_objective_range :13145). Score them with the SUR-03 cover probe and _position_would_be_hidden (:28515). Emit BEGIN_NORMAL_MOVE when one beats standing still and the Heavy and indirect gates allow it.
implementation_order.why: Objective holders are the most-shot units (F028). Because the terrain area is the objective, better protection inside it costs no OC.

implementation_order.mechanism: New generator replacing the AI-TACTIC-4 'avoiding charge threat — staying to shoot' REMAIN_STATIONARY (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7357-7391). For ranged units, sample endpoints within M that keep at least one target in range (_get_enemies_in_weapon_range :13760) and maximise the margin beyond each enemy melee unit's reach from _calculate_enemy_threat_data (:28695). Correct that reach to M+12″, plus D6 where an advance-and-charge rule applies. Choose by margin × target value.
implementation_order.why: The AI already detects charge danger but can only freeze or walk in. Kiting reuses the existing threat data.

implementation_order.mechanism: Second branch in _decide_engaged_unit (AIDecisionMaker.gd:11958). If the engaged enemy is a high-value non-MONSTER/VEHICLE unit, friendly unengaged shooters' expected damage (from the shooting-phase estimators) is at least its remaining wounds, and our engaged unit is cheap and not needed for OC (oc_without_us is already computed there), return BEGIN_FALL_BACK via _compute_fall_back_destinations (:12185), landing clear of the gunline's lanes.
implementation_order.why: An engaged non-MONSTER/VEHICLE unit cannot be targeted by shooting (04.02 requires an unengaged target), so a cheap tarpit currently shields the enemy's best unit from the AI's guns. It lives in the same function as item 1.

implementation_order.mechanism: Make _find_firing_position_toward_objective (AIDecisionMaker.gd:13848) and _clamp_move_for_weapon_range (:13780) check visibility to the target's models with probe models through TerrainManager.model_visible_11e (TerrainManager.gd:1209). Score the firing_position term (:10250-10268) on visible targets rather than centroid range. OFF-N01's exposure count is the follow-up on the same probe.
implementation_order.why: In 11e an obscuring area blocks a sight line completely, so centroid range overstates what the unit can shoot. A sight-line-aware endpoint is the base layer for every shooting intent.

implementation_order.mechanism: Rework _overwatch_exposure_penalty (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28660). Test visibility with probe models (TerrainManager.model_visible_11e) instead of the 24″ band alone. Skip it when the opponent has no CP or no unengaged, non-battle-shocked, non-TITANIC shooter, and for Overwatch-immune units. Price only the single worst newly exposed target per phase, since Fire Overwatch can be used once per phase (15.01). Then enable OVERWATCH_EXPOSURE_PENALTY through a profile and re-run the paired A/B.
implementation_order.why: The term already exists but is switched off because its range-only approximation over-taxes movement. Making it faithful to the rule is what lets it pay off (F004).

implementation_order.mechanism: Read MissionManager._kills_this_turn_11e (MissionManager.gd:3270) and the opponent's last-turn kill count into _build_primary_awareness (AIDecisionMaker.gd:22800). While a destroy-1+, kill-more or per-unit row is unmet this turn, add a kill-probability term (remaining wounds vs expected damage) to _build_phase_plan charge_intent (:3773), to the firing-position choice, and to _calculate_target_value (:17642), replacing the flat ×1.15 kill_pressure multiplier (:17879).
implementation_order.why: Five Purge the Foe primaries (plus No Prisoners) pay 3-4 VP per turn for one sure kill, and the engine already tracks the counts.

implementation_order.mechanism: Add a Hidden-spot candidate generator for units with no scoring job (the pass-3 fallback in _assign_units_to_objectives, AIDecisionMaker.gd:11651) and for forward staging. Sample points in nearby light/dense terrain areas reachable this move; keep those where _position_would_be_hidden (:28515) holds; rank by _hidden_immunity_fraction (:28548, fixed to use the per-observer detection_range_inches_for) and by forward progress. Pair it with HIDDEN_FORFEIT_PENALTY so the units do not shoot the benefit away, then re-run the mirror A/B.
implementation_order.why: F001 is implemented only as a bias on which objective to walk to, which is why it measured flat. The engine's errata-correct Hidden predicate (TerrainManager.gd:1001-1052) is ready to use.

user_examples.example: 'Move into cover'. Main entry: SUR-03 (13.08 benefit of cover, -1 BS to the attacker). Vehicles and monsters: SUR-08 (hull-down). The stronger infantry form: SUR-01 (Hidden). Break line of sight completely: SUR-02. On an objective: OBJ-06 (absorbs MIS-15). Denial form: DEN-06 (absorbs OBJ-38). While keeping [HEAVY]: OFF-06. While shooting: OFF-N01. On arrival or disembark: TRN-10. Out of turn: ADJ-05 (reactive move) and ADJ-22 (pre-battle).

'Move toward an enemy to shoot it'. Main entry: OFF-01. Supporting entries: sight line OFF-03; Hidden or Lone Operative targets OFF-04; half range and other bonus bands OFF-10; Advance with [ASSAULT] OFF-13; strip the target's cover OFF-17; safest firing spot OFF-N01. Target value from mission cards: OFF-14 (absorbs MIS-08). Shoot an objective holder off: OBJ-09. Shoot away screens: DEN-07. Kill-count cards: MIS-N01. Characters: OFF-15. From reserves or a transport: TRN-07, TRN-16.

'Move toward an enemy to charge it'. Main entry: OFF-02. Staging: out of Overwatch sight OFF-05 (merged into SUR-04); several targets in reach OFF-11; clean lane OFF-12; multi-unit charge OFF-16; strike first OFF-22; advance-and-charge OFF-23; Crushing Impact OFF-32; Waaagh! turn COO-06. Avoid Heroic Intervention: DEN-14 (absorbs OFF-24). Purpose-specific: card-paid targets OFF-14 (absorbs MIS-09); charge a holder off its objective OBJ-10; lock a shooter or actor DEN-03; tarpit a melee threat DEN-N01. From reserves or a transport: TRN-06, TRN-03. Pre-battle: ADJ-23.

other_gaps: Off an objective, an engaged unit always falls back when it can (AIDecisionMaker.gd:12123). _assess_engaged_unit_survival computes a 'hold' recommendation (:12410-12416) that nothing reads. So the AI leaves fights it is winning and releases its own lock charges (affects COO-18, DEN-03 and DEN-N01).

No 'what if I stood here' query for visibility or cover. _can_shooter_see_target (AIDecisionMaker.gd:190) takes unit IDs; F004 is a 24″ range band (:28648-28656); _position_has_cover (:14858) is a polygon-crossing proxy. TerrainManager already accepts probe model dicts (model_visible_11e :1209, model_fully_visible_11e :1215, unit_has_cover_11e :1388, is_model_hidden :1001). One shared, memoised _probe_unit_at(unit, dests) would unlock SUR-02/03/04/08, OFF-03/04/17/N01, OBJ-06 and TRN-10.

Engine line of sight ignores models: EnhancedLineOfSight.gd:27 is terrain-only, and TerrainManager.gd:1221-1224 says so. Rule 06.01 ignores only the observing and observed units' own models, so other units should block. The 11e SMOKESCREEN entry declares covers_screened (StratagemManager.gd:5106), but only the SMOKE unit itself receives the cover flags (StratagemManager.gd:1918-1927). The COO-19/SUR-31 walls and COO-N02 have no in-engine payoff until this is modelled.

Threat model (_calculate_enemy_threat_data, AIDecisionMaker.gd:28695). Charge reach is M + 12″ + engagement range, but 11.04 only needs the target within the roll, so the +2″ over-estimates. It ignores advance-and-charge grants, FLY and terrain. Shooting reach is weapon range with no enemy move, so SUR-13 (out-ranging) and SUR-19 (distance bands) cannot be scored.

Candidate structure: movement candidates are (unit, objective) pairs plus screen, corridor and attack slots (_assign_units_to_objectives :9834; pass 3 :11438), and the per-unit overrides only bend the heading toward the objective. Intents whose destination is not an objective need a generic positional-candidate generator scored in the same currency: SUR-01/02/09 staging, COO-02 aura spots, OFF-19 spotter spots, COO-11/COO-12 pickets, DEN-18 zones and OFF-N01 firing angles.

The movement plan is rebuilt only when a friendly unit becomes movable or moves again (need_plan, AIDecisionMaker.gd:6948-6985). Enemy reactive moves (F014), Rapid Ingress arrivals and Overwatch casualties mid-phase never trigger a re-plan.

Stale text. AIDecisionMaker.gd:2589-2591 quotes the pre-errata 13.09 ('dense' only), but TerrainManager.is_model_hidden already applies the light/dense errata (TerrainManager.gd:1031-1052), so the engine side of the Hidden fix is done. AIDecisionMaker.gd:2648-2652 says Fire Overwatch fires per move, but at edition 11+ MovementPhase.gd:1746-1752 offers it only at the end of the opponent's Movement phase. The errata check has since corrected SUR-01, SUR-12, OFF-04 and OBJ-06: Hidden needs light or dense terrain (Gone to Ground still needs intervening dense terrain).

_hidden_immunity_fraction (AIDecisionMaker.gd:28548-28575) measures 15″ centroid-to-centroid using detection_range_base_inches, not the per-observer detection_range_inches_for (TerrainManager.gd:1069) its comment promises, so Gone to Ground (SUR-11) is never valued.

The AI never embarks mid-battle. EMBARK_UNIT exists in the engine (MovementPhase.gd:465/555, _validate_embark_unit :9120), but the AI's embark scoring runs only at formations (AIDecisionMaker.gd:4637-4690), so TRN-05, TRN-23 and TRN-24 cannot happen. Separately, the engine's embark check uses disembarked_this_phase (MovementPhase.gd:9143), while 18.02 bars any unit set up on the battlefield this turn, including reserve arrivals.

The AI has no reference at all to [INDIRECT FIRE] (zero matches in AIDecisionMaker.gd, AIPlayer.gd and AIAbilityAnalyzer.gd) and selects no shooting type (RulesEngine.gd:6560), so OFF-07, OFF-19 and SUR-23 have no hook.

Screening (pass 3, AIDecisionMaker.gd:11438-11550) runs whenever the enemy has reserves (_get_enemy_reserves :14884), with no gate on when they can actually arrive: no ingress in round 1 (20.03), no Rapid Ingress in round 1 (15.07), and the enemy's CP. Round-1 screens for the first player are wasted units. The same CP gate is missing from the Overwatch term.

Advance planning uses M+2 in _select_movement_action (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7205, :7244) and in AIPlayer (AIPlayer.gd:1678), but scoring uses ADVANCE_EXPECTED_EXTRA_INCHES = 3.5 (:2256). The post-roll recompute keeps the pre-roll heading (AIPlayer.gd:1697-1716).
The Behind Enemy Lines push uses hard-coded Search-and-Destroy deployment-zone centres (AIDecisionMaker.gd:10393-10397, :23236) instead of the mission's deployment map.

Mission actions are chosen only in the Shooting phase (_evaluate_secondary_actions AIDecisionMaker.gd:23784; PERFORM_SECONDARY_ACTION :16474); the Movement phase never stages a carrier. In the engine only Sabotage, Vanguard Operation and Extract Intelligence are real per-unit actions (MissionManager.gd:1966-2010); Triangulate, Booby Trap and Sensor Sweep auto-resolve (MissionManager.gd:1872-1950). So MIS-01..06 staging matters only for the first three. There is no per-unit kill attribution for Consecrate (MissionManager.gd:1976-1978), which limits MIS-26.

Loaded transports have their shooting zeroed in movement scoring (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7398-7404), so no path drives a Firing Deck transport for its borrowed weapons (TRN-16). Post-shooting reactive moves such as SWIFT AS THE EAGLE and GO GET 'EM! are always declined because the engine has no executor for the move yet (AIDecisionMaker.gd:16397-16416), which blocks part of ADJ-24 and OBJ-43.

Queries the AI cannot ask yet: which enemy units could Fire Overwatch on point P (line of sight, 24″, unengaged, not battle-shocked, not TITANIC, opponent has CP); the chance this transport or vehicle dies before our next turn; a registry of enemy 'ends a move within X″' triggers and debuff radii (DEN-10); enemy Heroic Intervention eligibility (unengaged, within 12″, CP); kills this turn and the opponent's last-turn kills (tracked at MissionManager.gd:3270, never read by the AI); escape lanes from P (SUR-N02).

Deliberately kept separate (precursor vs execution, or a different move type for the same purpose): TRN-27/ADJ-26, OBJ-43/ADJ-33, DEN-25/ADJ-03, ADJ-36/COO-45, TRN-26/ADJ-37, TRN-25/DEN-01, ADJ-07/DEN-01, OBJ-34/COO-18, MIS-19/OBJ-14, DEN-28/MIS-24.
